items.title: Grammar 1–4 · Meeting New Friends

text.traditional: （美心跟良介在學校）
text.simplified: （美心跟良介在学校）
text.pinyin: (Měixīn gēn Liángjiè zài xuéxiào)
text.english: (Meixin and Ryosuke are at school.)

text.traditional: 你怎麼了？為什麼不去吃午飯？
text.simplified: 你怎么了？为什么不去吃午饭？
text.pinyin: Nǐ zěnmele? Wèishénme bú qù chī wǔfàn?
text.english: What's wrong with you? Why don't you go for lunch?

text.traditional: 今天早上起來的時候，覺得背很疼，我想休息一下。
text.simplified: 今天早上起来的时候，觉得背很疼，我想休息一下。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshàng qǐlái de shíhòu, juéde bèi hěn téng, wǒ xiǎng xiūxí yíxià.
text.english: When I woke up this morning, I felt my back hurt very much. I think I need to take some rest.

text.traditional: 要是明天還是很疼，最好去看醫生或是去藥房買藥。
text.simplified: 要是明天还是很疼，最好去看医生或是去药房买药。
text.pinyin: Yàoshì míngtiān háishì hěn téng, zuìhǎo qù kàn yīshēng huòshì qù yàofáng mǎi yào.
text.english: If your back still hurts tomorrow, you'd better go to the doctor or buy some medicine in a pharmacy.

text.traditional: 謝謝妳。對了！我最近在網路上認識了一個女生，她不但很溫柔，也很客氣。我每天都給她打電話，我們聊得很愉快。
text.simplified: 谢谢你。对了！我最近在网路上认识了一个女生，她不但很温柔，也很客气。我每天都给她打电话，我们聊得很愉快。
text.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ. Duìle! Wǒ zuìjìn zài wǎnglù shàng rènshì le yíge nǚshēng, tā búdàn hěn wēnróu, yě hěn kèqì. Wǒ měi tiān dōu gěi tā dǎ diànhuà, wǒmen liáo de hěn yúkuài.
text.english: Thank you. By the way, I met a girl online lately. She's not only gentle but also polite. I call her every day and we chat happily.

text.traditional: 你們認識多久了？
text.simplified: 你们认识多久了？
text.pinyin: Nǐmen rènshì duōjiǔ le?
text.english: How long have you known each other?

text.traditional: 差不多一個月了。
text.simplified: 差不多一个月了。
text.pinyin: Chàbùduō yíge yuè le.
text.english: For around one month.

text.traditional: 見過面了嗎？
text.simplified: 见过面了吗？
text.pinyin: Jiàn guò miàn le ma?
text.english: Have you ever met?

text.traditional: 還沒，她說她不好意思跟我見面，所以我不知道怎麼辦。
text.simplified: 还没，她说她不好意思跟我见面，所以我不知道怎么办。
text.pinyin: Háiméi, tā shuō tā bùhǎoyìsi gēn wǒ jiànmiàn, suǒyǐ wǒ bù zhīdào zěnmebàn.
text.english: Not yet. She said she feels embarrassed to meet me, so I have no idea what to do.

text.traditional: 也許她覺得一個人跟你見面不安全。這個禮拜六學校有舞會，你要不要請她跟她朋友一起來參加？
text.simplified: 也许她觉得一个人跟你见面不安全。这个礼拜六学校有舞会，你要不要请她跟她朋友一起来参加？
text.pinyin: Yěxǔ tā juéde yígerén gēn nǐ jiànmiàn bù ānquán. Zhège lǐbàiliù xuéxiào yǒu wǔhuì, nǐ yào búyào qǐng tā gēn tā péngyǒu yìqǐ lái cānjiā?
text.english: Perhaps she doesn't feel safe to meet you alone. There's going to be a dance party in the school this Saturday. Will you invite her and her friends?

text.traditional: 這個辦法不錯，妳以前也有這樣的經驗嗎？
text.simplified: 这个办法不错，你以前也有这样的经验吗？
text.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ búcuò, nǐ yǐqián yě yǒu zhèyàng de jīngyàn ma?
text.english: This is not a bad idea. Did you have such an experience before?

text.traditional: 當然有啊！以前有一個男生要跟我約會，我也很害怕，不敢自己跟他見面。
text.simplified: 当然有啊！以前有一个男生要跟我约会，我也很害怕，不敢自己跟他见面。
text.pinyin: Dāngrán yǒu a! Yǐqián yǒu yíge nánshēng yào gēn wǒ yuēhuì, wǒ yě hěn hàipà, bù gǎn zìjǐ gēn tā jiànmiàn.
text.english: Of course I did! There was a boy who wanted to have a date with me. I was afraid and dared not meet him by myself.

text.traditional: 後來呢？
text.simplified: 后来呢？
text.pinyin: Hòulái ne?
text.english: And then?

text.traditional: 那個時候我剛好要跟同學去動物園玩，我就約他一起去。那天大家在動物園裡看看動物、開開玩笑，後來我就敢一個人跟他約會了。
text.simplified: 那个时候我刚好要跟同学去动物园玩，我就约他一起去。那天大家在动物园里看看动物、开开玩笑，后来我就敢一个人跟他约会了。
text.pinyin: Nàge shíhòu wǒ gānghǎo yào gēn tóngxué qù dòngwùyuán wán, wǒ jiù yuē tā yìqǐ qù. Nà tiān dàjiā zài dòngwùyuán lǐ kànkan dòngwù, kāi kāiwánxiào, hòulái wǒ jiù gǎn yígerén gēn tā yuēhuì le.
text.english: At that time I just wanted to go to the zoo with my classmates, so I asked him to go together with us. On that day, we saw the animals and made jokes at the zoo. From then on, I dared have a date with him alone.

text.traditional: 聽妳說完了以後，我想我知道應該怎麼做了。
text.simplified: 听你说完了以后，我想我知道应该怎么做了。
text.pinyin: Tīng nǐ shuō wán le yǐhòu, wǒ xiǎng wǒ zhīdào yīnggāi zěnme zuò le.
text.english: After listening to what you said, I think I know what to do.

text.traditional: 現在你的背好一點兒了嗎？
text.simplified: 现在你的背好一点儿了吗？
text.pinyin: Xiànzài nǐ de bèi hǎo yìdiǎnr le ma?
text.english: Is your back a bit better now?

text.traditional: （摸摸自己的背）好像不疼了。
text.simplified: （摸摸自己的背）好像不疼了。
text.pinyin: (Mō mō zìjǐ de bèi) hǎoxiàng bù téng le.
text.english: (Touches his own back.) It seems okay now.

text.traditional: （兩人都笑了）
text.simplified: （两人都笑了）
text.pinyin: (Liǎng rén dōu xiào le)
text.english: (Both of them laugh.)

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Verb + 一下: a quick action
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask someone to do something briefly, or make an action feel small and easy.
grammarPages.explanation: This grammar indicates the action of the verb lasts for a short time or the amount of action is quite small.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Verb + 一下 (+ Object)

text.traditional: 他去一下洗手間，馬上回來。
text.simplified: 他去一下洗手间，马上回来。
text.pinyin: Tā qù yíxià xǐshǒujiān, mǎshàng huílái.
text.english: He stepped into the restroom for a moment and will be right back.

text.traditional: 你能介紹一下你自己嗎？
text.simplified: 你能介绍一下你自己吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ néng jièshào yíxià nǐ zìjǐ ma?
text.english: Could you introduce yourself a little?

text.traditional: 我去旁邊的商店買麵包，你可以等一下嗎？
text.simplified: 我去旁边的商店买面包，你可以等一下吗？
text.pinyin: Wǒ qù pángbiān de shāngdiàn mǎi miànbāo, nǐ kěyǐ děng yíxià ma?
text.english: I am going to the shop next door for bread; could you wait a moment?

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This grammar indicates the action of the verb lasts for a short time or the amount of action is quite small.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This grammar indicates the action of the verb lasts for a short time or the amount of action is quite small.

segments.traditional: 這裡有多少錢，你可以幫我
segments.simplified: 这里有多少钱，你可以帮我

repairs.note: 一點兒 is a small amount of something (喝一點兒水). A quick action takes 一下 after the verb.
有一點兒 goes before a feeling or quality (有一點兒累). A quick action takes 一下 after the verb.

items.fallbackRepair: 一下 comes right after the verb: 算一下.

result.traditional: 這裡有多少錢，你可以幫我算一下嗎？
result.simplified: 这里有多少钱，你可以帮我算一下吗？
result.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu duōshǎo qián, nǐ kěyǐ bāng wǒ suàn yíxià ma?
result.english: How much money is here? Could you count it for me?

repairs.note: B answers 馬上來: B is coming to where A is, so A asks with 來.
一點兒 is a small amount of something. A short visit takes 一下 after the verb.

items.fallbackRepair: 一下 comes right after the verb, before the place: 來一下我的辦公室.

result.traditional: 你可以來一下我的辦公室嗎？
result.simplified: 你可以来一下我的办公室吗？
result.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ lái yíxià wǒ de bàngōngshì ma?
result.english: Could you come to my office for a moment?

repairs.note: 覺得 gives an opinion and needs something after it (我覺得很好). Thinking it over for a moment is 想一下.
知道 is knowing, not a short action, so it cannot take 一下. She needs a moment to think: 想一下.

items.fallbackRepair: Who, then the action, then 一下: 我想一下.

result.traditional: 我想一下。
result.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yíxià.
result.english: Let me think for a moment.

summary: Put 一下 after a verb to say the action is short or small.
It is often used for requests, asking for help politely, or making an action sound relaxed.
An object can come after 一下: 看一下菜單.
一下 is about a short, light action, while 一次 counts how many times.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Give warm, practical advice about what someone should do.
grammarPages.explanation: This expression, often followed by a verb phrase, is used to give advice about what someone should do.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 最好 + Verb Phrase

text.traditional: 你最好去看醫生，聽聽醫生怎麼說。
text.simplified: 你最好去看医生，听听医生怎么说。
text.pinyin: Nǐ zuìhǎo qù kàn yīshēng, tīng tīng yīshēng zěnme shuō.
text.english: You had better see a doctor and hear what they say.

text.traditional: 我們最好每天下了課就去圖書館念書。
text.simplified: 我们最好每天下了课就去图书馆念书。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen zuìhǎo měi tiān xià le kè jiù qù túshūguǎn niànshū.
text.english: We had better go to the library to study every day after class.

text.traditional: 你最好不要一個人去。
text.simplified: 你最好不要一个人去。
text.pinyin: Nǐ zuìhǎo búyào yígerén qù.
text.english: You had better not go alone.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This expression, often followed by a verb phrase, is used to give advice about what someone should do.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This expression, often followed by a verb phrase, is used to give advice about what someone should do.

segments.traditional: 我覺得非常不舒服，好像發燒了。
segments.simplified: 我觉得非常不舒服，好像发烧了。

repairs.note: 很好 describes something (這個很好). Advice puts 最好 before the action.
A feels sick with a fever, so the advice is to rest, not to exercise.

items.fallbackRepair: 最好 comes before what the person should do: 最好在家休息.

result.traditional: 那你最好在家休息。
result.pinyin: Nà nǐ zuìhǎo zài jiā xiūxí.
result.english: Then you had better rest at home.

segments.traditional: 我今天上課遲到了，老師有一點兒不高興。
segments.simplified: 我今天上课迟到了，老师有一点儿不高兴。

repairs.note: A was late today, so tomorrow A should come earlier, not later.
比較 means "rather" and only describes (比較忙). Advice puts 最好 before the action.

items.fallbackRepair: 最好 first, then how to do it: 最好早一點兒來.

result.traditional: 你明天最好早一點兒來。
result.simplified: 你明天最好早一点儿来。
result.pinyin: Nǐ míngtiān zuìhǎo zǎo yìdiǎnr lái.
result.english: You had better come a little earlier tomorrow.

segments.traditional: 今年我想到台北101去跨年。

repairs.note: 不可以 is a rule (這裡不可以停車), not advice. After 最好, "don't" is 不要.
好像 means "it seems". To give advice use 最好.

items.fallbackRepair: Advice against something is 最好 + 不要 + the action.

result.traditional: 那天人很多，你最好不要開車去。
result.simplified: 那天人很多，你最好不要开车去。
result.pinyin: Nà tiān rén hěn duō, nǐ zuìhǎo búyào kāichē qù.
result.english: It will be very crowded that day. You had better not drive there.

summary: Put 最好 before a verb to give advice about what someone should do, like 最好休息.
For advice not to do something, use 最好不要.
Here 最好 gives advice and doesn't mean the best one. A noun can't follow it.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Add a second true point with 也 instead of stopping after the first.
grammarPages.explanation: The “不但……，也……” pattern connects two phrases or clauses and indicates the two situations exist at the same time. If “不但” and “也” have the same topic, “不但” should come after the topic, connect with a phrase, and “也” connects with another phrase. If related to different aspects, “也” should come after the second aspect.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 不但 + Clause 1 + 也 + Clause 2

text.traditional: 我不但想吃小籠包，也想吃牛肉麵。
text.simplified: 我不但想吃小笼包，也想吃牛肉面。
text.pinyin: Wǒ búdàn xiǎng chī xiǎolóngbāo, yě xiǎng chī niúròu miàn.
text.english: I not only want xiaolongbao, but also want beef noodles.

text.traditional: 學中文不但很有意思，也比較容易找工作。
text.simplified: 学中文不但很有意思，也比较容易找工作。
text.pinyin: Xué Zhōngwén búdàn hěn yǒuyìsi, yě bǐjiào róngyì zhǎo gōngzuò.
text.english: Learning Chinese is not only interesting; it also makes finding a job easier.

text.traditional: 因為台灣不但風景美，交通也很方便。
text.simplified: 因为台湾不但风景美，交通也很方便。
text.pinyin: Yīnwèi Táiwān búdàn fēngjǐng měi, jiāotōng yě hěn fāngbiàn.
text.english: Because Taiwan not only has beautiful scenery, but its transport is also convenient.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The “不但……，也……” pattern connects two phrases or clauses and indicates the two situations exist at the same time. If “不但” and “也” have the same topic, “不但” should come after the topic, connect with a phrase, and “也” connects with another phrase. If related to different aspects, “也” should come after the second aspect.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The “不但……，也……” pattern connects two phrases or clauses and indicates the two situations exist at the same time. If “不但” and “也” have the same topic, “不但” should come after the topic, connect with a phrase, and “也” connects with another phrase. If related to different aspects, “也” should come after the second aspect.

repairs.note: 和 joins things (書和筆), not two qualities of one thing. The second one takes 也.
Good-looking and not expensive are both good points, so nothing turns: 不但…，也….

items.fallbackRepair: 不但 before the first quality, 也 before the second: 不但好看，也不貴.

result.traditional: 我買的這件衣服不但好看，也不貴。
result.simplified: 我买的这件衣服不但好看，也不贵。
result.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi de zhè jiàn yīfu búdàn hǎokàn, yě bú guì.
result.english: This piece of clothing I bought is not only good-looking but also inexpensive.

alternatives.traditional: 我買的這件衣服不但不貴，也好看。
alternatives.simplified: 我买的这件衣服不但不贵，也好看。
alternatives.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi de zhè jiàn yīfu búdàn bú guì, yě hǎokàn.
alternatives.english: This piece of clothing I bought is not only inexpensive but also good-looking.

repairs.note: 都 sums up several things said before it (英文、法文都很好). Here the second language adds on with 也.
Here 還是 would mean "or" or "still". After 不但, the second good point takes 也: 法文也很好.

items.fallbackRepair: Two different things are good, so 也 comes after the second one: 法文也很好.

result.traditional: 我的印尼朋友不但英文很好，法文也很好。
result.pinyin: Wǒ de Yìnní péngyǒu búdàn Yīngwén hěn hǎo, Fǎwén yě hěn hǎo.
result.english: My Indonesian friend is not only good at English but also good at French.

alternatives.traditional: 我的印尼朋友不但法文很好，英文也很好。
alternatives.pinyin: Wǒ de Yìnní péngyǒu búdàn Fǎwén hěn hǎo, Yīngwén yě hěn hǎo.
alternatives.english: My Indonesian friend is not only good at French but also good at English.

repairs.note: 和 joins things (書和筆), not two actions. The second action takes 也.
Classes and work both make B busy. Nothing turns, so it is 不但…，也….

items.fallbackRepair: One person does both, so 不但 comes after 我, and 也 starts the second action.

result.traditional: 因為我不但要上課，也要工作，所以比較忙。
result.simplified: 因为我不但要上课，也要工作，所以比较忙。
result.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ búdàn yào shàngkè, yě yào gōngzuò, suǒyǐ bǐjiào máng.
result.english: Because I not only have classes but also have to work, so I am rather busy.

summary: 不但……也…… says two things are both true.
If both parts share one subject, put 不但 after the subject, not before it.
Put 也 right before the second point.
If the parts describe different sides of one topic, put 也 before the second side: 風景美，交通也很方便.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say an action is completely finished, and ask whether it is done yet.
grammarPages.explanation: The expression indicates that an action is finished. The “完”, serving as a verb complement, means “done” or “finished”.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Verb + 完 (+ 了)

text.traditional: 今天的作業不多，我很快就寫完了。
text.simplified: 今天的作业不多，我很快就写完了。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān de zuòyè bù duō, wǒ hěn kuài jiù xiě wán le.
text.english: There is not much homework today; I finished writing it quickly.

text.traditional: 聽說上個星期就賣完了。
text.simplified: 听说上个星期就卖完了。
text.pinyin: Tīngshuō shàng ge xīngqí jiù mài wán le.
text.english: I heard they sold out last week.

text.traditional: 這個禮拜我很忙，還沒看完。
text.simplified: 这个礼拜我很忙，还没看完。
text.pinyin: Zhège lǐbài wǒ hěn máng, háiméi kàn wán.
text.english: I have been busy this week, so I have not finished reading it yet.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The expression indicates that an action is finished. The “完”, serving as a verb complement, means “done” or “finished”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The expression indicates that an action is finished. The “完”, serving as a verb complement, means “done” or “finished”.

segments.traditional: 這家店的麵包很好吃，每天下午三點以前就
segments.simplified: 这家店的面包很好吃，每天下午三点以前就

repairs.note: This sentence is about the shop and its bread: the shop sells it (賣).
V到 means managing to get something (買到了). "None left" is V完.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb first, then 完: 賣完了.

result.traditional: 這家店的麵包很好吃，每天下午三點以前就賣完了。
result.simplified: 这家店的面包很好吃，每天下午三点以前就卖完了。
result.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de miànbāo hěn hǎochī, měitiān xiàwǔ sān diǎn yǐqián jiù màiwán le.
result.english: This shop's bread is delicious; it is sold out before three every afternoon.

repairs.note: It is morning (早上) and he then goes to work, so the meal is breakfast.
吃到 means managing to get something to eat. Finishing the meal is 吃完.

items.fallbackRepair: 完 comes right after the verb, before the thing: 吃完早飯.

result.traditional: 王先生早上吃完早飯，就去上班了。
result.simplified: 王先生早上吃完早饭，就去上班了。
result.pinyin: Wáng xiānshēng zǎoshàng chīwán zǎofàn, jiù qù shàngbān le.
result.english: Mr. Wang finished breakfast this morning and then went to work.

alternatives.traditional: 王先生早上早飯吃完，就去上班了。
alternatives.simplified: 王先生早上早饭吃完，就去上班了。
alternatives.pinyin: Wáng xiānshēng zǎoshàng zǎofàn chīwán, jiù qù shàngbān le.
alternatives.english: Mr. Wang finished breakfast this morning and then went to work.

segments.traditional: 我現在要去超級市場買東西，要買牛奶嗎？
segments.simplified: 我现在要去超级市场买东西，要买牛奶吗？

repairs.note: If the milk were finished, they would buy more now. 明天再買 means some is left: 還沒喝完.
Something not finished yet is 還沒 + V完. 不 does not go with a result that has not happened.
Milk is something you drink: 喝.

items.fallbackRepair: Not finished yet: 還沒, then the verb, then 完.

result.traditional: 昨天買的牛奶還沒喝完，明天再買吧！
result.simplified: 昨天买的牛奶还没喝完，明天再买吧！
result.pinyin: Zuótiān mǎi de niúnǎi háiméi hēwán, míngtiān zài mǎi ba!
result.english: We haven't finished the milk we bought yesterday. Let's buy more tomorrow!

summary: Put 完 right after a verb to show the action is finished.
Say V完了 for done and 還沒V完 for not finished yet.
完 says the action is all done. 了 only shows something is complete or has changed.
Put 了 at the end, after 完: 吃完飯了, not 吃了完飯.

items.title: Grammar 5–9 · The First Time They Met

text.traditional: 山本良介本來是一個害羞的日本學生，來台灣以後，他住在學校的宿舍，認識了很多朋友，常常跟他們去吃飯、打球。放假的時候，朋友帶他去參觀博物館、看表演，所以他覺得在台灣的生活很快樂，也好像不那麼害羞了。
text.simplified: 山本良介本来是一个害羞的日本学生，来台湾以后，他住在学校的宿舍，认识了很多朋友，常常跟他们去吃饭、打球。放假的时候，朋友带他去参观博物馆、看表演，所以他觉得在台湾的生活很快乐，也好像不那么害羞了。
text.pinyin: Shānběn Liángjiè běnlái shì yíge hàixiū de Rìběn xuéshēng, lái Táiwān yǐhòu, tā zhù zài xuéxiào de sùshè, rènshì le hěn duō péngyǒu, chángcháng gēn tāmen qù chīfàn, dǎqiú. Fàngjià de shíhòu, péngyǒu dài tā qù cānguān bówùguǎn, kàn biǎoyǎn, suǒyǐ tā juéde zài Táiwān de shēnghuó hěn kuàilè, yě hǎoxiàng bú nàme hàixiū le.
text.english: Yamamoto Ryosuke was originally a shy Japanese student. After coming to Taiwan, he lives in the school dorm and met many friends. Ryosuke often eats out and plays balls with them. On holidays, his friends take him to visit the museum and watch the show, so he feels very happy living in Taiwan and he doesn't seem to be as shy as before.

text.traditional: 有一天，他在網路上認識了一個女生，她是台灣的大學生。因為她覺得跟不熟的男生約會很危險，所以一直不敢跟良介見面。後來良介寄給她一張卡片，請她跟她的朋友來學校參加舞會。不久，他們就在學校見面了。他們見面的時候，良介的心跳得很快。
text.simplified: 有一天，他在网路上认识了一个女生，她是台湾的大学生。因为她觉得跟不熟的男生约会很危险，所以一直不敢跟良介见面。后来良介寄给她一张卡片，请她跟她的朋友来学校参加舞会。不久，他们就在学校见面了。他们见面的时候，良介的心跳得很快。
text.pinyin: Yǒu yì tiān, tā zài wǎnglù shàng rènshì le yíge nǚshēng, tā shì Táiwān de dàxuéshēng. Yīnwèi tā juéde gēn bù shóu de nánshēng yuēhuì hěn wéixiǎn, suǒyǐ yìzhí bù gǎn gēn Liángjiè jiànmiàn. Hòulái Liángjiè jì gěi tā yì zhāng kǎpiàn, qǐng tā gēn tā de péngyǒu lái xuéxiào cānjiā wǔhuì. Bùjiǔ, tāmen jiù zài xuéxiào jiànmiàn le. Tāmen jiànmiàn de shíhòu, Liángjiè de xīntiào de hěn kuài.
text.english: One day, he met a girl on the Internet. She is a Taiwanese university student. She thought dating a guy she was not familiar with in person was dangerous, so she had never dared to date Ryosuke. Later on, Ryosuke sent her a card and invited her and her friends to the school to attend a dance party. Soon after, they met at the school. When they met each other, Ryosuke's heart beat so fast.

text.traditional: 那天，他們一邊跳舞，一邊聊天，兩個人都很開心。良介覺得那個女生不但很漂亮，個性也很好，很想趕快再跟她約會。舞會結束以後，他們在學校裡散步，良介不好意思拉她的手，只跟她說，能認識她真的很幸運，希望以後有機會再跟她見面。
text.simplified: 那天，他们一边跳舞，一边聊天，两个人都很开心。良介觉得那个女生不但很漂亮，个性也很好，很想赶快再跟她约会。舞会结束以后，他们在学校里散步，良介不好意思拉她的手，只跟她说，能认识她真的很幸运，希望以后有机会再跟她见面。
text.pinyin: Nà tiān, tāmen yìbiān tiàowǔ, yìbiān liáotiān, liǎng ge rén dōu hěn kāixīn. Liángjiè juéde nàge nǚshēng búdàn hěn piàoliàng, gèxìng yě hěn hǎo, hěn xiǎng gǎnkuài zài gēn tā yuēhuì. Wǔhuì jiéshù yǐhòu, tāmen zài xuéxiào lǐ sànbù, Liángjiè bùhǎoyìsi lā tā de shǒu, zhǐ gēn tā shuō, néng rènshì tā zhēnde hěn xìngyùn, xīwàng yǐhòu yǒu jīhuì zài gēn tā jiànmiàn.
text.english: On that day, they chatted as they danced. Both of them were having a good time. Ryosuke thought the girl was not only beautiful but also with a great personality, so he wanted to have a date with her soon. After the dance party had ended, they took a walk in the school. Ryosuke was embarrassed and dared not hold her hand, but simply said to her that he was really lucky to meet her, and looking forward to seeing her again.

text.traditional: 那個女生覺得雖然良介是外國人，中文也說得不太好，可是他們的興趣一樣，都喜歡看書、運動，而且跟他在一起很安全、很有意思。現在他們不但常常上網聊天，也會一起去打籃球、騎腳踏車呢！
text.simplified: 那个女生觉得虽然良介是外国人，中文也说得不太好，可是他们的兴趣一样，都喜欢看书、运动，而且跟他在一起很安全、很有意思。现在他们不但常常上网聊天，也会一起去打篮球、骑脚踏车呢！
text.pinyin: Nàge nǚshēng juéde suīrán Liángjiè shì wàiguórén, Zhōngwén yě shuō de bú tài hǎo, kěshì tāmen de xìngqù yíyàng, dōu xǐhuān kàn shū, yùndòng, érqiě gēn tā zài yìqǐ hěn ānquán, hěn yǒuyìsi. Xiànzài tāmen búdàn chángcháng shàngwǎng liáotiān, yě huì yìqǐ qù dǎ lánqiú, qí jiǎotàchē ne!
text.english: The girl thinks that although Ryosuke is a foreigner and doesn't speak good Chinese, their interests are the same. They both like to read and exercise. Moreover, she feels secure and fun being with him. Now, they not only chat online often, but also play basketball and ride bicycles together!

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say where someone or something sits, stands, lives, or is placed.
grammarPages.explanation: The structure of the pattern is “V在+Location”. The verbs often placed before “在” include “住 (live)”, “坐 (sit)” and “站 (stand)”.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Verb + 在 + Location

text.traditional: 爸爸忘了他的手機放在哪裡了。
text.simplified: 爸爸忘了他的手机放在哪里了。
text.pinyin: Bàba wàngle tā de shǒujī fàng zài nǎlǐ le.
text.english: Dad forgot where he put his phone.

text.traditional: 你不要站在那麼高的地方，很危險！
text.simplified: 你不要站在那么高的地方，很危险！
text.pinyin: Nǐ búyào zhàn zài nàme gāo de dìfāng, hěn wéixiǎn!
text.english: Don't stand in such a high place—it is dangerous!

text.traditional: 我住在捷運站附近，走路五分鐘就到了。
text.simplified: 我住在捷运站附近，走路五分钟就到了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài jiéyùn zhàn fùjìn, zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
text.english: I live near the MRT station; it is a five-minute walk.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The structure of the pattern is “V在+Location”. The verbs often placed before “在” include “住 (live)”, “坐 (sit)” and “站 (stand)”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The structure of the pattern is “V在+Location”. The verbs often placed before “在” include “住 (live)”, “坐 (sit)” and “站 (stand)”.

practice.title: Look at the pictures and complete the sentences.

scene.alt: A little girl sitting on a wooden chair.

repairs.note: Look at the picture: the child is sitting, not standing.
After 在 comes a place. A thing becomes a place with 上: 椅子上.

items.fallbackRepair: With 坐, the place comes after the verb: 坐在椅子上.

result.traditional: 孩子坐在椅子上。
result.pinyin: Háizi zuò zài yǐzi shàng.
result.english: The child is sitting on the chair.

scene.alt: Two students standing in front of a convenience store.

repairs.note: Look at the picture: the two students are standing.
Look at the picture: they are outside, in front of the shop.

items.fallbackRepair: With 站, the place comes after the verb: 站在商店前面.

result.traditional: 有兩個學生站在商店前面。
result.simplified: 有两个学生站在商店前面。
result.pinyin: Yǒu liǎng ge xuéshēng zhàn zài shāngdiàn qiánmiàn.
result.english: Two students are standing in front of the shop.

scene.alt: A man writing a phone number on a sheet of paper.

repairs.note: A phone number is written down, not put somewhere: 寫在.
Look at the picture: he is writing on a sheet of paper, not in a book.

items.fallbackRepair: Where the number ends up comes after the verb: 寫在紙上.

result.traditional: 他的電話號碼寫在紙上。
result.simplified: 他的电话号码写在纸上。
result.pinyin: Tā de diànhuà hàomǎ xiě zài zhǐ shàng.
result.english: His phone number is written on the paper.

summary: Put 在 after the verb and before the place to say where a person or thing ends up.
Common verbs here are 住, 坐 and 站. 放 is used too.
Pick a verb that fits: 住在 is for living, while things use 放在 or 寫在.
In this pattern 在 comes after the verb. You can't say 在坐.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Mark who receives a thing or a message after verbs like 送、賣、寄、拿.
grammarPages.explanation: “給” functions as a preposition that comes after a verb, shows the direction, and marks the recipient of an action.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Verb + 給 + Receiver

text.traditional: 那些書，我送給朋友了。
text.simplified: 那些书，我送给朋友了。
text.pinyin: Nàxiē shū, wǒ sòng gěi péngyǒu le.
text.english: I gave those books to a friend.

text.traditional: 王先生的舊車賣給張小姐了。
text.simplified: 王先生的旧车卖给张小姐了。
text.pinyin: Wáng xiānshēng de jiù chē mài gěi Zhāng xiǎojiě le.
text.english: Mr. Wang sold his old car to Miss Zhang.

text.traditional: 我拿著電話，可是忘了要打給誰了。
text.simplified: 我拿着电话，可是忘了要打给谁了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ ná zhe diànhuà, kěshì wàngle yào dǎ gěi shéi le.
text.english: I was holding the phone but forgot whom I meant to call.

text.traditional: 桌上的水果，你拿給誰吃了？
text.simplified: 桌上的水果，你拿给谁吃了？
text.pinyin: Zhuō shàng de shuǐguǒ, nǐ ná gěi shéi chī le?
text.english: Who did you give the fruit on the table to?

text.traditional: 我沒聽過十二生肖的故事，你可以說給我聽嗎？
text.simplified: 我没听过十二生肖的故事，你可以说给我听吗？
text.pinyin: Wǒ méi tīng guò shí'èr shēngxiào de gùshì, nǐ kěyǐ shuō gěi wǒ tīng ma?
text.english: I have never heard the story of the twelve zodiac animals. Could you tell it to me?

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “給” functions as a preposition that comes after a verb, shows the direction, and marks the recipient of an action.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “給” functions as a preposition that comes after a verb, shows the direction, and marks the recipient of an action.

repairs.note: A gift costs nothing. There is a price (一件五十塊), so the clothes were sold: 賣給.
寄給 is mailing something to someone. The price tells you the clothes were sold: 賣給.
You write a letter or a card to someone (寫給), not clothes.

items.fallbackRepair: The price tells you what happened to the clothes: 賣給.

result.traditional: 那些舊衣服，我賣給同學了，一件五十塊。
result.simplified: 那些旧衣服，我卖给同学了，一件五十块。
result.pinyin: Nàxiē jiù yīfu, wǒ mài gěi tóngxué le, yí jiàn wǔshí kuài.
result.english: I sold those old clothes to a classmate, fifty dollars apiece.

segments.traditional: 這些漂亮的鉛筆，你打算
segments.simplified: 这些漂亮的铅笔，你打算

repairs.note: The one who receives a gift is a person, so ask with 誰.
在 marks a place (放在桌上). The person who receives takes 給.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 給, then the person: 送給誰.

result.traditional: 這些漂亮的鉛筆，你打算送給誰？
result.simplified: 这些漂亮的铅笔，你打算送给谁？
result.pinyin: Zhèxiē piàoliàng de qiānbǐ, nǐ dǎsuàn sòng gěi shéi?
result.english: Who do you plan to give these pretty pencils to?

repairs.note: After 是, the sentence closes with 的 (是…的), not 了.
寫在 says where something is written (寫在紙上). The person the card is for takes 給: 寫給我.

items.fallbackRepair: 寫給, then the person, and 的 closes 是…的: 寫給我的.

result.traditional: 這張卡片是我朋友寫給我的。
result.simplified: 这张卡片是我朋友写给我的。
result.pinyin: Zhè zhāng kǎpiàn shì wǒ péngyǒu xiě gěi wǒ de.
result.english: This card was written to me by my friend.

summary: Put 給 after a verb and before the receiver to show who gets the thing.
Common ones are 送給, 賣給, 拿給 and 打給.
給 must come right after a verb, and the receiver comes after 給: 送給朋友.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe two actions happening at the same time, with one or two subjects.
grammarPages.explanation: The “（一）邊……（，）（一）邊……” pattern implies that the two actions coming after each “一邊” happen at the same time or at the same place. This pattern is mostly used in modifying concrete action verbs and it can be used in sentences with only one subject or in complex sentences with two subjects, eg. “他一邊唱，我一邊跳。”. If “一” is omitted, there should be only one subject in the sentence, eg. “他邊唱邊跳。”.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 一邊 + Action 1 + 一邊 + Action 2

text.traditional: 有人一邊走路一邊玩手機，真危險。
text.simplified: 有人一边走路一边玩手机，真危险。
text.pinyin: Yǒu rén yì biān zǒulù yì biān wán shǒujī, zhēn wéixiǎn.
text.english: Some people walk and use their phones at the same time; that is really dangerous.

text.traditional: 很多學生喜歡一邊聽音樂，一邊念書。
text.simplified: 很多学生喜欢一边听音乐，一边念书。
text.pinyin: Hěn duō xuéshēng xǐhuān yì biān tīng yīnyuè, yì biān niànshū.
text.english: Many students like to listen to music while studying.

text.traditional: 上課的時候，老師一邊說，學生一邊寫。
text.simplified: 上课的时候，老师一边说，学生一边写。
text.pinyin: Shàngkè de shíhòu, lǎoshī yì biān shuō, xuéshēng yì biān xiě.
text.english: In class, the teacher talks while the students write.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The “（一）邊……（，）（一）邊……” pattern implies that the two actions coming after each “一邊” happen at the same time or at the same place. This pattern is mostly used in modifying concrete action verbs and it can be used in sentences with only one subject or in complex sentences with two subjects, eg. “他一邊唱，我一邊跳。”. If “一” is omitted, there should be only one subject in the sentence, eg. “他邊唱邊跳。”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The “（一）邊……（，）（一）邊……” pattern implies that the two actions coming after each “一邊” happen at the same time or at the same place. This pattern is mostly used in modifying concrete action verbs and it can be used in sentences with only one subject or in complex sentences with two subjects, eg. “他一邊唱，我一邊跳。”. If “一” is omitted, there should be only one subject in the sentence, eg. “他邊唱邊跳。”.

practice.title: Look at the pictures and complete the sentences.

scene.alt: A man driving a red car with music notes around him.

repairs.note: Look at the picture: he is in a car, driving, not walking.
Two actions at the same time take 一邊 before each one, not 也.

items.fallbackRepair: 一邊 goes before each of the two actions.

result.traditional: 很多人常常一邊開車，一邊聽音樂。
result.simplified: 很多人常常一边开车，一边听音乐。
result.pinyin: Hěn duō rén chángcháng yìbiān kāichē, yìbiān tīng yīnyuè.
result.english: Many people often listen to music while driving.

alternatives.traditional: 很多人常常一邊聽音樂，一邊開車。
alternatives.simplified: 很多人常常一边听音乐，一边开车。
alternatives.pinyin: Hěn duō rén chángcháng yìbiān tīng yīnyuè, yìbiān kāichē.
alternatives.english: Many people often drive while listening to music.

scene.alt: A boy eating from a bowl in front of the television.

repairs.note: Look at the picture: the child is eating and watching television, not sleeping.
和 joins things (書和筆), not two actions. Put 邊 before each action.

items.fallbackRepair: 邊 goes before each of the two actions: 邊吃飯邊看電視.

result.traditional: 媽媽不希望孩子邊吃飯邊看電視。
result.simplified: 妈妈不希望孩子边吃饭边看电视。
result.pinyin: Māma bù xīwàng háizi biān chīfàn biān kàn diànshì.
result.english: Mom doesn't want her child to watch television while eating.

alternatives.traditional: 媽媽不希望孩子邊看電視邊吃飯。
alternatives.simplified: 妈妈不希望孩子边看电视边吃饭。
alternatives.pinyin: Māma bù xīwàng háizi biān kàn diànshì biān chīfàn.
alternatives.english: Mom doesn't want her child to eat while watching television.

scene.alt: A man and a woman chatting at a café table with cups of coffee.

segments.traditional: 他喜歡跟朋友在咖啡廳
segments.simplified: 他喜欢跟朋友在咖啡厅

repairs.note: 先…再… puts one action after the other. In the picture they drink and chat at the same time: 一邊…，一邊….
先…再… puts one action after the other. In the picture they drink and chat at the same time: 一邊…，一邊….

items.fallbackRepair: 一邊 goes before each of the two actions.

result.traditional: 他喜歡跟朋友在咖啡廳一邊喝咖啡，一邊聊天。
result.simplified: 他喜欢跟朋友在咖啡厅一边喝咖啡，一边聊天。
result.pinyin: Tā xǐhuān gēn péngyǒu zài kāfēitīng yìbiān hē kāfēi, yìbiān liáotiān.
result.english: He likes to chat with friends over coffee at the café.

alternatives.traditional: 他喜歡跟朋友在咖啡廳一邊聊天，一邊喝咖啡。
alternatives.simplified: 他喜欢跟朋友在咖啡厅一边聊天，一边喝咖啡。
alternatives.pinyin: Tā xǐhuān gēn péngyǒu zài kāfēitīng yìbiān liáotiān, yìbiān hē kāfēi.
alternatives.english: He likes to drink coffee while chatting with friends at the café.

summary: Use 一邊 before each of two actions to say they happen at the same time, not one after the other.
It usually goes with specific action verbs.
One person can do both actions, or two people can each do one.
With one person, you can leave out 一 on both sides. With two people, keep 一.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Admit one fact, then give the surprising or contrasting result.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern implies that the speaker agrees to the information coming after “雖然” but the information coming after “可是” is unexpected.
grammarPages.pattern: 雖然 + Clause 1 + 可是 + Clause 2

text.traditional: 雖然不容易，可是我覺得很有意思。
text.simplified: 虽然不容易，可是我觉得很有意思。
text.pinyin: Suīrán bù róngyì, kěshì wǒ juéde hěn yǒuyìsi.
text.english: Although it is not easy, I find it very interesting.

text.traditional: 雖然他很聰明，可是不喜歡讀書，所以考得不好。
text.simplified: 虽然他很聪明，可是不喜欢读书，所以考得不好。
text.pinyin: Suīrán tā hěn cōngmíng, kěshì bù xǐhuān dúshū, suǒyǐ kǎo de bùhǎo.
text.english: Although he is clever, he does not like studying, so he did not do well on the test.

text.traditional: 雖然不舒服，可是今天公司有很重要的事，一定要去。
text.simplified: 虽然不舒服，可是今天公司有很重要的事，一定要去。
text.pinyin: Suīrán bù shūfu, kěshì jīntiān gōngsī yǒu hěn zhòngyào de shì, yídìng yào qù.
text.english: Although I feel unwell, something very important is happening at the company today, so I must go.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern implies that the speaker agrees to the information coming after “雖然” but the information coming after “可是” is unexpected.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern implies that the speaker agrees to the information coming after “雖然” but the information coming after “可是” is unexpected.

segments.traditional: 那件裙子非常貴，你還要買嗎？
segments.simplified: 那件裙子非常贵，你还要买吗？

repairs.note: The high price is not B's reason for buying. B accepts it and buys anyway: 雖然.
Liking the skirt goes against its high price, so the second half turns with 可是.

items.fallbackRepair: 雖然 opens the part B accepts, and 可是 turns to what matters more.

result.traditional: 雖然很貴，可是我很喜歡，還是要買。
result.simplified: 虽然很贵，可是我很喜欢，还是要买。
result.pinyin: Suīrán hěn guì, kěshì wǒ hěn xǐhuān, háishì yào mǎi.
result.english: Although it is expensive, I like it a lot, so I still want to buy it.

segments.traditional: 你為什麼住在這麼小的房子？
segments.simplified: 你为什么住在这么小的房子？

repairs.note: A asks why B lives there, so after 可是 comes the good side. A high price is no reason to stay.
Small and cheap pull in different directions, so the second half turns with 可是.

items.fallbackRepair: Start with what A said (it is small), then turn to the good side after 可是.

result.traditional: 雖然這個房子很小，可是很便宜。
result.simplified: 虽然这个房子很小，可是很便宜。
result.pinyin: Suīrán zhège fángzi hěn xiǎo, kěshì hěn piányí.
result.english: Although this house is small, it is cheap.

alternatives.traditional: 這個房子雖然很小，可是很便宜。
alternatives.simplified: 这个房子虽然很小，可是很便宜。
alternatives.pinyin: Zhège fángzi suīrán hěn xiǎo, kěshì hěn piányí.
alternatives.english: Although this house is small, it is cheap.

segments.traditional: 你玩遊戲常常輸，為什麼還要玩？
segments.simplified: 你玩游戏常常输，为什么还要玩？

repairs.note: A asks why B still plays. B must enjoy it: 很好玩.
不但…也… adds a second point of the same kind. Losing and still enjoying it is a turn: 雖然…，可是….
The second half goes against the first, so it turns with 可是, not 也.

items.fallbackRepair: 雖然 opens the part B accepts, and 可是 turns to why B still plays.

result.traditional: 雖然我常常輸，可是我覺得很好玩。
result.simplified: 虽然我常常输，可是我觉得很好玩。
result.pinyin: Suīrán wǒ chángcháng shū, kěshì wǒ juéde hěn hǎowán.
result.english: Although I often lose, I think it is a lot of fun.

summary: 雖然 admits a fact, then 可是 gives something unexpected or opposite.
Both the 雖然 part and the 可是 part must appear, and 可是 carries the contrast.
Don't use 所以 here, because 可是 shows contrast while 所以 shows a result.
Use 可是 or 但是 for the second part. 也 only adds and doesn't show contrast.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Meeting New Friends
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Emphasize a fact politely, as if saying 'you know' or 'actually'.
grammarPages.explanation: This particle “呢”, often placed at the end of a sentence, is used to emphasize that the foregoing action or fact is based on the speaker’s personal opinion. It shows a tone of politeness. The “呢” used here is different from that used in an interrogative sentence.
grammarPages.pattern: Statement + 呢！

text.traditional: 不，他家離我家很近呢！
text.simplified: 不，他家离我家很近呢！
text.pinyin: Bù, tā jiā lí wǒ jiā hěn jìn ne!
text.english: No—his home is actually very close to mine!

text.traditional: 可是我覺得很好看，想再看一次呢！
text.simplified: 可是我觉得很好看，想再看一次呢！
text.pinyin: Kěshì wǒ juéde hěn hǎokàn, xiǎng zài kàn yí cì ne!
text.english: But I think it is really good—I actually want to see it again!

text.traditional: 他沒出去玩，他一直在房間讀書呢！
text.simplified: 他没出去玩，他一直在房间读书呢！
text.pinyin: Tā méi chūqù wán, tā yìzhí zài fángjiān dúshū ne!
text.english: He did not go out to play—he has been studying in his room!

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This particle “呢”, often placed at the end of a sentence, is used to emphasize that the foregoing action or fact is based on the speaker’s personal opinion. It shows a tone of politeness. The “呢” used here is different from that used in an interrogative sentence.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This particle “呢”, often placed at the end of a sentence, is used to emphasize that the foregoing action or fact is based on the speaker’s personal opinion. It shows a tone of politeness. The “呢” used here is different from that used in an interrogative sentence.

segments.traditional: 良介在做什麼？我有事情想問他。
segments.simplified: 良介在做什么？我有事情想问他。

repairs.note: 嗎 asks a yes/no question. B is telling A what is going on, with 呢 for emphasis.
的 does not close a sentence about what someone is doing right now. B stresses it with 呢.

items.fallbackRepair: 在 before the action, and 呢 at the very end: 他在睡覺呢！

result.traditional: 他在睡覺呢！你等一下再來找他吧。
result.simplified: 他在睡觉呢！你等一下再来找他吧。
result.pinyin: Tā zài shuìjiào ne! Nǐ děng yíxià zài lái zhǎo tā ba.
result.english: He is sleeping! Come back for him a bit later.

segments.traditional: 這個週末妳要不要跟我去博物館？
segments.simplified: 这个周末你要不要跟我去博物馆？

repairs.note: 嗎 asks a yes/no question. The older sister is explaining why she is busy, with 呢 for emphasis.
She says 我沒空, so she does have a lot of homework: 還有.

items.fallbackRepair: 還有, then what she still has, and 呢 at the very end.

result.traditional: 我沒空，我還有很多功課呢！
result.simplified: 我没空，我还有很多功课呢！
result.pinyin: Wǒ méi kòng, wǒ hái yǒu hěn duō gōngkè ne!
result.english: I'm not free. I still have a lot of homework!

segments.traditional: 為什麼你每天都喝珍珠奶茶？
segments.simplified: 为什么你每天都喝珍珠奶茶？

segments.traditional: 珍珠奶茶又便宜又好喝，所以我

repairs.note: 嗎 asks a yes/no question. B is giving a reason, with 呢 for emphasis.
Before a measure word, "two" is 兩: 兩杯.

items.fallbackRepair: How often (一天), then the action, then how much, and 呢 at the very end: 一天喝兩杯呢！

result.traditional: 珍珠奶茶又便宜又好喝，所以我一天喝兩杯呢！
result.simplified: 珍珠奶茶又便宜又好喝，所以我一天喝两杯呢！
result.pinyin: Zhēnzhū nǎichá yòu piányí yòu hǎohē, suǒyǐ wǒ yì tiān hē liǎng bēi ne!
result.english: Bubble tea is cheap and tasty, so I drink two cups a day!

summary: Put 呢 at the end of a statement to stress an action or fact in a polite, relaxed tone.
This is not the 呢 of a question. For yes or no questions use 嗎.
吧 means a guess or suggestion. 呢 stresses a fact and sounds more sure.

items.title: Grammar 1–9 · I Have to Do Housework

text.traditional: 今天是開學的第一天，功課不多，我們一起去看球賽或是電影吧！
text.simplified: 今天是开学的第一天，功课不多，我们一起去看球赛或是电影吧！
text.pinyin: Jīntiān shì kāixué de dìyī tiān, gōngkè bù duō, wǒmen yìqǐ qù kàn qiúsài huòshì diànyǐng ba!
text.english: Today is the first day of school. We don't have much homework. Let's go watch a ball game or movie together!

text.traditional: 我不能去。我得先去我父母的餐廳幫忙，把桌子擦了，再把碗筷、刀叉洗一洗。
text.simplified: 我不能去。我得先去我父母的餐厅帮忙，把桌子擦了，再把碗筷、刀叉洗一洗。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bùnéng qù. Wǒ děi xiān qù wǒ fùmǔ de cāntīng bāngmáng, bǎ zhuōzi cā le, zài bǎ wǎnkuài, dāochā xǐ yì xǐ.
text.english: I can't go. I have to go to my parents' restaurant to help them wipe the tables first, and then wash the bowls, chopsticks, knives and forks.

text.traditional: 做那些事情要多久？
text.simplified: 做那些事情要多久？
text.pinyin: Zuò nàxiē shìqíng yào duōjiǔ?
text.english: How long will it take to do those things?

text.traditional: 客人多的時候差不多要兩個小時。
text.simplified: 客人多的时候差不多要两个小时。
text.pinyin: Kèrén duō de shíhòu chàbùduō yào liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
text.english: It takes about two hours when there are a lot of customers.

text.traditional: 要那麼久啊？
text.simplified: 要那么久啊？
text.pinyin: Yào nàme jiǔ a?
text.english: It takes such a long time! Isn't it?

text.traditional: 對啊，因為碗筷洗完了還得擦乾。有時候客人丟了東西，非常著急，我就得幫他們找一找，把東西拿給他們。
text.simplified: 对啊，因为碗筷洗完了还得擦干。有时候客人丢了东西，非常着急，我就得帮他们找一找，把东西拿给他们。
text.pinyin: Duì a, yīnwèi wǎnkuài xǐ wán le hái děi cāgān. Yǒushíhòu kèrén diū le dōngxi, fēicháng zhāojí, wǒ jiù děi bāng tāmen zhǎo yì zhǎo, bǎ dōngxi ná gěi tāmen.
text.english: Yes, because I have to wipe them dry after washing them. Sometimes when customers lose something and they are very anxious, I have to help them look for it and give it to them.

text.traditional: 那些事情做完以後，你就有空去看球賽了，對吧？
text.simplified: 那些事情做完以后，你就有空去看球赛了，对吧？
text.pinyin: Nàxiē shìqíng zuò wán yǐhòu, nǐ jiù yǒukòng qù kàn qiúsài le, duì ba?
text.english: After those things are finished, you're free to go watch a ball game, right?

text.traditional: 不，我得趕快回家。媽媽說我的房間太髒了，叫我今天一定要打掃。
text.simplified: 不，我得赶快回家。妈妈说我的房间太脏了，叫我今天一定要打扫。
text.pinyin: Bù, wǒ děi gǎnkuài huí jiā. Māma shuō wǒ de fángjiān tài zāng le, jiào wǒ jīntiān yídìng yào dǎsǎo.
text.english: No, I need to hurry home. My mom said that my room is too dirty, and I must do the cleaning today.

text.traditional: 你的房間有多髒啊？晚一點兒再打掃，應該沒關係吧？
text.simplified: 你的房间有多脏啊？晚一点儿再打扫，应该没关系吧？
text.pinyin: Nǐ de fángjiān yǒu duō zāng a? Wǎn yìdiǎnr zài dǎsǎo, yīnggāi méiguānxi ba?
text.english: How dirty is your room? It should be ok if you clean it later, isn't it?

text.traditional: 我已經三個月沒掃地了。
text.simplified: 我已经三个月没扫地了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng sān ge yuè méi sǎodì le.
text.english: I haven't swept the floor for three months.

text.traditional: 太久了吧！暑假那麼長，你什麼事都沒做嗎？
text.simplified: 太久了吧！暑假那么长，你什么事都没做吗？
text.pinyin: Tài jiǔ le ba! Shǔjià nàme cháng, nǐ shénme shì dōu méi zuò ma?
text.english: It's too long! The summer vacation was so long. Didn't you do anything?

text.traditional: 我先去日本玩了十天，回台灣以後，又跟朋友去南部玩了兩個星期。
text.simplified: 我先去日本玩了十天，回台湾以后，又跟朋友去南部玩了两个星期。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiān qù Rìběn wán le shí tiān, huí Táiwān yǐhòu, yòu gēn péngyǒu qù nánbù wán le liǎng ge xīngqí.
text.english: I went on a trip to Japan for ten days first. After coming back to Taiwan, I went traveling with my friends in southern Taiwan for two weeks.

text.traditional: 你玩了這麼多天，功課做了沒有？
text.simplified: 你玩了这么多天，功课做了没有？
text.pinyin: Nǐ wán le zhème duō tiān, gōngkè zuò le méiyǒu?
text.english: You went on a trip for so many days. Did you do your homework?

text.traditional: 暑假快結束的時候，我才看完老師要我們看的書，當然就沒時間打掃了。
text.simplified: 暑假快结束的时候，我才看完老师要我们看的书，当然就没时间打扫了。
text.pinyin: Shǔjià kuài jiéshù de shíhòu, wǒ cái kàn wán lǎoshī yào wǒmen kàn de shū, dāngrán jiù méi shíjiān dǎsǎo le.
text.english: When the summer vacation was about to end, I just finished reading the book the teacher had asked us to read. Of course I didn't have time to do the cleaning.

text.traditional: 可是如果房間太亂，我會覺得不舒服，也沒辦法念書。
text.simplified: 可是如果房间太乱，我会觉得不舒服，也没办法念书。
text.pinyin: Kěshì rúguǒ fángjiān tài luàn, wǒ huì juéde bù shūfu, yě méibànfǎ niànshū.
text.english: But if my room is too messy, I will not only feel uncomfortable but also find myself unable to study.

text.traditional: 對了，我家裡有一些中文小說，我覺得把那些書都丟了很可惜，送給你好嗎？
text.simplified: 对了，我家里有一些中文小说，我觉得把那些书都丢了很可惜，送给你好吗？
text.pinyin: Duìle, wǒ jiā lǐ yǒu yìxiē Zhōngwén xiǎoshuō, wǒ juéde bǎ nàxiē shū dōu diū le hěn kěxí, sòng gěi nǐ hǎo ma?
text.english: By the way, there are some Chinese novels in my house. I think it is a pity to throw them away. Can I give them to you?

text.traditional: 好啊！那些書對我學中文很有用。我先回宿舍把功課寫完，就去你家拿。
text.simplified: 好啊！那些书对我学中文很有用。我先回宿舍把功课写完，就去你家拿。
text.pinyin: Hǎo a! Nàxiē shū duì wǒ xué Zhōngwén hěn yǒuyòng. Wǒ xiān huí sùshè bǎ gōngkè xiě wán, jiù qù nǐ jiā ná.
text.english: Sure! Those books are very useful and can help me learn Chinese. I will get them from your house after I go back to the dormitory to finish my homework.

text.traditional: 太好了！這樣你就可以跟我一起打掃了。
text.simplified: 太好了！这样你就可以跟我一起打扫了。
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Zhèyàng nǐ jiù kěyǐ gēn wǒ yìqǐ dǎsǎo le.
text.english: That's great! Then you can do some cleaning with me.

text.traditional: 哈哈哈！
text.simplified: 哈哈哈！
text.pinyin: Hāhāhā!
text.english: Hahaha!

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.titleEnglish: The 把 construction: doing something to an object (1 of 4)
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 把 to say what you do to a thing and how the action ends.
grammarPages.explanation: The “把 construction”, also known as “disposal construction”, refers to how the Object is disposed of by the Subject through certain actions and cause certain result. Because this pattern often consists of a variety of complicated elements, the lesson begins with the most basic structure. The verbs used here must be outward and transitive, such as “看 (to see)”, “吃 (to eat)”, “賣 (to sell)”, and “寫 (to write)”. In negative sentences, negation words “不”, “沒” or “別” should be placed before “把”.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + (Negation) + 把 + Noun + Verb + 了

text.traditional: 爸爸把晚餐吃了嗎？
text.simplified: 爸爸把晚餐吃了吗？
text.pinyin: Bàba bǎ wǎncān chī le ma?
text.english: Did Dad eat the dinner?

text.traditional: 王先生沒把舊車賣了。
text.simplified: 王先生没把旧车卖了。
text.pinyin: Wáng xiānshēng méi bǎ jiù chē mài le.
text.english: Mr. Wang did not sell the old car.

text.traditional: 哥哥把牛奶喝了，就去睡覺了。
text.simplified: 哥哥把牛奶喝了，就去睡觉了。
text.pinyin: Gēge bǎ niúnǎi hē le, jiù qù shuìjiào le.
text.english: My older brother drank the milk and then went to bed.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The “把 construction”, also known as “disposal construction”, refers to how the Object is disposed of by the Subject through certain actions and cause certain result. Because this pattern often consists of a variety of complicated elements, the lesson begins with the most basic structure. The verbs used here must be outward and transitive, such as “看 (to see)”, “吃 (to eat)”, “賣 (to sell)”, and “寫 (to write)”. In negative sentences, negation words “不”, “沒” or “別” should be placed before “把”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The “把 construction”, also known as “disposal construction”, refers to how the Object is disposed of by the Subject through certain actions and cause certain result. Because this pattern often consists of a variety of complicated elements, the lesson begins with the most basic structure. The verbs used here must be outward and transitive, such as “看 (to see)”, “吃 (to eat)”, “賣 (to sell)”, and “寫 (to write)”. In negative sentences, negation words “不”, “沒” or “別” should be placed before “把”.

repairs.note: 給 marks the one who receives something. The thing that is dealt with comes after 把.

items.fallbackRepair: Who, then 把, then the thing, then what was done to it: 我把舊的字典賣了.

result.traditional: 我把舊的字典賣了。
result.simplified: 我把旧的字典卖了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ jiù de zìdiǎn mài le.
result.english: I sold the old dictionary.

repairs.note: 對 marks whom something is aimed at. The thing that is dealt with comes after 把.

items.fallbackRepair: Who, then 把, then the thing, then what was done to it: 誰把我買的蛋糕吃了？

result.traditional: 誰把我買的蛋糕吃了？
result.simplified: 谁把我买的蛋糕吃了？
result.pinyin: Shéi bǎ wǒ mǎi de dàngāo chī le?
result.english: Who ate the cake I bought?

repairs.note: 給 marks the one who receives something. The thing that is dealt with comes after 把.
在 marks a place. The thing that is dealt with comes after 把.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 first, then the thing, then what was done to it: 把不要的小說丟了.

result.traditional: 我昨天把不要的小說丟了。
result.simplified: 我昨天把不要的小说丢了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān bǎ búyào de xiǎoshuō diū le.
result.english: Yesterday I threw away the novels I didn't want.

alternatives.traditional: 昨天我把不要的小說丟了。
alternatives.simplified: 昨天我把不要的小说丢了。
alternatives.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ bǎ búyào de xiǎoshuō diū le.
alternatives.english: Yesterday I threw away the novels I didn't want.

summary: 把 puts the thing you act on before the verb and says what was done to it.
The verb must act on the object, like 看, 吃, 賣 or 寫.
The verb needs a result after it, such as 了 or 完. Plain 吃 isn't enough.
Put 不, 沒 or 別 before 把.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.titleEnglish: The 把 construction with the result 完 (2 of 4)
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that a task is finished: 把家事做完、把工作做完.
grammarPages.explanation: This grammar denotes that the action of the verb is over. The “完” after the verb, used as the V complement, means to end or to finish. Pay attention to the usage of “完”. This lesson uses the complement structure to describe the end of the action instead of using the word “完” alone. For example, the meaning of “我完了。（I'm finished.）” is completely different from the V 完 pattern.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + (Negation) + 把 + Noun + Verb + 完

text.traditional: 媽媽把家事做完以後，就休息了。
text.simplified: 妈妈把家事做完以后，就休息了。
text.pinyin: Māma bǎ jiāshì zuò wán yǐhòu, jiù xiūxí le.
text.english: After Mom finished the housework, she rested.

text.traditional: 因為你沒把工作做完，所以老闆不太高興。
text.simplified: 因为你没把工作做完，所以老板不太高兴。
text.pinyin: Yīnwèi nǐ méi bǎ gōngzuò zuò wán, suǒyǐ lǎobǎn bú tài gāoxìng.
text.english: Because you didn't finish the work, the boss is not very happy.

text.traditional: 請你先聽我把話說完，你再說，好嗎？
text.simplified: 请你先听我把话说完，你再说，好吗？
text.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ xiān tīng wǒ bǎ huà shuō wán, nǐ zài shuō, hǎo ma?
text.english: Please listen to me finish speaking before you speak, okay?

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This grammar denotes that the action of the verb is over. The “完” after the verb, used as the V complement, means to end or to finish. Pay attention to the usage of “完”. This lesson uses the complement structure to describe the end of the action instead of using the word “完” alone. For example, the meaning of “我完了。（I'm finished.）” is completely different from the V 完 pattern.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This grammar denotes that the action of the verb is over. The “完” after the verb, used as the V complement, means to end or to finish. Pay attention to the usage of “完”. This lesson uses the complement structure to describe the end of the action instead of using the word “完” alone. For example, the meaning of “我完了。（I'm finished.）” is completely different from the V 完 pattern.

practice.title: Complete the dialogues with the given words.

repairs.note: 給 marks the one who receives something. The thing to finish comes after 把.
在 marks a place. The thing to finish comes after 把, and finishing is V完.
V到 is reaching a place or a point. Finishing a task is V完: 寫完.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then the verb, then 完: 把書法寫完.

result.traditional: 我把書法寫完就去。
result.simplified: 我把书法写完就去。
result.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shūfǎ xiěwán jiù qù.
result.english: I'll go as soon as I finish my calligraphy.

repairs.note: A newspaper is read, not washed. The washing comes after: 再洗.
給 marks the one who receives something. The thing to finish comes after 把.
在 marks a place. The thing to finish comes after 把, and finishing is V完.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then the verb, then 完: 把報紙看完.

result.traditional: 等我把報紙看完再洗。
result.simplified: 等我把报纸看完再洗。
result.pinyin: Děng wǒ bǎ bàozhǐ kànwán zài xǐ.
result.english: I'll wash them once I've finished reading the newspaper.

repairs.note: 給 marks the one who receives something. The thing to finish comes after 把.
在 marks a place. The thing to finish comes after 把.
Mom puts one thing after the other: first finish dinner, then television. That is 再.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then the finished action, then 再 before what comes next.

result.traditional: 你把晚飯吃完再看電視。
result.simplified: 你把晚饭吃完再看电视。
result.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ wǎnfàn chīwán zài kàn diànshì.
result.english: Finish your dinner first, then watch television.

summary: Use 完 in a 把 sentence to say an action on the object is finished: 把家事做完.
完 goes right after the verb.
我完了 is different: it means all hope is gone, while 做完 means the action ended.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.titleEnglish: The 把 construction with a repeated verb (3 of 4)
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Make a request sound lighter: 把手洗一洗、把地掃一掃.
grammarPages.explanation: The “V一V” pattern softens the tone and makes an action simple and clear. When used together with “把 construction”, it gives requests or orders in a gentler tone. However, the verb used in this pattern has to be monosyllabic.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 把 + Noun + Verb + 一 + Verb

text.traditional: 把你的手洗一洗，我們要吃飯了。
text.simplified: 把你的手洗一洗，我们要吃饭了。
text.pinyin: Bǎ nǐ de shǒu xǐ yì xǐ, wǒmen yào chīfàn le.
text.english: Wash your hands; we are about to eat.

text.traditional: 回家以後，我先把垃圾倒一倒再去洗澡。
text.simplified: 回家以后，我先把垃圾倒一倒再去洗澡。
text.pinyin: Huí jiā yǐhòu, wǒ xiān bǎ lèsè dào yí dào zài qù xǐzǎo.
text.english: After going home, I first take out the garbage and then take a shower.

text.traditional: 太太：我覺得頭很疼，你可以幫我做家事嗎？先生：沒問題！我先把地掃一掃，等孩子回來以後，再把他們的髒衣服洗一洗。
text.simplified: 太太：我觉得头很疼，你可以帮我做家事吗？先生：没问题！我先把地扫一扫，等孩子回来以后，再把他们的脏衣服洗一洗。
text.pinyin: Tàitai: Wǒ juéde tóu hěn téng, nǐ kěyǐ bāng wǒ zuò jiāshì ma? Xiānshēng: Méi wèntí! Wǒ xiān bǎ dì sǎo yì sǎo, děng háizi huílái yǐhòu, zài bǎ tāmen de zāng yīfu xǐ yì xǐ.
text.english: Wife: I have a bad headache. Can you help me do the housework? Husband: No problem! I'll sweep the floor first, and after the children come back, I'll wash their dirty clothes.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The “V一V” pattern softens the tone and makes an action simple and clear. When used together with “把 construction”, it gives requests or orders in a gentler tone. However, the verb used in this pattern has to be monosyllabic.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The “V一V” pattern softens the tone and makes an action simple and clear. When used together with “把 construction”, it gives requests or orders in a gentler tone. However, the verb used in this pattern has to be monosyllabic.

practice.title: Complete the sentences with the given words.

repairs.note: 把價錢查了 is also good Chinese, but this exercise practises verb + 一 + verb: 把價錢查一查.
This is a plan, not a question. A softened action repeats the verb around 一: 查一查.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then verb + 一 + the same verb: 把價錢查一查.

result.traditional: 買手機以前，我先上網把價錢查一查再去買。
result.simplified: 买手机以前，我先上网把价钱查一查再去买。
result.pinyin: Mǎi shǒujī yǐqián, wǒ xiān shàngwǎng bǎ jiàqián chá yì chá zài qù mǎi.
result.english: Before buying a cell phone, I first check the prices online and then go buy it.

repairs.note: 把功課寫完 is also good Chinese, but this exercise practises verb + 一 + verb: 把功課寫一寫.
This is an instruction, not a question. A softened action repeats the verb around 一: 寫一寫.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then verb + 一 + the same verb: 把功課寫一寫.

result.traditional: 「你們把功課寫一寫就可以回家了。」
result.simplified: 「你们把功课写一写就可以回家了。」
result.pinyin: “Nǐmen bǎ gōngkè xiě yì xiě jiù kěyǐ huí jiā le.”
result.english: Get your homework done and then you can go home.

segments.traditional: 我晚一點兒再擦，現在要跟朋友去看球賽呢！
segments.simplified: 我晚一点儿再擦，现在要跟朋友去看球赛呢！

repairs.note: 給 marks the person who receives something. The table that is wiped comes after 把.
A gentle request repeats the verb around 一, not 不: 擦一擦.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then verb + 一 + the same verb: 把桌子擦一擦.

result.traditional: 你可以幫我把桌子擦一擦嗎？
result.simplified: 你可以帮我把桌子擦一擦吗？
result.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bāng wǒ bǎ zhuōzi cā yì cā ma?
result.english: Could you give the table a wipe for me?

summary: Use V一V in a 把 sentence for a quick, light action on the object.
It makes a request or instruction sound more polite and relaxed.
Only use one-syllable verbs, like 洗一洗 or 掃一掃.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.titleEnglish: The 把 construction with 給 (4 of 4)
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say who receives something: 把小說送給朋友、把舊車賣給你.
grammarPages.explanation: “給” is a preposition that indicates the direction of action and marks the recipient of the Direct Object. It can collocate with verbs “拿 (to take)”, “送 (to give)”, “賣 (to sell)”, “寄 (to send)”, “踢 (to kick)”, etc. It can also be used in 把 construction, such as “我把你做的蛋糕送給朋友了。”.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 把 + Noun + Verb + 給 + Receiver

text.traditional: 我昨天把那些小說送給朋友了。
text.simplified: 我昨天把那些小说送给朋友了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān bǎ nàxiē xiǎoshuō sòng gěi péngyǒu le.
text.english: Yesterday I gave those novels to a friend.

text.traditional: 王先生為什麼不想把舊車賣給你？
text.simplified: 王先生为什么不想把旧车卖给你？
text.pinyin: Wáng xiānshēng wèishénme bù xiǎng bǎ jiù chē mài gěi nǐ?
text.english: Why doesn't Mr. Wang want to sell the old car to you?

text.traditional: A：你昨天為什麼沒把感冒藥拿給孩子吃？B：醫生說那個藥是給大人吃的，不可以給小孩吃。
text.simplified: A：你昨天为什么没把感冒药拿给孩子吃？B：医生说那个药是给大人吃的，不可以给小孩吃。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ zuótiān wèishénme méi bǎ gǎnmào yào ná gěi háizi chī? B: Yīshēng shuō nàge yào shì gěi dàrén chī de, bù kěyǐ gěi xiǎohái chī.
text.english: A: Why didn't you give the cold medicine to the child yesterday? B: The doctor said that medicine is for adults; it must not be given to children.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “給” is a preposition that indicates the direction of action and marks the recipient of the Direct Object. It can collocate with verbs “拿 (to take)”, “送 (to give)”, “賣 (to sell)”, “寄 (to send)”, “踢 (to kick)”, etc. It can also be used in 把 construction, such as “我把你做的蛋糕送給朋友了。”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “給” is a preposition that indicates the direction of action and marks the recipient of the Direct Object. It can collocate with verbs “拿 (to take)”, “送 (to give)”, “賣 (to sell)”, “寄 (to send)”, “踢 (to kick)”, etc. It can also be used in 把 construction, such as “我把你做的蛋糕送給朋友了。”.

repairs.note: 對 marks whom something is aimed at. The thing given comes after 把, and the person after 送給.
跟 means "with". The thing given comes after 把, and the person after 送給.

items.fallbackRepair: 把, then the thing, then 送給, then the person: 把禮物送給張小姐.

result.traditional: 我昨天就把禮物送給張小姐了。
result.simplified: 我昨天就把礼物送给张小姐了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān jiù bǎ lǐwù sòng gěi Zhāng xiǎojiě le.
result.english: I already gave the gift to Miss Zhang yesterday.

repairs.note: 對 marks whom something is aimed at. The thing sent comes after 把, and the person after 寄給.

items.fallbackRepair: 沒 goes before 把, then the thing, then 寄給, then the person.

result.traditional: 哥哥是不是沒把生日卡片寄給媽媽？
result.simplified: 哥哥是不是没把生日卡片寄给妈妈？
result.pinyin: Gēge shì búshì méi bǎ shēngrì kǎpiàn jì gěi māma?
result.english: Did my older brother not send the birthday card to Mom?

repairs.note: A song is something you hear: 唱給我聽.
對 marks whom something is aimed at. The song comes after 把, and the listener after 唱給.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the song, then 唱給, then the person, then 聽.

result.traditional: 你可以把那首中文歌唱給我聽嗎？
result.simplified: 你可以把那首中文歌唱给我听吗？
result.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bǎ nà shǒu Zhōngwén gē chàng gěi wǒ tīng ma?
result.english: Could you sing that Chinese song for me?

summary: Put 給 after the verb in a 把 sentence to say who receives the object.
Say the thing first, then the verb with 給, then the receiver: 把舊車賣給你.
Don't put 給 before the verb. Common verbs are 送, 賣, 拿 and 寄.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask how big, long, far, high or expensive something is: 多大、多長、多遠.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern contains “Question Word 多+Vs (as predicate)” to inquire the degree achieved. In this pattern, “有” is frequently omitted.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + (有) + 多 + Vs?

text.traditional: A：你家離學校（有）多遠？B：我家離學校很遠，走路差不多要五十分鐘。
text.simplified: A：你家离学校（有）多远？B：我家离学校很远，走路差不多要五十分钟。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ jiā lí xuéxiào (yǒu) duō yuǎn? B: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn yuǎn, zǒulù chàbùduō yào wǔshí fēnzhōng.
text.english: A: How far is your home from school? B: My home is far from school; walking takes about fifty minutes.

text.traditional: A：那張桌子（有）多長？B：那張桌子（有）八十公分。
text.simplified: A：那张桌子（有）多长？B：那张桌子（有）八十公分。
text.pinyin: A: Nà zhāng zhuōzi (yǒu) duō cháng? B: Nà zhāng zhuōzi (yǒu) bāshí gōngfēn.
text.english: A: How long is that table? B: That table is 80 centimeters long.

text.traditional: A：你知道合歡山（有）多高嗎？B：差不多三千五百公尺。
text.simplified: A：你知道合欢山（有）多高吗？B：差不多三千五百公尺。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ zhīdào Héhuān Shān (yǒu) duō gāo ma? B: Chàbùduō sānqiānwǔbǎi gōngchǐ.
text.english: A: Do you know how high Hehuan Mountain is? B: About 3,500 meters.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern contains “Question Word 多+Vs (as predicate)” to inquire the degree achieved. In this pattern, “有” is frequently omitted.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern contains “Question Word 多+Vs (as predicate)” to inquire the degree achieved. In this pattern, “有” is frequently omitted.

practice.title: Complete the dialogues with the given words.

repairs.note: 很 states a degree. Asking about the degree is 多 + the quality.
幾 goes with a measure word (幾歲). Before a quality like 大, "how" is 多.
多少 asks for an amount of things (多少錢). Before a quality, "how" is just 多.
怎麼 asks in what way. Asking how old is 多大.

items.fallbackRepair: 多 first, then the quality: 多大？

result.traditional: 你妹妹多大？
result.pinyin: Nǐ mèimei duō dà?
result.english: How old is your younger sister?

segments.traditional: 聽說那場演唱會的票很貴，
segments.simplified: 听说那场演唱会的票很贵，

repairs.note: 多少 asks for an amount of things (多少錢). Before a quality, "how" is just 多.
很 states a degree. Asking about the degree is 多 + the quality.

items.fallbackRepair: 有 first, then 多, then the quality: 有多貴？

result.traditional: 聽說那場演唱會的票很貴，有多貴？
result.simplified: 听说那场演唱会的票很贵，有多贵？
result.pinyin: Tīngshuō nà chǎng yǎnchànghuì de piào hěn guì, yǒu duō guì?
result.english: I hear the tickets for that concert are expensive. How expensive?

repairs.note: B answers in kilograms (公斤), so the question is about weight: 重.
多少 asks for an amount of things. Before a quality, "how" is just 多.
幾 goes with a measure word (幾公斤). Before a quality like 重, "how" is 多.
很 states a degree. Asking about the degree is 多 + the quality.

items.fallbackRepair: 多 first, then the quality: 多重？

result.traditional: 你現在多重？
result.simplified: 你现在多重？
result.pinyin: Nǐ xiànzài duō zhòng?
result.english: How much do you weigh now?

summary: Put 多 before 大, 長, 高 or 遠 to ask how big, long, tall or far something is.
多 goes before the word: say 多高, not 高多.
有 can come before 多 but is often left out.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.titleTraditional: time-duration 沒 V（O）了 / time-duration 不 V（O）
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Not doing something for a period of time
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how long something has not happened or will not happen: 兩天沒睡覺、半年不說中文.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern, always including a negation word “不” or “沒,” indicates the time duration of a certain situation in which an action has yet to happen.
grammarPages.pattern: Time duration + 沒 + Verb (+ Object) + 了 / Time duration + 不 + Verb (+ Object)

text.traditional: 我已經兩天沒睡覺了，真累！
text.simplified: 我已经两天没睡觉了，真累！
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng liǎng tiān méi shuìjiào le, zhēn lèi!
text.english: I haven't slept for two days; I'm really tired!

text.traditional: 你想，如果山本良介半年不說中文，他還記得怎麼說嗎？
text.simplified: 你想，如果山本良介半年不说中文，他还记得怎么说吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng, rúguǒ Shānběn Liángjiè bàn nián bù shuō Zhōngwén, tā hái jìde zěnme shuō ma?
text.english: Do you think that if Yamamoto Ryosuke doesn't speak Chinese for half a year, he will still remember how to speak it?

text.traditional: A：他的房間有老鼠！B：真的嗎？他多久沒打掃了？
text.simplified: A：他的房间有老鼠！B：真的吗？他多久没打扫了？
text.pinyin: A: Tā de fángjiān yǒu lǎoshǔ! B: Zhēnde ma? Tā duōjiǔ méi dǎsǎo le?
text.english: A: There are mice in his room! B: Really? How long has it been since he cleaned?

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern, always including a negation word “不” or “沒,” indicates the time duration of a certain situation in which an action has yet to happen.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern, always including a negation word “不” or “沒,” indicates the time duration of a certain situation in which an action has yet to happen.

repairs.note: A stretch of time up to now without doing something takes 沒…了.
過 is for something done at least once. Time without doing it is 沒 + verb + 了.

items.fallbackRepair: How long, then 沒, then the action, then 了: 多久沒洗頭了？

result.traditional: 你的頭髮好髒！你多久沒洗頭了？
result.simplified: 你的头发好脏！你多久没洗头了？
result.pinyin: Nǐ de tóufǎ hǎo zāng! Nǐ duōjiǔ méi xǐ tóu le?
result.english: Your hair is so dirty! How long has it been since you washed it?

alternatives.traditional: 你的頭髮好髒！你沒洗頭多久了？
alternatives.simplified: 你的头发好脏！你没洗头多久了？
alternatives.pinyin: Nǐ de tóufǎ hǎo zāng! Nǐ méi xǐ tóu duōjiǔ le?
alternatives.english: Your hair is so dirty! How long has it been since you washed it?

segments.traditional: 林先生非常不喜歡說話。
segments.simplified: 林先生非常不喜欢说话。

repairs.note: After 能, B imagines what he could do, not what happened. That takes 不.
Nothing has happened yet: B only imagines it. There is no 了.
三點 is a point in time. How long he could stay silent is a length of time: 三天.

items.fallbackRepair: The length of time, then 不, then the action: 三天不說話.

result.traditional: 對啊，我想他能三天不說話。
result.simplified: 对啊，我想他能三天不说话。
result.pinyin: Duì a, wǒ xiǎng tā néng sān tiān bù shuōhuà.
result.english: Right, I think he could go three days without talking.

segments.traditional: 為什麼你今天一定要去運動？
segments.simplified: 为什么你今天一定要去运动？

repairs.note: A stretch of time up to now without doing something takes 沒…了.
星期一 is a day. How long B has gone without exercise is a length of time: 一個星期.

items.fallbackRepair: The length of time, then 沒, then the action, then 了.

result.traditional: 因為我已經一個星期沒運動了。
result.simplified: 因为我已经一个星期没运动了。
result.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ yǐjīng yí ge xīngqí méi yùndòng le.
result.english: Because I haven't exercised for a week already.

summary: Put a length of time before 沒 or 不 to say how long an action hasn't happened: 兩天沒睡覺.
了 often comes at the end. With 沒, it shows the state still continues up to now.
不 can describe a repeated or habitual absence of the action.
多久沒 asks how long since the last time, not how many times.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Question word + 都 / 也: all or none
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that everyone, everything or everywhere is included or excluded: 誰也不認識、哪裡都有.
grammarPages.explanation: In Chinese, question words may co-occur with “都” or “也” in declarative sentences to indicate entirety. That is, in affirmative sentences, this pattern indicates total inclusion, while in negative ones, it indicates total exclusion.
grammarPages.pattern: Question word + 都 / 也 + Verb phrase

text.traditional: 錢先生哪國語言都會說。
text.simplified: 钱先生哪国语言都会说。
text.pinyin: Qián xiānshēng nǎ guó yǔyán dōu huì shuō.
text.english: Mr. Qian can speak the languages of every country.

text.traditional: 我不舒服，什麼都不想吃。
text.simplified: 我不舒服，什么都不想吃。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù shūfu, shénme dōu bù xiǎng chī.
text.english: I don't feel well; I don't want to eat anything.

text.traditional: 我剛剛到台灣，誰也不認識。
text.simplified: 我刚刚到台湾，谁也不认识。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gānggāng dào Táiwān, shéi yě bú rènshì.
text.english: I have just arrived in Taiwan; I don't know anyone.

text.traditional: 中國菜很有名，哪裡都有中國餐廳。
text.simplified: 中国菜很有名，哪里都有中国餐厅。
text.pinyin: Zhōngguó cài hěn yǒumíng, nǎlǐ dōu yǒu Zhōngguó cāntīng.
text.english: Chinese food is famous; Chinese restaurants are everywhere.

text.traditional: 這個字很難，我怎麼寫都不對。
text.simplified: 这个字很难，我怎么写都不对。
text.pinyin: Zhège zì hěn nán, wǒ zěnme xiě dōu bú duì.
text.english: This character is hard; however I write it, it is wrong.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In Chinese, question words may co-occur with “都” or “也” in declarative sentences to indicate entirety. That is, in affirmative sentences, this pattern indicates total inclusion, while in negative ones, it indicates total exclusion.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In Chinese, question words may co-occur with “都” or “也” in declarative sentences to indicate entirety. That is, in affirmative sentences, this pattern indicates total inclusion, while in negative ones, it indicates total exclusion.

segments.traditional: 我們什麼時候去看電影？
segments.simplified: 我们什么时候去看电影？

repairs.note: A asks when, so the answer keeps 什麼時候.
After a question word, "any" takes 都.
B is answering, not asking. "Any time" is 什麼時候都….

items.fallbackRepair: The question word, then 都, then what is true: 什麼時候都可以.

result.traditional: 什麼時候都可以。
result.simplified: 什么时候都可以。
result.pinyin: Shénme shíhòu dōu kěyǐ.
result.english: Any time is fine.

segments.traditional: 你覺得我穿哪一件衣服好看？
segments.simplified: 你觉得我穿哪一件衣服好看？

repairs.note: A asks which piece of clothing, so the answer keeps 哪一件.
After a question word, "any" takes 都.
After the question word comes 都, then the quality: 哪一件都好看.

items.fallbackRepair: The question word, then 都, then what is true: 哪一件都好看.

result.traditional: 你穿哪一件都好看。
result.pinyin: Nǐ chuān nǎ yí jiàn dōu hǎokàn.
result.english: You look good in any of them.

segments.traditional: 放暑假的時候，你想去哪裡玩？
segments.simplified: 放暑假的时候，你想去哪里玩？

repairs.note: A asks where, so the answer keeps 哪裡.
A asks where, so the answer keeps 哪裡.
After a question word, "everywhere" takes 都.

items.fallbackRepair: The question word, then 都, then what is true: 哪裡都想去.

result.traditional: 我哪裡都想去。
result.simplified: 我哪里都想去。
result.pinyin: Wǒ nǎlǐ dōu xiǎng qù.
result.english: I want to go everywhere.

summary: Put 都 or 也 after a question word to mean everything, everyone or everywhere.
In a positive sentence it includes all. In a negative sentence it means none.
The question word comes first, then 都 or 也: 誰也不認識.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that something happens again: 又餓了、又要去買書.
grammarPages.explanation: “又” means the repetition of the same action or the reappearance of similar situation. “再” and “又” both mean repetition. However, “再” emphasizes the intention to repeat certain actions, so it can be used in imperative sentences and placed after modal verbs, e.g., “請再說一次” (Please say it again.) and “我想再喝一杯”. (I'd like to have another drink.) “又” is used after certain actions or showing the intention of performing the action. “又” mostly collocates with “了” or “沒” and is placed before the modal verbs. e.g., “我又說了一次” (I said that again.) and “我又想喝了” (I wanted to drink again.)
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 又 + Verb phrase

text.traditional: 他剛剛吃了一碗牛肉麵和三個包子，現在又餓了。
text.simplified: 他刚刚吃了一碗牛肉面和三个包子，现在又饿了。
text.pinyin: Tā gānggāng chī le yì wǎn niúròu miàn hé sān ge bāozi, xiànzài yòu è le.
text.english: He just ate a bowl of beef noodles and three steamed buns, and now he is hungry again.

text.traditional: 金先生上個月買的書都看完了，今天又要去買書了。
text.simplified: 金先生上个月买的书都看完了，今天又要去买书了。
text.pinyin: Jīn xiānshēng shàng ge yuè mǎi de shū dōu kàn wán le, jīntiān yòu yào qù mǎi shū le.
text.english: Mr. Jin finished all the books he bought last month, and today he is going to buy books again.

text.traditional: 他去美國旅行了兩個星期以後，又去越南玩了五天。
text.simplified: 他去美国旅行了两个星期以后，又去越南玩了五天。
text.pinyin: Tā qù Měiguó lǚxíng le liǎng ge xīngqí yǐhòu, yòu qù Yuènán wán le wǔ tiān.
text.english: After traveling in the United States for two weeks, he went on to Vietnam for another five days.

segments.traditional: 姐姐上個禮拜買了新衣服，昨天
segments.simplified: 姐姐上个礼拜买了新衣服，昨天

repairs.note: 再 is for doing something again later. Something that already happened again takes 又.

items.fallbackRepair: 又 before the verb, and 了 after it: 又買了一件.

result.traditional: 姐姐上個禮拜買了新衣服，昨天又買了一件。
result.simplified: 姐姐上个礼拜买了新衣服，昨天又买了一件。
result.pinyin: Jiějie shàng ge lǐbài mǎi le xīn yīfu, zuótiān yòu mǎi le yí jiàn.
result.english: My older sister bought new clothes last week, and yesterday she bought another one.

segments.traditional: 他去年來台灣學了半年的中文，今年
segments.simplified: 他去年来台湾学了半年的中文，今年

repairs.note: 再 is for doing something again later. Something that already happened again takes 又.

items.fallbackRepair: 又 before the verb, and 了 after it: 又來了.

result.traditional: 他去年來台灣學了半年的中文，今年又來了。
result.simplified: 他去年来台湾学了半年的中文，今年又来了。
result.pinyin: Tā qùnián lái Táiwān xué le bànnián de Zhōngwén, jīnnián yòu lái le.
