segments.traditional: 那個學生前天沒寫功課，昨天
segments.simplified: 那个学生前天没写功课，昨天

repairs.note: 再 is for doing something again later. Something that already happened again takes 又.
The teacher is unhappy, so the homework was again not done: 又沒寫.

items.fallbackRepair: 又 first, then 沒, then the verb: 又沒寫.

result.traditional: 那個學生前天沒寫功課，昨天又沒寫，老師很不高興。
result.simplified: 那个学生前天没写功课，昨天又没写，老师很不高兴。
result.pinyin: Nàge xuéshēng qiántiān méi xiě gōngkè, zuótiān yòu méi xiě, lǎoshī hěn bù gāoxìng.
result.english: That student didn't do the homework the day before yesterday and again didn't do it yesterday; the teacher is very unhappy.

summary: 又 says the same action or a similar situation happens again.
又 goes before the verb and often pairs with 了 or 沒.
再 is for wanting or planning to do it again, usually after a word like can or want.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say something happened later than expected: 十一點才起來、昨天才到.
grammarPages.explanation: “才” implies that an action happened or will happen later than expected.
grammarPages.pattern: Time + 才 + Verb phrase

text.traditional: 我昨天太累了，所以今天早上十一點才起來。
text.simplified: 我昨天太累了，所以今天早上十一点才起来。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān tài lèi le, suǒyǐ jīntiān zǎoshàng shíyī diǎn cái qǐlái.
text.english: I was too tired yesterday, so I did not get up until eleven this morning.

text.traditional: A：你是上個月從英國到台灣的嗎？B：不是，我是昨天才到的。
text.simplified: A：你是上个月从英国到台湾的吗？B：不是，我是昨天才到的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ shì shàng ge yuè cóng Yīngguó dào Táiwān de ma? B: Búshì, wǒ shì zuótiān cái dào de.
text.english: A: Did you come to Taiwan from the UK last month? B: No, I only arrived yesterday.

text.traditional: A：我們什麼時候考試？我還沒準備，怎麼辦？B：我們下個禮拜才考，你還有時間準備。
text.simplified: A：我们什么时候考试？我还没准备，怎么办？B：我们下个礼拜才考，你还有时间准备。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen shénme shíhòu kǎoshì? Wǒ háiméi zhǔnbèi, zěnmebàn? B: Wǒmen xià ge lǐbài cái kǎo, nǐ háiyǒu shíjiān zhǔnbèi.
text.english: A: When is our exam? I haven't prepared yet; what should I do? B: Our exam is not until next week; you still have time to prepare.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “才” implies that an action happened or will happen later than expected.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “才” implies that an action happened or will happen later than expected.

practice.title: Complete the dialogues with the given words.

segments.traditional: 聽說你這個週末要去日本？
segments.simplified: 听说你这个周末要去日本？

repairs.note: Next weekend is later than A thought, and later than expected takes 才.
B says 不是, so it is not this weekend.
B is going to Japan, away from here: 去.

items.fallbackRepair: The time first, then 才, then the verb: 下個週末才去.

result.traditional: 不是，我下個週末才去。
result.simplified: 不是，我下个周末才去。
result.pinyin: Búshì, wǒ xià ge zhōumò cái qù.
result.english: No, I'm not going until next weekend.

segments.traditional: 趕快起來！你早上八點有中文課！
segments.simplified: 赶快起来！你早上八点有中文课！

repairs.note: Ten o'clock is later than A thought, and later than expected takes 才.
B says 不對, so the class is not at eight.
B does have class, only later: 才有課.

items.fallbackRepair: The time first, then 才, then what happens: 早上十點才有課.

result.traditional: 不對，我早上十點才有課。
result.simplified: 不对，我早上十点才有课。
result.pinyin: Bú duì, wǒ zǎoshàng shí diǎn cái yǒu kè.
result.english: No, I don't have class until ten in the morning.

segments.traditional: 你明天晚上要不要跟我一起去看籃球比賽？
segments.simplified: 你明天晚上要不要跟我一起去看篮球比赛？

repairs.note: B is talking about when B will be free, which is still to come: 後天.
B is not free tomorrow, and is free only the day after: 才有空.
Here the day after tomorrow is later than A hoped, which takes 才.

items.fallbackRepair: The time first, then 才, then what happens: 後天才有空.

result.traditional: 不好意思，我明天沒空，後天才有空。
result.simplified: 不好意思，我明天没空，后天才有空。
result.pinyin: Bùhǎoyìsi, wǒ míngtiān méi kòng, hòutiān cái yǒukòng.
result.english: Sorry, I'm not free tomorrow; I won't be free until the day after tomorrow.

summary: Put 才 before the verb to say something happens later than expected, which the speaker sees as late.
The time comes first, then 才, then the verb: 十一點才起來.

items.title: Grammar 10–11 · I Want to Live in a Clean Place

dialogue.title: 短文 · 我要住在乾淨的地方

text.traditional: 山本良介今天早上出門的時候，看見房間門口有一個袋子。他把袋子打開，發現裡面都是垃圾。下樓的時候，樓梯上也有垃圾。他想：「是誰把垃圾丟在這裡的？好髒啊！」他知道應該先把垃圾丟到垃圾桶，再去上課，可是他很急，不想在開學的第一天就遲到，所以什麼都沒做就去上課了。
text.simplified: 山本良介今天早上出门的时候，看见房间门口有一个袋子。他把袋子打开，发现里面都是垃圾。下楼的时候，楼梯上也有垃圾。他想：「是谁把垃圾丢在这里的？好脏啊！」他知道应该先把垃圾丢到垃圾桶，再去上课，可是他很急，不想在开学的第一天就迟到，所以什么都没做就去上课了。
text.pinyin: Shānběn Liángjiè jīntiān zǎoshàng chūmén de shíhòu, kànjiàn fángjiān ménkǒu yǒu yíge dàizi. Tā bǎ dàizi dǎkāi, fāxiàn lǐmiàn dōu shì lèsè. Xià lóu de shíhòu, lóutī shàng yě yǒu lèsè. Tā xiǎng: “Shì shéi bǎ lèsè diū zài zhèlǐ de? Hǎo zāng a!” Tā zhīdào yīnggāi xiān bǎ lèsè diū dào lèsè tǒng, zài qù shàngkè, kěshì tā hěn jí, bù xiǎng zài kāixué de dìyī tiān jiù chídào, suǒyǐ shénme dōu méi zuò jiù qù shàngkè le.
text.english: When Yamamoto Ryosuke went out this morning, he saw a bag at the door of his dorm room. He opened the bag and found that there was nothing but garbage in it. When he went downstairs, there was also garbage on the stairs. “Who dumped the garbage here? It's so dirty!” he thought. He knew that he should have thrown the garbage to the trash can before attending class, but he was in a hurry because he did not want to be late on the first day of school. Therefore, he went to class without doing anything.

text.traditional: 中午良介回去的時候，覺得宿舍裡的空氣很不好。因為垃圾的味道很臭，而且到處都有小蟲子在飛，他就趕快把全部的垃圾都丟了。良介記得小時候媽媽告訴過他，吃完飯以後要洗碗、倒垃圾。星期六起床以後，不但要打掃房間，也得把髒衣服洗一洗。這些家事做完了以後，住在房子裡的每一個人才會覺得舒服。要是客人或是鄰居要來，也不用擔心家裡太髒。
text.simplified: 中午良介回去的时候，觉得宿舍里的空气很不好。因为垃圾的味道很臭，而且到处都有小虫子在飞，他就赶快把全部的垃圾都丢了。良介记得小时候妈妈告诉过他，吃完饭以后要洗碗、倒垃圾。星期六起床以后，不但要打扫房间，也得把脏衣服洗一洗。这些家事做完了以后，住在房子里的每一个人才会觉得舒服。要是客人或是邻居要来，也不用担心家里太脏。
text.pinyin: Zhōngwǔ Liángjiè huíqù de shíhòu, juéde sùshè lǐ de kōngqì hěn bùhǎo. Yīnwèi lèsè de wèidào hěn chòu, érqiě dàochù dōu yǒu xiǎo chóngzi zài fēi, tā jiù gǎnkuài bǎ quánbù de lèsè dōu diū le. Liángjiè jìde xiǎoshíhòu māma gàosu guò tā, chī wán fàn yǐhòu yào xǐ wǎn, dào lèsè. Xīngqíliù qǐchuáng yǐhòu, búdàn yào dǎsǎo fángjiān, yě děi bǎ zāng yīfu xǐ yì xǐ. Zhèxiē jiāshì zuò wán le yǐhòu, zhù zài fángzi lǐ de měi yíge rén cái huì juéde shūfu. Yàoshì kèrén huòshì línjū yào lái, yě búyòng dānxīn jiā lǐ tài zāng.
text.english: At noon, when Ryosuke went back to the dorm, he felt that the air was not good, and that the smell of garbage was not good. What's more, there were insects flying everywhere. So he immediately threw all the garbage away. Ryosuke remembered as a child, his mother had taught him to do the dishes and take out the garbage after finishing a meal. On Saturday after waking up, in addition to cleaning up his room, he needed to wash dirty clothes. After the housework is done, everyone living in the house would feel comfortable. If a guest or a neighbor came to visit them, there was no need to worry that the house was too dirty, either.

text.traditional: 晚上良介吃完飯，回宿舍的時候，他看見牆上寫著「不要亂丟垃圾」，可是地上還是有一些垃圾。他想，要是每個人都覺得打掃是別人的事，不久以後，這個地方就會又髒又亂，沒有人想住了。
text.simplified: 晚上良介吃完饭，回宿舍的时候，他看见墙上写着「不要乱丢垃圾」，可是地上还是有一些垃圾。他想，要是每个人都觉得打扫是别人的事，不久以后，这个地方就会又脏又乱，没有人想住了。
text.pinyin: Wǎnshàng Liángjiè chī wán fàn, huí sùshè de shíhòu, tā kànjiàn qiángshàng xiě zhe “búyào luàn diū lèsè”, kěshì dìshàng háishì yǒu yìxiē lèsè. Tā xiǎng, yàoshì měi ge rén dōu juéde dǎsǎo shì biérén de shì, bùjiǔ yǐhòu, zhège dìfāng jiù huì yòu zāng yòu luàn, méiyǒu rén xiǎng zhù le.
text.english: After eating in the evening, Ryosuke went back to school. He saw “No Littering” written on the wall. However, there was still some garbage on the ground. He thought that if everyone considers cleaning to be other people's business, this place would be dirty and messy soon after, and nobody wants to live in.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.titleEnglish: The 把 construction with 在 and 到
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say where something ends up: 丟在浴室裡、拿到桌子上.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern is the combination of “S（+Neg）+把+N+V+Complement” (see the first grammar after the dialogue in this lesson) and “V在” (see the first grammar after the text in Lesson One) and “V到”. It indicates the location or place of the Object after the action is over.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 把 + Noun + Verb + 在 / 到 + Place

text.traditional: 孩子把髒衣服丟在浴室裡。
text.simplified: 孩子把脏衣服丢在浴室里。
text.pinyin: Háizi bǎ zāng yīfu diū zài yùshì lǐ.
text.english: The child threw the dirty clothes in the bathroom.

text.traditional: 你怎麼沒把地址寫在信封上呢？
text.simplified: 你怎么没把地址写在信封上呢？
text.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme méi bǎ dìzhǐ xiě zài xìnfēng shàng ne?
text.english: How come you didn't write the address on the envelope?

text.traditional: 我覺得把錢放在銀行比放在家裡安全得多。
text.simplified: 我觉得把钱放在银行比放在家里安全得多。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde bǎ qián fàng zài yínháng bǐ fàng zài jiā lǐ ānquán de duō.
text.english: I think putting money in the bank is much safer than keeping it at home.

text.traditional: 媽媽把蛋糕拿到廚房的桌子上。
text.simplified: 妈妈把蛋糕拿到厨房的桌子上。
text.pinyin: Māma bǎ dàngāo ná dào chúfáng de zhuōzi shàng.
text.english: Mom took the cake to the kitchen table.

text.traditional: 你不可以把球踢到馬路上，太危險了。
text.simplified: 你不可以把球踢到马路上，太危险了。
text.pinyin: Nǐ bù kěyǐ bǎ qiú tī dào mǎlù shàng, tài wéixiǎn le.
text.english: You must not kick the ball onto the road; it's too dangerous.

text.traditional: 李小姐把生日卡片寄到男朋友家。
text.simplified: 李小姐把生日卡片寄到男朋友家。
text.pinyin: Lǐ xiǎojiě bǎ shēngrì kǎpiàn jì dào nánpéngyǒu jiā.
text.english: Miss Li mailed the birthday card to her boyfriend's home.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is the combination of “S（+Neg）+把+N+V+Complement” (see the first grammar after the dialogue in this lesson) and “V在” (see the first grammar after the text in Lesson One) and “V到”. It indicates the location or place of the Object after the action is over.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern is the combination of “S（+Neg）+把+N+V+Complement” (see the first grammar after the dialogue in this lesson) and “V在” (see the first grammar after the text in Lesson One) and “V到”. It indicates the location or place of the Object after the action is over.

repairs.note: 穿 is for clothes and shoes. A watch is worn with 戴.
給 marks the one who receives something. Where the watch ends up takes 在.
對 marks whom something is aimed at. Where the watch ends up takes 在.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 在 before the place: 戴在你的手上.

result.traditional: 為什麼你把我的手錶戴在你的手上？
result.simplified: 为什么你把我的手表戴在你的手上？
result.pinyin: Wèishénme nǐ bǎ wǒ de shǒubiǎo dài zài nǐ de shǒu shàng?
result.english: Why are you wearing my watch on your wrist?

repairs.note: The student forgot to take it home, so the textbook is not at home.
給 marks the one who receives something. Where the textbook was left takes 在.
帶 is carrying something along. Leaving it somewhere is 放在.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 在, then the place: 放在教室裡.

result.traditional: 那個學生把課本放在教室裡，忘了帶回家了。
result.simplified: 那个学生把课本放在教室里，忘了带回家了。
result.pinyin: Nàge xuéshēng bǎ kèběn fàng zài jiàoshì lǐ, wàng le dài huí jiā le.
result.english: That student left the textbook in the classroom and forgot to take it home.

segments.traditional: 地上，所以房間的味道真不好。
segments.simplified: 地上，所以房间的味道真不好。

repairs.note: The room smells bad, so what lies on the floor is dirty clothes.
給 marks the person who receives something. Where the clothes end up takes 在.

items.fallbackRepair: 把, then the thing, then the verb, then 在 before the place.

result.traditional: 室友常常把髒衣服丟在地上，所以房間的味道真不好。
result.simplified: 室友常常把脏衣服丢在地上，所以房间的味道真不好。
result.pinyin: Shìyǒu chángcháng bǎ zāng yīfu diū zài dì shàng, suǒyǐ fángjiān de wèidào zhēn bù hǎo.
result.english: My roommate often throws dirty clothes on the floor, so the room smells really bad.

segments.traditional: 考試的時候，不可以把手機放在桌子上，請你
segments.simplified: 考试的时候，不可以把手机放在桌子上，请你

repairs.note: 給 marks the one who receives something. The thing to move comes after 把.
A phone is put somewhere, not written: 放.
對 marks whom something is aimed at. The thing to move comes after 把.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then the verb, then 到 before where it goes.

result.traditional: 考試的時候，不可以把手機放在桌子上，請你把手機放到袋子裡。
result.simplified: 考试的时候，不可以把手机放在桌子上，请你把手机放到袋子里。
result.pinyin: Kǎoshì de shíhòu, bù kěyǐ bǎ shǒujī fàng zài zhuōzi shàng, qǐng nǐ bǎ shǒujī fàng dào dàizi lǐ.
result.english: During the exam you may not leave your phone on the desk; please put it in your bag.

repairs.note: 送給 gives something to a person. Taking someone to a place is 送到.
The person is moved to a new place, and movement to a place takes 到.
An injured person is taken to a hospital, not to a bank.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 到, then the place: 送到醫院.

result.traditional: 警察把那個受傷的人送到醫院。
result.simplified: 警察把那个受伤的人送到医院。
result.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ nàge shòushāng de rén sòng dào yīyuàn.
result.english: The police took the injured person to the hospital.

repairs.note: The drink is carried into a new place, and movement to a place takes 到.
給 marks the one who receives something. Where the drink is carried takes 到.
What moves the drink into the library is carrying it: 帶到.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 到, then the place: 帶到圖書館裡.

result.traditional: 你不可以把飲料帶到圖書館裡。
result.simplified: 你不可以把饮料带到图书馆里。
result.pinyin: Nǐ bù kěyǐ bǎ yǐnliào dài dào túshūguǎn lǐ.
result.english: You may not bring drinks into the library.

summary: Put 在 or 到 and the place after the verb in a 把 sentence, not before it: 丟在浴室裡.
在 marks where the object stays after the action. 到 marks the place it reaches.
An address stays on the envelope, so use 寫在. Use 寄到 for sending something to a place.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Have to Do Housework
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what result follows only when a condition is met: 才不會覺得冷、才能寫得好看.
grammarPages.explanation: In this pattern, the adverb “才” in the second clause is used to show consequences when the conditions and causes in the first clause are fulfilled. Thus, “得 (have to)”, “要 (need to)”, “為了 (in order to)”, and “因為 (because)” are often used in the first clause of this pattern.
grammarPages.pattern: Condition + 才 + Result

text.traditional: 他昨天是因為生病才沒來上課。
text.simplified: 他昨天是因为生病才没来上课。
text.pinyin: Tā zuótiān shì yīnwèi shēngbìng cái méi lái shàngkè.
text.english: Yesterday he missed class only because he was sick.

text.traditional: 你最好再穿一件衣服，才不會覺得冷。
text.simplified: 你最好再穿一件衣服，才不会觉得冷。
text.pinyin: Nǐ zuìhǎo zài chuān yí jiàn yīfu, cái bú huì juéde lěng.
text.english: You'd better put on another piece of clothing so you won't feel cold.

text.traditional: 你得每天練習寫字，字才能寫得好看。
text.simplified: 你得每天练习写字，字才能写得好看。
text.pinyin: Nǐ děi měi tiān liànxí xiě zì, zì cáinéng xiě de hǎokàn.
text.english: You have to practice writing every day; only then can your characters look good.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In this pattern, the adverb “才” in the second clause is used to show consequences when the conditions and causes in the first clause are fulfilled. Thus, “得 (have to)”, “要 (need to)”, “為了 (in order to)”, and “因為 (because)” are often used in the first clause of this pattern.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In this pattern, the adverb “才” in the second clause is used to show consequences when the conditions and causes in the first clause are fulfilled. Thus, “得 (have to)”, “要 (need to)”, “為了 (in order to)”, and “因為 (because)” are often used in the first clause of this pattern.

repairs.note: Here 再 would only put one action after another. Going in is possible only after buying the ticket: 才可以進去.
Buying the ticket is what lets you in: 才可以進去.
Only after buying the ticket can you go in: 才可以進去.

items.fallbackRepair: 才 first, then 可以, then the action: 才可以進去.

result.traditional: 你得先買票，才可以進去。
result.simplified: 你得先买票，才可以进去。
result.pinyin: Nǐ děi xiān mǎi piào, cái kěyǐ jìnqù.
result.english: You have to buy a ticket first; only then can you go in.

segments.traditional: 你應該早一點兒睡覺，明天
segments.simplified: 你应该早一点儿睡觉，明天

repairs.note: Going to bed earlier is so that you will not be late: 才不會遲到.
Here 再 would only put one action after another. Sleeping early is what keeps you from being late: 才不會遲到.
Sleeping early is the only way not to be late, and "only then" is 才.

items.fallbackRepair: 才 first, then 不會, then the verb: 才不會遲到.

result.traditional: 你應該早一點兒睡覺，明天才不會遲到。
result.simplified: 你应该早一点儿睡觉，明天才不会迟到。
result.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi zǎo yìdiǎnr shuìjiào, míngtiān cái bú huì chídào.
result.english: You should go to bed a little earlier; only then will you not be late tomorrow.

repairs.note: 所以 starts a result. Here the result already has 才, and the reason opens with 是因為.
Having plenty of money is no reason for not buying a gift.
雖然 needs a turn with 可是 after it. The reason before 才 opens with 是因為.

items.fallbackRepair: 是 first, then 因為, then the reason: 是因為沒有錢，才….

result.traditional: 我是因為沒有錢，才沒買禮物給你的。
result.simplified: 我是因为没有钱，才没买礼物给你的。
result.pinyin: Wǒ shì yīnwèi méiyǒu qián, cái méi mǎi lǐwù gěi nǐ de.
result.english: It was because I had no money that I didn't buy you a gift.

summary: 才 goes in the second part and says the result happens only after the earlier condition or reason is true.
Put 才 right before the result: 才不會覺得冷.
The first part often has 得, 要, 為了 or 因為.

items.title: Grammar 1–7 · I Want to Rent a House

text.traditional: （良介去看房子，他和可欣到了公寓的門口，房東王太太剛好出來了。）
text.simplified: （良介去看房子，他和可欣到了公寓的门口，房东王太太刚好出来了。）
text.pinyin: (Liángjiè qù kàn fángzi, tā hé Kěxīn dào le gōngyù de ménkǒu, fángdōng Wáng tàitai gānghǎo chūlái le.)
text.english: (Ryosuke goes to view a house. When Kexin and he arrive at the gate of the apartment building, Mrs. Wang, the landlord just shows up.)

text.traditional: 王太太，您好。我是陳可欣。這位是我的朋友山本良介，我陪他來看房子。
text.simplified: 王太太，您好。我是陈可欣。这位是我的朋友山本良介，我陪他来看房子。
text.pinyin: Wáng tàitai, nín hǎo. Wǒ shì Chén Kěxīn. Zhè wèi shì wǒ de péngyǒu Shānběn Liángjiè, wǒ péi tā lái kàn fángzi.
text.english: Hello, Mrs. Wang. I'm Kexin Chen. This is my friend, Yamamoto Ryosuke. I come with him to view the house.

text.traditional: 你們好！這棟公寓一共有六層，我要出租的房子在四樓，我們一起上去看看吧！
text.simplified: 你们好！这栋公寓一共有六层，我要出租的房子在四楼，我们一起上去看看吧！
text.pinyin: Nǐmen hǎo! Zhè dòng gōngyù yígòng yǒu liù céng, wǒ yào chūzū de fángzi zài sì lóu, wǒmen yìqǐ shàngqù kànkan ba!
text.english: Hello! This is a six-story apartment building, and the apartment I'd like to rent out is on the fourth floor. Let's go up and have a look.

text.traditional: 好的。對了，請問有家具嗎？
text.simplified: 好的。对了，请问有家具吗？
text.pinyin: Hǎo de. Duìle, qǐngwèn yǒu jiājù ma?
text.english: OK. Oh! By the way, is there any furniture?

text.traditional: 有。臥室有床、書桌、椅子、沙發，還有一個大衣櫃，可以掛很多衣服，而且冰箱、洗衣機都是新的。
text.simplified: 有。卧室有床、书桌、椅子、沙发，还有一个大衣柜，可以挂很多衣服，而且冰箱、洗衣机都是新的。
text.pinyin: Yǒu. Wòshì yǒu chuáng, shūzhuō, yǐzi, shāfā, háiyǒu yíge dà yīguì, kěyǐ guà hěn duō yīfu, érqiě bīngxiāng, xǐyījī dōu shì xīn de.
text.english: Yes, there are a bed, a desk, a chair and a sofa in the bedroom. There's also a big closet where you can hang up many clothes. Also, both the refrigerator and the washing machine are new.

text.traditional: （三人到了四樓）
text.simplified: （三人到了四楼）
text.pinyin: (Sān rén dào le sì lóu)
text.english: (The three reach the fourth floor)

text.traditional: 請進！我給你們介紹介紹。這是客廳，右邊是廚房，臥室和浴室在那邊。
text.simplified: 请进！我给你们介绍介绍。这是客厅，右边是厨房，卧室和浴室在那边。
text.pinyin: Qǐng jìn! Wǒ gěi nǐmen jièshào jièshào. Zhè shì kètīng, yòubiān shì chúfáng, wòshì hé yùshì zài nàbiān.
text.english: Come in, please. Let me show you around. This is the living room. The kitchen is on the right. The bedroom and the bathroom are there.

text.traditional: 房間看起來很好！請問附近有超級市場嗎？
text.simplified: 房间看起来很好！请问附近有超级市场吗？
text.pinyin: Fángjiān kànqǐlái hěn hǎo! Qǐngwèn fùjìn yǒu chāojíshìchǎng ma?
text.english: The room looks nice! Is there any supermarket nearby?

text.traditional: 有啊！從這裡出去，走五分鐘就有超市和便利商店了。
text.simplified: 有啊！从这里出去，走五分钟就有超市和便利商店了。
text.pinyin: Yǒu a! Cóng zhèlǐ chūqù, zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng jiù yǒu chāoshì hé biànlì shāngdiàn le.
text.english: Yes, there is. Go out from here, the supermarket and convenience store are just a five-minute walk away.

text.traditional: 這裡有網路嗎？
text.simplified: 这里有网路吗？
text.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu wǎnglù ma?
text.english: Is the Internet access available here?

text.traditional: 沒有，我可以替你裝網路，可是每個月的費用要自己付。
text.simplified: 没有，我可以替你装网路，可是每个月的费用要自己付。
text.pinyin: Méiyǒu, wǒ kěyǐ tì nǐ zhuāng wǎnglù, kěshì měi ge yuè de fèiyòng yào zìjǐ fù.
text.english: No. I can set up the Internet connection for you, but you have to pay the monthly fee yourself.

text.traditional: 聽起來不錯。請問房租一個月多少錢？
text.simplified: 听起来不错。请问房租一个月多少钱？
text.pinyin: Tīngqǐlái búcuò. Qǐngwèn fángzū yíge yuè duōshǎo qián?
text.english: Sounds pretty good. How much is the rent each month?

text.traditional: 一個月一萬五千塊，不包括水費、電費，還要兩個月的押金。
text.simplified: 一个月一万五千块，不包括水费、电费，还要两个月的押金。
text.pinyin: Yíge yuè yíwànwǔqiān kuài, bù bāokuò shuǐfèi, diànfèi, háiyào liǎng ge yuè de yājīn.
text.english: It's $15,000 a month, water and electricity not included. Two-month rental deposit is also needed.

text.traditional: 好，我先跟我朋友討論一下，請您等一會兒。
text.simplified: 好，我先跟我朋友讨论一下，请您等一会儿。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ xiān gēn wǒ péngyǒu tǎolùn yíxià, qǐng nín děng yìhuǐr.
text.english: OK. I'd like to discuss with my friend first. Please wait a moment.

text.traditional: 你覺得這裡怎麼樣？
text.simplified: 你觉得这里怎么样？
text.pinyin: Nǐ juéde zhèlǐ zěnmeyàng?
text.english: What do you think of this place?

text.traditional: 這邊的環境不錯，可是付了房租以後，我的獎學金就只剩一萬塊了。
text.simplified: 这边的环境不错，可是付了房租以后，我的奖学金就只剩一万块了。
text.pinyin: Zhèbiān de huánjìng búcuò, kěshì fù le fángzū yǐhòu, wǒ de jiǎngxuéjīn jiù zhǐ shèng yíwàn kuài le.
text.english: The environment here is not bad, but after I pay the rent, I'll only have $10,000 of my scholarship left.

text.traditional: 這樣的房子都不便宜。你問問王太太，房租能不能便宜一點兒。
text.simplified: 这样的房子都不便宜。你问问王太太，房租能不能便宜一点儿。
text.pinyin: Zhèyàng de fángzi dōu bù piányí. Nǐ wèn wèn Wáng tàitai, fángzū néng bùnéng piányí yìdiǎnr.
text.english: All the houses of this kind are not cheap. Ask Mrs. Wang if she can lower the rent.

text.traditional: 王太太，這個公寓我很滿意，可是房租有一點兒貴，可以便宜一點兒嗎？
text.simplified: 王太太，这个公寓我很满意，可是房租有一点儿贵，可以便宜一点儿吗？
text.pinyin: Wáng tàitai, zhège gōngyù wǒ hěn mǎnyì, kěshì fángzū yǒuyìdiǎnr guì, kěyǐ piányí yìdiǎnr ma?
text.english: Mrs. Wang, I'm quite satisfied with this apartment, but the rent is a little bit expensive. Can it be a little cheaper?

text.traditional: 我想想……你是留學生吧？我兒子也去法國留學了，我知道外國人找房子不太容易。
text.simplified: 我想想……你是留学生吧？我儿子也去法国留学了，我知道外国人找房子不太容易。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiǎng… nǐ shì liúxuéshēng ba? Wǒ érzi yě qù Fǎguó liúxué le, wǒ zhīdào wàiguórén zhǎo fángzi bú tài róngyì.
text.english: Let me think about it... You're an international student, aren't you? My son has also been studying in France, so I know it's not easy for a foreigner to find a house.

text.traditional: 對啊！我看了好幾個地方，有的環境很好，可是房租太貴；有些房東一看我是外國人，就不願意租給我了。
text.simplified: 对啊！我看了好几个地方，有的环境很好，可是房租太贵；有些房东一看我是外国人，就不愿意租给我了。
text.pinyin: Duì a! Wǒ kàn le hǎojǐ ge dìfāng, yǒude huánjìng hěn hǎo, kěshì fángzū tài guì; yǒuxiē fángdōng yí kàn wǒ shì wàiguórén, jiù bú yuànyì zū gěi wǒ le.
text.english: That's right! I've visited several places. Some of them, the environment is not bad, but the rent is too expensive. Some landlords were unwilling to rent out to me on seeing I'm a foreigner.

text.traditional: 好吧！你那麼喜歡，那就一個月一萬兩千塊。
text.simplified: 好吧！你那么喜欢，那就一个月一万两千块。
text.pinyin: Hǎo ba! Nǐ nàme xǐhuān, nà jiù yíge yuè yíwànliǎngqiān kuài.
text.english: Alright! Now that you like this apartment so much, I'll just charge you $12,000 each month.

text.traditional: 太好了！謝謝您，我決定租半年。下個星期一可以簽約嗎？
text.simplified: 太好了！谢谢您，我决定租半年。下个星期一可以签约吗？
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Xièxie nín, wǒ juédìng zū bàn nián. Xià ge xīngqíyī kěyǐ qiānyuē ma?
text.english: That's great! Thank you. I decide to rent it for half a year. May I sign the lease next Monday?

text.traditional: 可以，你過來簽約的時候請帶護照、房租和兩個月的押金。簽約以後會給你鑰匙，你就可以搬進來了。
text.simplified: 可以，你过来签约的时候请带护照、房租和两个月的押金。签约以后会给你钥匙，你就可以搬进来了。
text.pinyin: Kěyǐ, nǐ guòlái qiānyuē de shíhòu qǐng dài hùzhào, fángzū hé liǎng ge yuè de yājīn. Qiānyuē yǐhòu huì gěi nǐ yàoshi, nǐ jiù kěyǐ bān jìnlái le.
text.english: Yes. When you come to sign the lease, please bring your passport, rent and a two-month deposit. After the lease is signed, I'll give you the keys and you can move in.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Rent a House
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Directional verb + 來 / 去 (1 of 4)
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say whether movement comes toward you or goes away: come up, go down, come in, go out.
grammarPages.explanation: A directional compound describes the direction of the action. The structures include: (1) directional verb + 來/去, (2) motion verb + directional verb + 來/去, (3) motion verb + directional verb + location + 來/去, (4) combined with 把 construction to indicate the Subject moves the Object to another location: S + 把 + O + motion verb + directional verb + (location) + 來/去.
grammarPages.pattern: Directional verb + 來 / 去

text.traditional: 我的房間在二樓，請上來。
text.simplified: 我的房间在二楼，请上来。
text.pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān zài èr lóu, qǐng shàng lái.
text.english: My room is on the second floor. Please come up.

text.traditional: 爸爸有事找你，你趕快過去。
text.simplified: 爸爸有事找你，你赶快过去。
text.pinyin: Bàba yǒu shì zhǎo nǐ, nǐ gǎnkuài guòqù.
text.english: Dad is looking for you. Hurry over.

text.traditional: 他出去一會兒，五分鐘以後就回來。
text.simplified: 他出去一会儿，五分钟以后就回来。
text.pinyin: Tā chūqù yìhuǐr, wǔ fēnzhōng yǐhòu jiù huí lái.
text.english: He went out for a while; he will be back in five minutes.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: A directional compound describes the direction of the action. result.english: Tomorrow is Mom's birthday; we're going to buy a cake to celebrate for her.

summary: Repeat a two-syllable verb as XYXY to say you do the action briefly and casually.
Don't add 一下 or 一點 to it. XYXY already means a short time.
Don't put 一 in the middle: say 打掃打掃, not 打掃一打掃.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Rent a House
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Judgemental 起來: how something seems
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use V起來 to say how something looks, sounds or feels.
grammarPages.explanation: The pattern is used to make comments on someone or something. The verb placed before “起來” is often a monosyllabic sensory verb or action verb, such as “看 (look)”, “聽 (sound)”, 吃 (taste), “喝 (drink)”, “穿 (wear)”, etc. “起來” is followed by comments; thus, the structure is “V 起來 (+Adv) +Vs”.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + V起來 (+ Adv) + Adjective

text.traditional: A：王小姐看起來很害羞。B：是啊！她不敢跟不熟的男生說話。
text.simplified: A：王小姐看起来很害羞。B：是啊！她不敢跟不熟的男生说话。
text.pinyin: A: Wáng xiǎojiě kànqǐlái hěn hàixiū. B: Shì a! Tā bù gǎn gēn bù shóu de nánshēng shuōhuà.
text.english: A: Miss Wang looks shy. B: Yes! She doesn't dare talk to boys she doesn't know well.

text.traditional: A：明天放假，我們去動物園吧。B：聽起來不錯，我們幾點去呢？
text.simplified: A：明天放假，我们去动物园吧。B：听起来不错，我们几点去呢？
text.pinyin: A: Míngtiān fàngjià, wǒmen qù dòngwùyuán ba. B: Tīngqǐlái búcuò, wǒmen jǐdiǎn qù ne?
text.english: A: We're off tomorrow. Let's go to the zoo. B: That sounds good. What time shall we go?

text.traditional: A：這件裙子是今年最流行的。B：看起來不錯，你穿起來應該很好看。
text.simplified: A：这件裙子是今年最流行的。B：看起来不错，你穿起来应该很好看。
text.pinyin: A: Zhè jiàn qúnzi shì jīnnián zuì liúxíng de. B: Kànqǐlái búcuò, nǐ chuān qǐlái yīnggāi hěn hǎokàn.
text.english: A: This skirt is the most popular style this year. B: It looks nice. It should look good on you.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The pattern is used to make comments on someone or something. The verb placed before “起來” is often a monosyllabic sensory verb or action verb, such as “看 (look)”, “聽 (sound)”, 吃 (taste), “喝 (drink)”, “穿 (wear)”, etc. “起來” is followed by comments; thus, the structure is “V 起來 (+Adv) +Vs”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The pattern is used to make comments on someone or something. The verb placed before “起來” is often a monosyllabic sensory verb or action verb, such as “看 (look)”, “聽 (sound)”, 吃 (taste), “喝 (drink)”, “穿 (wear)”, etc. “起來” is followed by comments; thus, the structure is “V 起來 (+Adv) +Vs”.

practice.title: Complete the dialogues with the given words.

segments.traditional: 媽媽今天做的雞湯看起來很好喝。
segments.simplified: 妈妈今天做的鸡汤看起来很好喝。

repairs.note: The older brother has already said how it looks. After 可是 comes how it tastes: 喝起來.
The younger brother says 可是, so his view goes the other way: 不好喝.
喝出來 is telling what something is by tasting. Giving your opinion of the taste is 喝起來.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 起來, then the opinion: 喝起來不好喝.

result.traditional: 可是喝起來不好喝。
result.simplified: 可是喝起来不好喝。
result.pinyin: Kěshì hēqǐlái bù hǎohē.
result.english: But it doesn't taste good.

segments.traditional: 離這裡最近的捷運站，走路要二十分鐘。
segments.simplified: 离这里最近的捷运站，走路要二十分钟。

repairs.note: B is not talking about living there. B is reacting to what A said: 聽起來.
Twenty minutes on foot is not close.
聽出來 is recognizing something by listening. Giving your impression of what you hear is 聽起來.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 起來, then the opinion: 聽起來有點兒遠.

result.traditional: 聽起來有點兒遠。
result.simplified: 听起来有点儿远。
result.pinyin: Tīngqǐlái yǒudiǎnr yuǎn.
result.english: That sounds a bit far.

segments.traditional: 我覺得這個房子不錯，交通也很方便。
segments.simplified: 我觉得这个房子不错，交通也很方便。

repairs.note: The wife says 可是 and points to their four children, so her view is that it is too small.
Giving an opinion of how something is to live in is 住起來.
住下來 is settling down somewhere. Giving an opinion of how it is to live in is 住起來.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 起來, then the opinion: 住起來太小了.

result.traditional: 可是我們有四個孩子，住起來太小了。
result.simplified: 可是我们有四个孩子，住起来太小了。
result.pinyin: Kěshì wǒmen yǒu sì ge háizi, zhùqǐlái tài xiǎo le.
result.english: But we have four children; it would be too small to live in.

summary: Verb plus 起來 gives your feeling or opinion about a person or thing.
The verb is often one syllable, such as 看, 聽, 吃, 喝 or 穿.
Put the comment last, after 起來: 看起來不錯.
For how clothes look on you, use 穿起來.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Rent a House
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 替: for or on behalf of someone
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that you do something for someone else with 替.
grammarPages.explanation: “替” is used in the situation when a person cannot do something for some reason and finds someone else to do it for him.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 替 + Person + Verb Phrase

text.traditional: 你可以替我裝網路嗎？費用我自己付。
text.simplified: 你可以替我装网路吗？费用我自己付。
text.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ tì wǒ zhuāng wǎnglù ma? Fèiyòng wǒ zìjǐ fù.
text.english: Can you set up the internet for me? I'll pay the fee myself.

text.traditional: 昨天王老師不舒服，所以林老師替他上課。
text.simplified: 昨天王老师不舒服，所以林老师替他上课。
text.pinyin: Zuótiān Wáng lǎoshī bù shūfu, suǒyǐ Lín lǎoshī tì tā shàngkè.
text.english: Teacher Wang didn't feel well yesterday, so Teacher Lin taught the class for him.

text.traditional: 孩子應該自己打掃房間，父母不要常常替他們做。
text.simplified: 孩子应该自己打扫房间，父母不要常常替他们做。
text.pinyin: Háizi yīnggāi zìjǐ dǎsǎo fángjiān, fùmǔ búyào chángcháng tì tāmen zuò.
text.english: Children should clean their rooms themselves. Parents should not often do it for them.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “替” is used in the situation when a person cannot do something for some reason and finds someone else to do it for him.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “替” is used in the situation when a person cannot do something for some reason and finds someone else to do it for him.

repairs.note: 跟 means "with". Doing something in someone's place is 替.
對 marks whom something is aimed at. Doing something in someone's place is 替.

items.fallbackRepair: A has no wallet, so B pays in A's place: 我替你付.

result.traditional: 沒關係，我替你付。
result.simplified: 没关系，我替你付。
result.pinyin: Méiguānxi, wǒ tì nǐ fù.
result.english: It's all right, I'll pay for you.

segments.traditional: 明天我有事不能去上班，你可以幫我嗎？
segments.simplified: 明天我有事不能去上班，你可以帮我吗？

segments.traditional: 我沒做過你的工作，沒辦法
segments.simplified: 我没做过你的工作，没办法

repairs.note: A is the one who cannot go. B would be working in A's place: 替你.
A will not be there, so B cannot work "with" A. Working in A's place is 替你.
對 marks whom something is aimed at. Doing something in someone's place is 替.

items.fallbackRepair: 替, then the person, then the action: 替你上班.

result.traditional: 我沒做過你的工作，沒辦法替你上班。
result.simplified: 我没做过你的工作，没办法替你上班。
result.pinyin: Wǒ méi zuòguo nǐ de gōngzuò, méibànfǎ tì nǐ shàngbān.
result.english: I've never done your job, so I can't go to work in your place.

segments.traditional: 我不知道怎麼寫這個作業，你可以替我寫嗎？
segments.simplified: 我不知道怎么写这个作业，你可以替我写吗？

repairs.note: 跟 means "with". Doing the homework in his place is 替.
對 marks whom something is aimed at. Doing something in someone's place is 替.

items.fallbackRepair: The older brother would be the one writing, in his younger brother's place: 我替你寫作業.

result.traditional: 如果媽媽知道我替你寫作業，她會打我們！
result.simplified: 如果妈妈知道我替你写作业，她会打我们！
result.pinyin: Rúguǒ māma zhīdào wǒ tì nǐ xiě zuòyè, tā huì dǎ wǒmen!
result.english: If Mom finds out I did your homework for you, she'll spank us both!

summary: 替 means doing something in place of someone who can't do it themselves.
Put 替 and the person before the verb: 替我裝網路.
Always say what is done. You can't stop after 替他.

items.title: Grammar 8–9 · Renting a House Is Not Easy

dialogue.title: 短文 · 租房子不容易

text.traditional: 山本良介來台灣以後，一直住在學校的宿舍，可是他下個學期不想住了，因為室友很晚才睡覺，總是在半夜開著燈打電腦，聲音很吵。除了生活習慣很不一樣，良介的室友還常常把房間弄得很髒，所以他決定到學校外面去租房子。
text.simplified: 山本良介来台湾以后，一直住在学校的宿舍，可是他下个学期不想住了，因为室友很晚才睡觉，总是在半夜开着灯打电脑，声音很吵。除了生活习惯很不一样，良介的室友还常常把房间弄得很脏，所以他决定到学校外面去租房子。
text.pinyin: Shānběn Liángjiè lái Táiwān yǐhòu, yìzhí zhù zài xuéxiào de sùshè, kěshì tā xià ge xuéqí bù xiǎng zhù le, yīnwèi shìyǒu hěn wǎn cái shuìjiào, zǒngshì zài bànyè kāi zhe dēng dǎ diànnǎo, shēngyīn hěn chǎo. Chúle shēnghuó xíguàn hěn bù yíyàng, Liángjiè de shìyǒu hái chángcháng bǎ fángjiān nòng de hěn zāng, suǒyǐ tā juédìng dào xuéxiào wàimiàn qù zū fángzi.
text.english: After Yamamoto Ryosuke came to Taiwan, he has always been living in the school dormitory, but he doesn't want to live there next semester. That was because his roommate slept late, always used the computer with the light on at midnight, and made a lot of noise. In addition to different living habits, Ryosuke's roommate often made their room dirty, so he decided to rent a house off-campus.

text.traditional: 良介本來覺得找房子不難，沒想到不太順利。他上租屋網站找了很多資料，可是看了好幾個地方都不滿意。有的房東一看他是外國人，就不太願意租給他。陳可欣知道他的問題以後，就決定陪他去找房子、看房子。
text.simplified: 良介本来觉得找房子不难，没想到不太顺利。他上租屋网站找了很多资料，可是看了好几个地方都不满意。有的房东一看他是外国人，就不太愿意租给他。陈可欣知道他的问题以后，就决定陪他去找房子、看房子。
text.pinyin: Liángjiè běnlái juéde zhǎo fángzi bù nán, méixiǎngdào bú tài shùnlì. Tā shàng zūwū wǎngzhàn zhǎo le hěn duō zīliào, kěshì kàn le hǎojǐ ge dìfāng dōu bù mǎnyì. Yǒude fángdōng yí kàn tā shì wàiguórén, jiù bú tài yuànyì zū gěi tā. Chén Kěxīn zhīdào tā de wèntí yǐhòu, jiù juédìng péi tā qù zhǎo fángzi, kàn fángzi.
text.english: Ryosuke supposed that finding a house was not difficult. He never thought that it would not go smoothly. He searched for a lot of information on house rental websites. However, after he viewed several places, he still was not satisfied. Some landlords were unwilling to rent out their houses to him just because he was a foreigner. After knowing his problem, Chen Kexin decided to accompany him to find and view houses.

text.traditional: 良介聽說王太太的公寓要出租，就找可欣一起去看看。那個公寓附近的環境不錯，離學校也不太遠。雖然良介很想租，但是付了房租以後，獎學金就只剩下一萬塊錢了。他問王太太，房租可不可以便宜一點兒。因為王太太的兒子在法國留學，她知道一個人在國外生活不容易。她想了想，決定只收良介一萬兩千元的房租，良介很高興可以搬家了。
text.simplified: 良介听说王太太的公寓要出租，就找可欣一起去看看。那个公寓附近的环境不错，离学校也不太远。虽然良介很想租，但是付了房租以后，奖学金就只剩下一万块钱了。他问王太太，房租可不可以便宜一点儿。因为王太太的儿子在法国留学，她知道一个人在国外生活不容易。她想了想，决定只收良介一万两千元的房租，良介很高兴可以搬家了。
text.pinyin: Liángjiè tīngshuō Wáng tàitai de gōngyù yào chūzū, jiù zhǎo Kěxīn yìqǐ qù kànkan. Nàge gōngyù fùjìn de huánjìng búcuò, lí xuéxiào yě bú tài yuǎn. Suīrán Liángjiè hěn xiǎng zū, dànshì fù le fángzū yǐhòu, jiǎngxuéjīn jiù zhǐ shèngxià yíwàn kuài qián le. Tā wèn Wáng tàitai, fángzū kě bù kěyǐ piányí yìdiǎnr. Yīnwèi Wáng tàitai de érzi zài Fǎguó liúxué, tā zhīdào yígerén zài guówài shēnghuó bù róngyì. Tā xiǎng le xiǎng, juédìng zhǐ shōu Liángjiè yíwànliǎngqiān yuán de fángzū, Liángjiè hěn gāoxìng kěyǐ bānjiā le.
text.english: As soon as Ryosuke heard Mrs. Wang's apartment was for rent, he went with Kexin to have a look. The surroundings of the apartment were not bad and it was not too far away from the school. Although Ryosuke would like to rent it, he would have only $10,000 of his scholarship left after paying the rent. He asked Mrs. Wang whether the rent could be cheaper. Because Mrs. Wang's son has been studying in France, she knew that it was not easy to live abroad alone. After thinking it over, she decided to charge Ryosuke a rent of only $12,000. Ryosuke was happy that he could move.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Rent a House
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 除了……還…… to add a second, more important point.
grammarPages.explanation: The pattern indicates there are different situations coming after “除了” and “還”, with the latter one being even more important than the former. “除了” can be followed by nouns, verbs, intransitive state verbs (Vs) or phrases. If the Subjects of the two clauses are different, the second Subject should be placed before “還”, as in example 2.
grammarPages.pattern: 除了 + Clause 1，Subject + 還 + Clause 2

text.traditional: 我除了喜歡吃蘋果，還喜歡吃香蕉。
text.simplified: 我除了喜欢吃苹果，还喜欢吃香蕉。
text.pinyin: Wǒ chúle xǐhuān chī píngguǒ, hái xǐhuān chī xiāngjiāo.
text.english: Besides liking to eat apples, I also like to eat bananas.

text.traditional: 很多人喜歡來這裡旅行，除了風景很好，交通還很方便。
text.simplified: 很多人喜欢来这里旅行，除了风景很好，交通还很方便。
text.pinyin: Hěn duō rén xǐhuān lái zhèlǐ lǚxíng, chúle fēngjǐng hěn hǎo, jiāotōng hái hěn fāngbiàn.
text.english: Many people like to travel here. Besides the nice scenery, the transportation is also convenient.

text.traditional: A：白小姐生日的時候，男朋友送給她一個很貴的皮包。B：除了皮包，還送給她一輛車呢！
text.simplified: A：白小姐生日的时候，男朋友送给她一个很贵的皮包。B：除了皮包，还送给她一辆车呢！
text.pinyin: A: Bái xiǎojiě shēngrì de shíhòu, nánpéngyǒu sòng gěi tā yíge hěn guì de píbāo. B: Chúle píbāo, hái sòng gěi tā yí liàng chē ne!
text.english: A: On Miss Bai's birthday, her boyfriend gave her a very expensive purse. B: Besides the purse, he also gave her a car!

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The pattern indicates there are different situations coming after “除了” and “還”, with the latter one being even more important than the former. “除了” can be followed by nouns, verbs, intransitive state verbs (Vs) or phrases. If the Subjects of the two clauses are different, the second Subject should be placed before “還”, as in example 2.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The pattern indicates there are different situations coming after “除了” and “還”, with the latter one being even more important than the former. “除了” can be followed by nouns, verbs, intransitive state verbs (Vs) or phrases. If the Subjects of the two clauses are different, the second Subject should be placed before “還”, as in example 2.

segments.traditional: 學校外面有沒有便利商店？
segments.simplified: 学校外面有没有便利商店？

repairs.note: 都 does not add anything new. After 除了, one more thing is added with 還.
B is not giving a reason. B adds one more shop: 除了…，還….
The bookstore is not a result of the convenience store. It is one more shop: 還有.

items.fallbackRepair: 除了 before the first thing, then 還 + 有 before the one added.

result.traditional: 有，除了便利商店，還有銀行。
result.simplified: 有，除了便利商店，还有银行。
result.pinyin: Yǒu, chúle biànlì shāngdiàn, hái yǒu yínháng.
result.english: Yes. Besides a convenience store, there is also a bank.

segments.traditional: 那棟公寓看起來不錯，你為什麼不租？
segments.simplified: 那栋公寓看起来不错，你为什么不租？

segments.traditional: ，還要自己裝網路，所以我不要租。
segments.simplified: ，还要自己装网路，所以我不要租。

repairs.note: B is listing reasons not to rent it. Cheap rent is not one of them.
所以 starts a result, and it comes later in this sentence. The first of two drawbacks opens with 除了.
如果 sets up an "if". B is listing two real drawbacks: 除了…，還….

items.fallbackRepair: 除了 before the first drawback; 還 adds the second.

result.traditional: 除了房租很貴，還要自己裝網路，所以我不要租。
result.simplified: 除了房租很贵，还要自己装网路，所以我不要租。
result.pinyin: Chúle fángzū hěn guì, hái yào zìjǐ zhuāng wǎnglù, suǒyǐ wǒ búyào zū.
result.english: Besides the rent being expensive, I would also have to install the internet myself, so I don't want to rent it.

segments.traditional: 你為什麼要搬出去？宿舍不好嗎？
segments.simplified: 你为什么要搬出去？宿舍不好吗？

repairs.note: B is giving reasons for moving out. A polite roommate is not one of them.
都 does not add anything new. After 除了, a second problem is added with 還.

items.fallbackRepair: 除了 before the first problem, then 還 before the second.

result.traditional: 我跟室友除了生活習慣不一樣，他還很吵，所以我要搬家。
result.simplified: 我跟室友除了生活习惯不一样，他还很吵，所以我要搬家。
result.pinyin: Wǒ gēn shìyǒu chúle shēnghuó xíguàn bù yíyàng, tā hái hěn chǎo, suǒyǐ wǒ yào bānjiā.
result.english: Besides my roommate and me having different living habits, he is also very noisy, so I want to move out.

summary: Say one thing first, then add another, more important thing.
After 除了 you can use a noun, a verb, or a short sentence.
Put 還 before the second verb or adjective.
If the two parts have different subjects, the second subject goes before 還.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: I Want to Rent a House
grammarPages.titleEnglish: The 把 construction with V得 + comment
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 把 with V得 to say how an action leaves something.
grammarPages.explanation: In this pattern, “把” is followed by the Object that receives the action of a verb, while “V得” is followed by the outcome after the action.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + 得 + Adv + Adjective

text.traditional: 弟弟把足球踢得很遠。
text.simplified: 弟弟把足球踢得很远。
text.pinyin: Dìdi bǎ zúqiú tī de hěn yuǎn.
text.english: My younger brother kicked the soccer ball very far.

text.traditional: 他把那隻兔子畫得很可愛。
text.simplified: 他把那只兔子画得很可爱。
text.pinyin: Tā bǎ nà zhī tùzi huà de hěn kě'ài.
text.english: He drew that rabbit so that it looks very cute.

text.traditional: 請你不要把這個問題弄得更麻煩。
text.simplified: 请你不要把这个问题弄得更麻烦。
text.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ búyào bǎ zhège wèntí nòng de gèng máfán.
text.english: Please don't make this problem even more troublesome.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In this pattern, “把” is followed by the Object that receives the action of a verb, while “V得” is followed by the outcome after the action.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In this pattern, “把” is followed by the Object that receives the action of a verb, while “V得” is followed by the outcome after the action.

repairs.note: Between a verb and how it turned out, the particle is 得, not 的: 打掃得很乾淨.

items.fallbackRepair: 把, then the thing, then the verb, then 得, then how it turned out.

result.traditional: 妹妹昨天把臥室打掃得很乾淨。
result.simplified: 妹妹昨天把卧室打扫得很干净。
result.pinyin: Mèimei zuótiān bǎ wòshì dǎsǎo de hěn gānjìng.
result.english: My younger sister got the bedroom really clean yesterday.

repairs.note: Between a verb and how it turned out, the particle is 得, not 的: 寫得那麼難看.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then the verb, then 得, then how it turned out.

result.traditional: 你為什麼把自己的名字寫得那麼難看？
result.simplified: 你为什么把自己的名字写得那么难看？
result.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme bǎ zìjǐ de míngzi xiě de nàme nánkàn?
result.english: Why did you write your own name so badly?

repairs.note: 的 links 新家 to 客廳; 得 links the verb to how it turned out: 新家的客廳弄得很漂亮.
How it turned out is linked to the verb with 得, not 了.

items.fallbackRepair: 把 before the thing, then the verb, then 得, then how it turned out.

result.traditional: 林小姐把新家的客廳弄得很漂亮。
result.simplified: 林小姐把新家的客厅弄得很漂亮。
result.pinyin: Lín xiǎojiě bǎ xīn jiā de kètīng nòng de hěn piàoliàng.
result.english: Miss Lin has made the living room of her new home very pretty.

summary: Use 把 and an action verb plus 得 to say how far or how well the action turned out.
The thing being handled goes right after 把.
Put 得 right after the verb, then the degree or result: 把足球踢得很遠.

items.title: Grammar 1–3 · It’s Fun to Go to the Night Market

text.traditional: （可欣約美心一起去逛夜市）
text.simplified: （可欣约美心一起去逛夜市）
text.pinyin: (Kěxīn yuē Měixīn yìqǐ qù guàng yèshì)
text.english: (Kexin invites Meixin to go to the night market together.)

text.traditional: 妳平常不愛逛夜市，今天怎麼忽然想去啊？
text.simplified: 你平常不爱逛夜市，今天怎么忽然想去啊？
text.pinyin: Nǐ píngcháng bú ài guàng yèshì, jīntiān zěnme hūrán xiǎng qù a?
text.english: You don't usually like to go to night markets. Why do you suddenly want to go today?

text.traditional: 因為良介說他跟朋友都想到夜市看看，請我給他們介紹介紹台灣的小吃。
text.simplified: 因为良介说他跟朋友都想到夜市看看，请我给他们介绍介绍台湾的小吃。
text.pinyin: Yīnwèi Liángjiè shuō tā gēn péngyǒu dōu xiǎngdào yèshì kànkan, qǐng wǒ gěi tāmen jièshào jièshào Táiwān de xiǎochī.
text.english: Because Ryosuke said that he and his friend both wanted to look around the night market, and asked me to introduce some Taiwanese snacks to them.

text.traditional: 你們在哪裡見面呢？
text.simplified: 你们在哪里见面呢？
text.pinyin: Nǐmen zài nǎlǐ jiànmiàn ne?
text.english: Where will you meet?

text.traditional: 在捷運站二號出口。他們應該快到了。
text.simplified: 在捷运站二号出口。他们应该快到了。
text.pinyin: Zài jiéyùn zhàn èr hào chūkǒu. Tāmen yīnggāi kuài dào le.
text.english: At Exit 2 of the MRT station. They should be arriving soon.

text.traditional: （可欣跟美心到了捷運站二號出口）
text.simplified: （可欣跟美心到了捷运站二号出口）
text.pinyin: (Kěxīn gēn Měixīn dào le jiéyùn zhàn èr hào chūkǒu)
text.english: (Kexin and Meixin arrive at Exit 2 of the MRT station.)

text.traditional: 不好意思，妳們等了很久了嗎？
text.simplified: 不好意思，你们等了很久了吗？
text.pinyin: Bùhǎoyìsi, nǐmen děng le hěn jiǔ le ma?
text.english: Sorry! Have you been waiting for a long time?

text.traditional: 我們也剛到。良介，給我們介紹一下你的朋友吧！
text.simplified: 我们也刚到。良介，给我们介绍一下你的朋友吧！
text.pinyin: Wǒmen yě gāng dào. Liángjiè, gěi wǒmen jièshào yíxià nǐ de péngyǒu ba!
text.english: We just arrived, too. Ryosuke, introduce your friend to us!

text.traditional: 他是我的好朋友龍介，這幾天到台灣來旅行。
text.simplified: 他是我的好朋友龙介，这几天到台湾来旅行。
text.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyǒu Lóngjiè, zhè jǐ tiān dào Táiwān lái lǚxíng.
text.english: He is my good friend Ryusuke. He is traveling in Taiwan these days.

text.traditional: 妳們好，我叫九十九龍介。
text.simplified: 你们好，我叫九十九龙介。
text.pinyin: Nǐmen hǎo, wǒ jiào Jiǔshíjiǔ Lóngjiè.
text.english: Hello! I'm Ryusuke Tsukumo.

text.traditional: 你好，我是陳可欣，良介的大學同學。她是我室友王美心。
text.simplified: 你好，我是陈可欣，良介的大学同学。她是我室友王美心。
text.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ shì Chén Kěxīn, Liángjiè de dàxué tóngxué. Tā shì wǒ shìyǒu Wáng Měixīn.
text.english: Hello! I'm Kexin Chen, Ryosuke's university classmate. She is my roommate Meixin Wang.

text.traditional: 很高興認識你。你的姓真特別！
text.simplified: 很高兴认识你。你的姓真特别！
text.pinyin: Hěn gāoxìng rènshì nǐ. Nǐ de xìng zhēn tèbié!
text.english: Nice to meet you! Your surname is so special!

text.traditional: 是啊！姓九十九的日本人很少。我一直想來夜市逛逛，今天請妳們帶我去吃好吃的台灣小吃。
text.simplified: 是啊！姓九十九的日本人很少。我一直想来夜市逛逛，今天请你们带我去吃好吃的台湾小吃。
text.pinyin: Shì a! Xìng Jiǔshíjiǔ de Rìběnrén hěn shǎo. Wǒ yìzhí xiǎng lái yèshì guàngguang, jīntiān qǐng nǐmen dài wǒ qù chī hǎochī de Táiwān xiǎochī.
text.english: Yes! Few Japanese people have this surname. I have always wanted to walk around a night market. Please take me to eat delicious Taiwanese snacks today.

text.traditional: 沒問題，夜市就在前面。
text.simplified: 没问题，夜市就在前面。
text.pinyin: Méi wèntí, yèshì jiù zài qiánmiàn.
text.english: No problem. The night market is right ahead.

text.traditional: 我聽說台灣的夜市很有意思，有各種小吃跟點心，買東西還可以殺價呢！
text.simplified: 我听说台湾的夜市很有意思，有各种小吃跟点心，买东西还可以杀价呢！
text.pinyin: Wǒ tīngshuō Táiwān de yèshì hěn yǒuyìsi, yǒu gè zhǒng xiǎochī gēn diǎnxīn, mǎi dōngxi hái kěyǐ shājià ne!
text.english: I heard that Taiwanese night markets are very interesting. They have all kinds of snacks and treats, and you can even bargain when you buy things!

text.traditional: 沒錯，有時候我在夜市買衣服也會殺價。對了！等一下你會看到一些招牌上有英文、日文，就是希望外國遊客也看得懂。
text.simplified: 没错，有时候我在夜市买衣服也会杀价。对了！等一下你会看到一些招牌上有英文、日文，就是希望外国游客也看得懂。
text.pinyin: Méicuò, yǒushíhòu wǒ zài yèshì mǎi yīfu yě huì shājià. Duìle! Děng yíxià nǐ huì kàndào yìxiē zhāopái shàng yǒu Yīngwén, Rìwén, jiùshì xīwàng wàiguó yóukè yě kàn de dǒng.
text.english: That's right. Sometimes I bargain when I buy clothes at the night market too. By the way! Later you'll see English and Japanese on some signboards; that's to help foreign tourists understand them.

text.traditional: 這裡有臭豆腐、炸雞排、蚵仔煎……，這些小吃都很好吃。當然，還有有名的珍珠奶茶。
text.simplified: 这里有臭豆腐、炸鸡排、蚵仔煎……，这些小吃都很好吃。当然，还有有名的珍珠奶茶。
text.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu chòu dòufǔ, zhá jī pái, ézǐjiān…, zhèxiē xiǎochī dōu hěn hǎochī. Dāngrán, háiyǒu yǒumíng de zhēnzhū nǎichá.
text.english: There is stinky tofu, fried chicken cutlet, oyster omelet... These snacks are all delicious. Of course, there is also the famous pearl milk tea.

text.traditional: 聽說這裡的珍珠奶茶喝起來又香又甜，可是我不習慣喝太甜的飲料。
text.simplified: 听说这里的珍珠奶茶喝起来又香又甜，可是我不习惯喝太甜的饮料。
text.pinyin: Tīngshuō zhèlǐ de zhēnzhū nǎichá hē qǐlái yòu xiāng yòu tián, kěshì wǒ bù xíguàn hē tài tián de yǐnliào.
text.english: I heard that the pearl milk tea here tastes fragrant and sweet, but I am not used to drinks that are too sweet.

text.traditional: 在台灣，你可以請他們少放一點兒糖，或是選無糖的、半糖的，也可以決定加多少冰塊。
text.simplified: 在台湾，你可以请他们少放一点儿糖，或是选无糖的、半糖的，也可以决定加多少冰块。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, nǐ kěyǐ qǐng tāmen shǎo fàng yìdiǎnr táng, huòshì xuǎn wú táng de, bàn táng de, yě kěyǐ juédìng jiā duōshǎo bīngkuài.
text.english: In Taiwan, you can ask them to put in less sugar, or choose sugar-free or half-sugar, and you can also decide how much ice to add.

text.traditional: 太好了！妳們還推薦我們吃什麼？
text.simplified: 太好了！你们还推荐我们吃什么？
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Nǐmen hái tuījiàn wǒmen chī shénme?
text.english: That's great! What else do you recommend we eat?

text.traditional: 要是你們想吃特別的，我就推薦你們吃臭豆腐，辣的更好吃。（美心買了一份臭豆腐）你們聞，這就是臭豆腐的味道，臭不臭？
text.simplified: 要是你们想吃特别的，我就推荐你们吃臭豆腐，辣的更好吃。（美心买了一份臭豆腐）你们闻，这就是臭豆腐的味道，臭不臭？
text.pinyin: Yàoshì nǐmen xiǎng chī tèbié de, wǒ jiù tuījiàn nǐmen chī chòu dòufǔ, là de gèng hǎochī. (Měixīn mǎi le yí fèn chòu dòufǔ) Nǐmen wén, zhè jiù shì chòu dòufǔ de wèidào, chòu bú chòu?
text.english: If you want to eat something special, I recommend stinky tofu. The spicy one is even more delicious. (Meixin buys a serving of stinky tofu.) Smell it! This is the smell of stinky tofu. Is it stinky?

text.traditional: （良介、龍介聞了一下）
text.simplified: （良介、龙介闻了一下）
text.pinyin: (Liángjiè, Lóngjiè wén le yíxià)
text.english: (Ryosuke and Ryusuke take a sniff.)

text.traditional: 這種味道我不討厭。其實我什麼小吃都想試試，特別是炸雞排，聽說又大又好吃。
text.simplified: 这种味道我不讨厌。其实我什么小吃都想试试，特别是炸鸡排，听说又大又好吃。
text.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng wèidào wǒ bù tǎoyàn. Qíshí wǒ shénme xiǎochī dōu xiǎng shì shì, tèbié shì zhá jī pái, tīngshuō yòu dà yòu hǎochī.
text.english: I don't dislike this smell. Actually, I want to try every snack, especially the fried chicken cutlet. I heard it's big and delicious.

text.traditional: 我不敢吃臭豆腐，可是很想吃雞排。
text.simplified: 我不敢吃臭豆腐，可是很想吃鸡排。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù gǎn chī chòu dòufǔ, kěshì hěn xiǎng chī jīpái.
text.english: I don't dare eat stinky tofu, but I really want to eat the chicken cutlet.

text.traditional: 好，那麼我們先去買雞排，我再帶你們去喝非常好喝的香蕉牛奶。
text.simplified: 好，那么我们先去买鸡排，我再带你们去喝非常好喝的香蕉牛奶。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, nàme wǒmen xiān qù mǎi jīpái, wǒ zài dài nǐmen qù hē fēicháng hǎohē de xiāngjiāo niúnǎi.
text.english: OK, then let's go buy the chicken cutlet first, and then I'll take you to drink some delicious banana milk.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: It’s Fun to Go to the Night Market
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Point at exactly where something or someone is.
grammarPages.explanation: In conversation, if something mentioned is within reach, “就” can be used to show emphasis and affirmation.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject / Thing + 就 + 在 / 是 + Place / Person

text.traditional: A：我忘了把筆放在哪裡了。B：我看看，你的筆就在桌上啊！
text.simplified: A：我忘了把笔放在哪里了。B：我看看，你的笔就在桌上啊！
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ wàngle bǎ bǐ fàng zài nǎlǐ le. B: Wǒ kànkan, nǐ de bǐ jiù zài zhuō shàng a!
text.english: A: I forgot where I put the pen. B: Let me see—your pen is right there on the desk!

text.traditional: A：喂，請問，陳可欣小姐在家嗎？B：我就是。
text.simplified: A：喂，请问，陈可欣小姐在家吗？B：我就是。
text.pinyin: A: Wéi, qǐngwèn, Chén Kěxīn xiǎojiě zài jiā ma? B: Wǒ jiùshì.
text.english: A: Hello, may I ask, is Ms. Chen Kexin at home? B: This is she.

text.traditional: A：我聽說他家在學校附近。B：是啊！他家就在學校旁邊，走路五分鐘就到了。
text.simplified: A：我听说他家在学校附近。B：是啊！他家就在学校旁边，走路五分钟就到了。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ tīngshuō tā jiā zài xuéxiào fùjìn. B: Shì a! Tā jiā jiù zài xuéxiào pángbiān, zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
text.english: A: I heard his home is near the school. B: Yes! His home is right next to the school; it is a five-minute walk.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In conversation, if something mentioned is within reach, “就” can be used to show emphasis and affirmation.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In conversation, if something mentioned is within reach, “就” can be used to show emphasis and affirmation.

practice.title: Complete the dialogues with the given phrases.

repairs.note: B points at one car right here. That takes 就, not 都.
在 says where something is. Saying which one it is takes 是: 就是那輛….
Nothing was said before for 也 to add to. Pointing at the one right here is 就.

items.fallbackRepair: 就 first, then 是, then which one: 就是那輛紅色的英國車.

result.traditional: 就是那輛紅色的英國車。
result.simplified: 就是那辆红色的英国车。
result.pinyin: Jiùshì nà liàng hóngsè de Yīngguó chē.
result.english: It's that red British car right there.

segments.traditional: 我忘了把鑰匙放在哪裡了。
segments.simplified: 我忘了把钥匙放在哪里了。

repairs.note: A asks where the keys are, and a place takes 在: 就在….
B points at one spot right here. That takes 就, not 都.
B is showing that the keys are right here, close by. That is 就.

items.fallbackRepair: 就 first, then 在, then the place: 就在那本中文書的旁邊.

result.traditional: 就在那本中文書的旁邊。
result.simplified: 就在那本中文书的旁边。
result.pinyin: Jiù zài nà běn Zhōngwén shū de pángbiān.
result.english: They are right beside that Chinese book.

segments.traditional: 聽說王先生的女朋友很漂亮，是哪一位？
segments.simplified: 听说王先生的女朋友很漂亮，是哪一位？

repairs.note: 在 says where something is. Saying which person she is takes 是: 就是那位….
Nothing was said before for 也 to add to. Pointing at the one right here is 就.
B points at one person. That takes 就, not 都.

items.fallbackRepair: 就 first, then 是, then which one: 就是那位長頭髮的小姐.

result.traditional: 就是那位長頭髮的小姐。
result.simplified: 就是那位长头发的小姐。
result.pinyin: Jiùshì nà wèi cháng tóufǎ de xiǎojiě.
result.english: She is that young lady with long hair right there.

summary: Use 就 before 在 or 是 to say it is right here, or exactly this one.
Don't use 才 for this. 才 means late, slow, or only that much.
When someone asks who is there or if you are home, answer 我就是, not 我就在.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: V到: success and ability with 到
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say whether an action reached its result, and whether you can do it at all.
grammarPages.explanation: Resultative Complements are used to express the result of an action or a behavior. The structure is “Verb + RC.” The resultative complement “到” indicates that the outcome of a verb is successfully achieved. Besides, the pattern “V得到/V不到” indicates the potential or capability of achieving something or not, while the patterns “V到了” and “沒V到” indicate whether the outcome of a verb was achieved or not at last. The verbs often used in this pattern include “看 (see)”, “聽 (hear)”, “拿 (take)”, “走 (walk)”, “買 (buy)”, “找 (find)”, “租 (rent)”, “做 (do)” and “想 (think)”.
grammarPages.pattern: Verb + 到 (result) / Verb + 得 / 不 + 到 (potential)

text.traditional: 李先生租到了不錯的公寓。
text.simplified: 李先生租到了不错的公寓。
text.pinyin: Lǐ xiānshēng zū dào le búcuò de gōngyù.
text.english: Mr. Li successfully rented a nice apartment.

text.traditional: 我沒想到那個外國人會說中文。
text.simplified: 我没想到那个外国人会说中文。
text.pinyin: Wǒ méixiǎngdào nàge wàiguórén huì shuō Zhōngwén.
text.english: I didn't expect that foreigner to speak Chinese.

text.traditional: 妹妹昨天在百貨公司逛了很久，買到了很多她喜歡的衣服。
text.simplified: 妹妹昨天在百货公司逛了很久，买到了很多她喜欢的衣服。
text.pinyin: Mèimei zuótiān zài bǎihuò gōngsī guàng le hěn jiǔ, mǎi dào le hěn duō tā xǐhuān de yīfu.
text.english: Yesterday my younger sister shopped at the department store for a long time and bought many clothes she likes.

text.traditional: 我找不到我的錢包，怎麼辦？
text.simplified: 我找不到我的钱包，怎么办？
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎo bú dào wǒ de qiánbāo, zěnmebàn?
text.english: I can't find my wallet. What should I do?

text.traditional: 在台灣，到處都吃得到小吃。
text.simplified: 在台湾，到处都吃得到小吃。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, dàochù dōu chī de dào xiǎochī.
text.english: In Taiwan, you can get snacks to eat everywhere.

text.traditional: 台北101離這裡有一點兒遠，你十五分鐘走得到走不到？
text.simplified: 台北101离这里有一点儿远，你十五分钟走得到走不到？
text.pinyin: Táiběi 101 lí zhèlǐ yǒuyìdiǎnr yuǎn, nǐ shíwǔ fēnzhōng zǒu de dào zǒu bú dào?

subsections.title: V到了 / 沒V到: the result was or was not reached
subsections.explanation: 「V到了」表示動作最後成功了；「沒V到」表示最後沒有成功。

subsections.title: V得到 / V不到: can or cannot reach the result
subsections.explanation: 「V得到」表示有能力或機會達到；「V不到」表示沒有能力或機會達到。

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: Resultative Complements are used to express the result of an action or a behavior. The structure is “Verb + RC.” The resultative complement “到” indicates that the outcome of a verb is successfully achieved. Besides, the pattern “V得到/V不到” indicates the potential or capability of achieving something or not, while the patterns “V到了” and “沒V到” indicate whether the outcome of a verb was achieved or not at last. The verbs often used in this pattern include “看 (see)”, “聽 (hear)”, “拿 (take)”, “走 (walk)”, “買 (buy)”, “找 (find)”, “租 (rent)”, “做 (do)” and “想 (think)”.

The structure is “Verb + RC.” The resultative complement “到” indicates that the outcome of a verb is successfully achieved. summary: 到 after a verb means the action reached its result.
V到了 and 沒V到 say whether the action worked in the end.

Put 不 between the verb and 到: 找不到, not 不到找.

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say whether someone understood, and whether they can understand.
grammarPages.explanation: When serving as a resultative complement, “懂” indicates that the subject understands something. Thus, “懂” often comes after verbs such as “聽 (listen)” and “看 (look, watch, see)”. Besides, the “V得懂/V不懂” pattern indicates whether the subject has the ability to understand something, while the “V懂了” and “沒V懂” patterns indicate whether the subject understood something or not after a certain action.

Besides, the “V得懂/V不懂” pattern indicates whether the subject has the ability to understand something, while the “V懂了” and “沒V懂” patterns indicate whether the subject understood something or not after a certain action.

items.title: Grammar 4–8 · The Night Market Culture in Taiwan

dialogue.title: 短文 · 台灣的夜市文化

text.traditional: 除了百貨公司，夜市也是台灣人常去的地方。那裡有各種好吃的小吃、好喝的飲料和好玩的遊戲。一般的夜市大概從晚上六點開始，到半夜才結束。很多台灣人喜歡去夜市吃喝玩樂，所以夜市總是很熱鬧，到了週末晚上更是擠得不得了。
text.simplified: 除了百货公司，夜市也是台湾人常去的地方。那里有各种好吃的小吃、好喝的饮料和好玩的游戏。一般的夜市大概从晚上六点开始，到半夜才结束。很多台湾人喜欢去夜市吃喝玩乐，所以夜市总是很热闹，到了周末晚上更是挤得不得了。
text.pinyin: Chúle bǎihuò gōngsī, yèshì yě shì Táiwān rén cháng qù de dìfāng. Nàlǐ yǒu gè zhǒng hǎochī de xiǎochī, hǎohē de yǐnliào hé hǎowán de yóuxì. Yìbān de yèshì dàgài cóng wǎnshàng liù diǎn kāishǐ, dào bànyè cái jiéshù. Hěn duō Táiwān rén xǐhuān qù yèshì chīhēwánlè, suǒyǐ yèshì zǒngshì hěn rènao, dào le zhōumò wǎnshàng gèng shì jǐ de bùdéliǎo.
text.english: Besides department stores, night markets are also places Taiwanese people often go. There are all kinds of delicious snacks, tasty drinks and fun games. An ordinary night market opens at about six in the evening and closes at midnight. Many Taiwanese people like to eat, drink and have fun at night markets, so they are always lively—and even more packed on weekend nights.

text.traditional: 這幾年，來台灣旅遊的外國人越來越多了。他們去夜市可以一邊逛街，一邊吃小吃，還能了解台灣的夜市文化。很多小吃的做法簡單，價錢也便宜，誰都吃得起。台灣最常見的小吃除了臭豆腐、蚵仔煎，還有鹹酥雞、滷肉飯、烤魷魚。天氣熱的時候，排隊買豆花、芒果冰、西瓜汁的人很多，生意好極了！逛夜市的時候，不但吃得飽，也買得到流行的衣服，你一定不會覺得無聊。最有意思的是，買東西的時候，你可以跟老闆講價，也許能便宜一點兒。
text.simplified: 这几年，来台湾旅游的外国人越来越多了。他们去夜市可以一边逛街，一边吃小吃，还能了解台湾的夜市文化。很多小吃的做法简单，价钱也便宜，谁都吃得起。台湾最常见的小吃除了臭豆腐、蚵仔煎，还有咸酥鸡、卤肉饭、烤鱿鱼。天气热的时候，排队买豆花、芒果冰、西瓜汁的人很多，生意好极了！逛夜市的时候，不但吃得饱，也买得到流行的衣服，你一定不会觉得无聊。最有意思的是，买东西的时候，你可以跟老板讲价，也许能便宜一点儿。
text.pinyin: Zhè jǐ nián, lái Táiwān lǚyóu de wàiguórén yuèláiyuè duō le. Tāmen qù yèshì kěyǐ yìbiān guàngjiē, yìbiān chī xiǎochī, hái néng liǎojiě Táiwān de yèshì wénhuà. Hěn duō xiǎochī de zuòfǎ jiǎndān, jiàqián yě piányí, shéi dōu chī de qǐ. Táiwān zuì chángjiàn de xiǎochī chúle chòu dòufǔ, ézǐjiān, háiyǒu xiánsūjī, lǔròu fàn, kǎo yóuyú. Tiānqì rè de shíhòu, páiduì mǎi dòuhuā, mángguǒ bīng, xīguā zhī de rén hěn duō, shēngyì hǎo jíle! Guàng yèshì de shíhòu, búdàn chī de bǎo, yě mǎi de dào liúxíng de yīfu, nǐ yídìng bú huì juéde wúliáo. Zuì yǒuyìsi de shì, mǎi dōngxi de shíhòu, nǐ kěyǐ gēn lǎobǎn jiǎngjià, yěxǔ néng piányí yìdiǎnr.
text.english: In recent years, more and more foreigners have come to Taiwan to travel. At night markets they can shop, eat snacks, and learn about Taiwan's night market culture. Many snacks are simple to make and cheap; anyone can afford them. Besides stinky tofu and oyster omelet, the most common Taiwanese snacks also include popcorn chicken, braised pork on rice and grilled squid. When the weather is hot, many people line up to buy tofu pudding, mango ice and watermelon juice—business is great! When you walk around a night market, you can not only eat your fill but also buy trendy clothes, so you will definitely not feel bored. Most interestingly, when you buy things you can bargain with the vendor; perhaps you can get a lower price.

text.traditional: 在台灣，很多寺廟附近都有夜市，比如說：台北的龍山寺旁邊有華西街夜市。對龍山寺有興趣的外國遊客，常常先去廟裡參觀，再去夜市逛逛。這樣的旅行除了能了解寺廟文化，還吃得到有名的小吃，真的太值得了！
text.simplified: 在台湾，很多寺庙附近都有夜市，比如说：台北的龙山寺旁边有华西街夜市。对龙山寺有兴趣的外国游客，常常先去庙里参观，再去夜市逛逛。这样的旅行除了能了解寺庙文化，还吃得到有名的小吃，真的太值得了！
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, hěn duō sìmiào fùjìn dōu yǒu yèshì, bǐrú shuō: Táiběi de Lóngshān Sì pángbiān yǒu Huáxī Jiē yèshì. Duì Lóngshān Sì yǒu xìngqù de wàiguó yóukè, chángcháng xiān qù miào lǐ cānguān, zài qù yèshì guàngguang. Zhèyàng de lǚxíng chúle néng liǎojiě sìmiào wénhuà, hái chī de dào yǒumíng de xiǎochī, zhēnde tài zhídé le!
text.english: In Taiwan, many temples have night markets nearby. For example, Huaxi Street Night Market is next to Longshan Temple in Taipei. Foreign tourists who are interested in Longshan Temple often visit the temple first and then walk around the night market. On a trip like this, besides learning about temple culture, you can also eat famous snacks—it is really worth it!

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Vs得不得了 / Vs極了: extreme degree
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that something is extremely tall, delicious, lively or tiring.
grammarPages.explanation: The “Vs得不得了” pattern implies a very great degree. The complement “得＋不得了” should come after Vs to add intensity. When this pattern is used, degree adverbs such as “很” and “非常” should not be placed before Vs at the same time. The “Vs極了” pattern also implies a very great degree. The complement “極了” should come after Vs to add intensity. When this pattern is used, adverbs of degree such as “很” and “非常” should not be placed before Vs at the same time.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Vs + 得不得了 / Vs + 極了

text.traditional: 台北101大樓高得不得了！
text.simplified: 台北101大楼高得不得了！
text.pinyin: Táiběi 101 dàlóu gāo de bùdéliǎo!
text.english: The Taipei 101 building is extremely tall!

text.traditional: 我媽媽烤的蛋糕好吃得不得了！
text.simplified: 我妈妈烤的蛋糕好吃得不得了！
text.pinyin: Wǒ māma kǎo de dàngāo hǎochī de bùdéliǎo!
text.english: The cake my mom baked is incredibly delicious!

text.traditional: 他累得不得了，一回家就睡了。
text.simplified: 他累得不得了，一回家就睡了。
text.pinyin: Tā lèi de bùdéliǎo, yì huí jiā jiù shuì le.
text.english: He was extremely tired and went to sleep as soon as he got home.

text.traditional: 週末的時候，夜市熱鬧極了！
text.simplified: 周末的时候，夜市热闹极了！
text.pinyin: Zhōumò de shíhòu, yèshì rènao jíle!
text.english: On weekends, the night market is extremely lively!

text.traditional: 他十歲就能念大學，真是聰明極了！
text.simplified: 他十岁就能念大学，真是聪明极了！
text.pinyin: Tā shí suì jiù néng niàn dàxué, zhēnshì cōngmíng jíle!
text.english: He could attend university at ten—truly extremely smart!

text.traditional: 她快結婚了，所以最近心情好極了！
text.simplified: 她快结婚了，所以最近心情好极了！
text.pinyin: Tā kuài jiéhūn le, suǒyǐ zuìjìn xīnqíng hǎo jíle!
text.english: She is getting married soon, so she has been in a great mood lately!

極了 follows the quality directly: 好極了.

items.fallbackRepair: The quality first, then 極, then 了: 好極了.

result.traditional: 他打得好極了。
result.simplified: 他打得好极了。
result.pinyin: Tā dǎ de hǎo jíle.
result.english: He plays extremely well.

repairs.note: The mistake in the first sentence is the degree word 很. 非常 is the same kind of word, and this pattern cannot have one before the quality.
極 goes with 了 and no 得: 聰明極了. After 得 the ending is 不得了.

items.fallbackRepair: Who, then the quality, then 得, then 不得了: 他聰明得不得了.

result.traditional: 他聰明得不得了！
result.simplified: 他聪明得不得了！
result.pinyin: Tā cōngmíng de bùdéliǎo!
result.english: He is incredibly clever!

segments.traditional: 台灣夏天的天氣熱得極了！
segments.simplified: 台湾夏天的天气热得极了！

repairs.note: 得 is the mistake in the first sentence: 極了 follows the quality directly.
極了 follows the quality directly: 熱極了.

items.fallbackRepair: The quality first, then 極, then 了: 熱極了.

result.traditional: 台灣夏天的天氣熱極了！
result.simplified: 台湾夏天的天气热极了！
result.pinyin: Táiwān xiàtiān de tiānqì rè jíle!
result.english: Summer weather in Taiwan is extremely hot!

segments.traditional: 他的房間非常乾淨極了！
segments.simplified: 他的房间非常干净极了！

repairs.note: 極了 follows the quality directly, with no 得: 乾淨極了.
極了 follows the quality directly: 乾淨極了.

items.fallbackRepair: The mistake in the first sentence is 非常. The thing first, then the quality, then 極, then 了.

result.traditional: 他的房間乾淨極了！
result.simplified: 他的房间干净极了！
result.pinyin: Tā de fángjiān gānjìng jíle!
result.english: His room is extremely clean!

summary: Put 得不得了 or 極了 after a state word to say the degree is very high.
Don't put 很 or 非常 before the word. You can't say 很累得不得了.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: It’s Fun to Go to the Night Market
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that something changes more and more over time.
grammarPages.explanation: The “越來越……” pattern is used to express the level of changes or the amount increasing or decreasing with time. It also includes “S+越來越+Vs / Vst+O / Vaux+V+O.”
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 越來越 + Verb / Adjective

text.traditional: 我跟室友越來越熟了。
text.simplified: 我跟室友越来越熟了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn shìyǒu yuèláiyuè shóu le.
text.english: My roommate and I are getting more and more familiar.

text.traditional: 那個人很不客氣，所以他的朋友越來越少了。
text.simplified: 那个人很不客气，所以他的朋友越来越少了。
text.pinyin: Nà ge rén hěn bú kèqì, suǒyǐ tā de péngyǒu yuèláiyuè shǎo le.
text.english: That person is very rude, so he has fewer and fewer friends.

text.traditional: 阮先生在台灣住了半年了，越來越了解台灣的文化了。
text.simplified: 阮先生在台湾住了半年了，越来越了解台湾的文化了。
text.pinyin: Ruǎn xiānshēng zài Táiwān zhù le bànnián le, yuèláiyuè liǎojiě Táiwān de wénhuà le.
text.english: Mr. Ruan has lived in Taiwan for half a year and understands Taiwanese culture more and more.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The “越來越……” pattern is used to express the level of changes or the amount increasing or decreasing with time. It also includes “S+越來越+Vs / Vst+O / Vaux+V+O.”
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The “越來越……” pattern is used to express the level of changes or the amount increasing or decreasing with time. It also includes “S+越來越+Vs / Vst+O / Vaux+V+O.”

practice.title: Rewrite the sentences with 越來越……

segments.traditional: 冬天到了，今天比昨天更冷了。

repairs.note: Winter is here and today is colder than yesterday: 冷.
更 is in the first sentence, with 比. Without 比, a change that keeps growing is 越來越.

items.fallbackRepair: 越 + 來 + 越, then the quality: 越來越冷.

result.traditional: 冬天到了，天氣越來越冷了。
result.simplified: 冬天到了，天气越来越冷了。
result.pinyin: Dōngtiān dào le, tiānqì yuèláiyuè lěng le.
result.english: Winter is here, and the weather is getting colder and colder.

segments.traditional: 第二課的中國字比第一課的難寫；第三課的中國字比第二課的更難寫……
segments.simplified: 第二课的中国字比第一课的难写；第三课的中国字比第二课的更难写……

repairs.note: Each lesson's characters are harder than the last: 難寫.
很 states a degree. A change that keeps growing from lesson to lesson is 越來越.
一樣 means "the same". Each lesson is harder than the last: 越來越難寫.

items.fallbackRepair: 越來越 first, then the quality: 越來越難寫.

result.traditional: 中國字越來越難寫了。
result.simplified: 中国字越来越难写了。
result.pinyin: Zhōngguó zì yuèláiyuè nán xiě le.
result.english: Chinese characters are getting harder and harder to write.

segments.traditional: 那個日本人以前不敢說中文，住在台灣一個月以後，現在敢說了。
segments.simplified: 那个日本人以前不敢说中文，住在台湾一个月以后，现在敢说了。

repairs.note: He did not dare before, and now he does: 敢.
一樣 means "the same". He has changed: 越來越敢說中文了.

items.fallbackRepair: 越來越 first, then 敢, then the action: 越來越敢說中文.

result.traditional: 那個日本人越來越敢說中文了。
result.simplified: 那个日本人越来越敢说中文了。
result.pinyin: Nàge Rìběn rén yuèláiyuè gǎn shuō Zhōngwén le.
result.english: That Japanese person is becoming more and more confident about speaking Chinese.

summary: 越來越 says a degree or amount keeps getting bigger or smaller over time.
Put it after the subject and before the verb or adjective: 朋友越來越少了.
Don't add 很 after it.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: It’s Fun to Go to the Night Market
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say whether you can afford to eat, drink, buy or rent something.
grammarPages.explanation: The verb complement “起” implies one's ability to afford something. Thus, only a few verbs, such as “吃 (eat)”, “喝 (drink)”, “念 (study)”, “買 (buy)”, “住 (live)”, “付 (pay)”, “租 (rent)”, “穿 (wear)” and “用 (use)”, can be used along with “起”. The common patterns include “V得起” and “V不起”, but patterns like “V起了” or “沒V起” are not acceptable in Chinese.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + V + 得起 / 不起

text.traditional: 那件衣服太貴了，我怎麼買得起？
text.simplified: 那件衣服太贵了，我怎么买得起？
text.pinyin: Nà jiàn yīfu tài guì le, wǒ zěnme mǎi de qǐ?
text.english: That piece of clothing is too expensive. How could I afford it?

text.traditional: 台灣小吃的價錢很便宜，誰都吃得起。
text.simplified: 台湾小吃的价钱很便宜，谁都吃得起。
text.pinyin: Táiwān xiǎochī de jiàqián hěn piányí, shéi dōu chī de qǐ.
text.english: Taiwanese snacks are cheap; anyone can afford to eat them.

text.traditional: 他非常有錢，當然喝得起一杯一千塊的酒。
text.simplified: 他非常有钱，当然喝得起一杯一千块的酒。
text.pinyin: Tā fēicháng yǒu qián, dāngrán hē de qǐ yì bēi yìqiān kuài de jiǔ.
text.english: He is very rich; of course he can afford a glass of wine that costs a thousand dollars.

text.traditional: 在這裡看醫生貴得不得了，沒錢的人看不起。
text.simplified: 在这里看医生贵得不得了，没钱的人看不起。
text.pinyin: Zài zhèlǐ kàn yīshēng guì de bùdéliǎo, méi qián de rén kànbùqǐ.
text.english: Seeing a doctor here is extremely expensive; people without money can't afford it.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The verb complement “起” implies one's ability to afford something. Thus, only a few verbs, such as “吃 (eat)”, “喝 (drink)”, “念 (study)”, “買 (buy)”, “住 (live)”, “付 (pay)”, “租 (rent)”, “穿 (wear)” and “用 (use)”, can be used along with “起”. The common patterns include “V得起” and “V不起”, but patterns like “V起了” or “沒V起” are not acceptable in Chinese.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The verb complement “起” implies one's ability to afford something. Thus, only a few verbs, such as “吃 (eat)”, “喝 (drink)”, “念 (study)”, “買 (buy)”, “住 (live)”, “付 (pay)”, “租 (rent)”, “穿 (wear)” and “用 (use)”, can be used along with “起”. The common patterns include “V得起” and “V不起”, but patterns like “V起了” or “沒V起” are not acceptable in Chinese.

repairs.note: The watch is too expensive, so the speaker cannot afford it: 買不起.
買不到 is not being able to find something to buy. Not having the money for it is 買不起.

items.fallbackRepair: Who, then the verb, then 不, then 起: 我買不起.

result.traditional: 那個牌子的錶太貴了，我買不起。
result.simplified: 那个牌子的表太贵了，我买不起。
result.pinyin: Nàge páizi de biǎo tài guì le, wǒ mǎibùqǐ.
result.english: Watches of that brand are too expensive; I can't afford one.

segments.traditional: 那碗牛肉麵只賣四十塊錢，誰都
segments.simplified: 那碗牛肉面只卖四十块钱，谁都

repairs.note: At forty dollars a bowl, anyone can afford it: 吃得起.
Beef noodles are eaten: 吃.
吃得飽 is about getting full. The sentence is about the low price: 吃得起.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 得, then 起: 吃得起.

result.traditional: 那碗牛肉麵只賣四十塊錢，誰都吃得起。
result.simplified: 那碗牛肉面只卖四十块钱，谁都吃得起。
result.pinyin: Nà wǎn niúròu miàn zhǐ mài sìshí kuài qián, shéi dōu chīdeqǐ.
result.english: That bowl of beef noodles is only forty dollars; anyone can afford to eat it.

repairs.note: 喝不到 is not being able to get any. The sentence is about the price: 喝不起, 喝得起.
喝得完 is being able to finish it. The sentence is about the price: 喝不起, 喝得起.
Coffee is drunk, not eaten: 喝.

items.fallbackRepair: Three hundred is too much and fifty is fine: 喝不起 first, then 喝得起.

result.traditional: 我喝不起一杯三百元的咖啡，只喝得起五十元的。
result.pinyin: Wǒ hēbùqǐ yì bēi sānbǎi yuán de kāfēi, zhǐ hēdeqǐ wǔshí yuán de.
result.english: I can't afford a three-hundred-dollar cup of coffee; I can only afford a fifty-dollar one.

segments.traditional: 這個公寓一個月的房租五萬塊錢，你要租嗎？
segments.simplified: 这个公寓一个月的房租五万块钱，你要租吗？

repairs.note: 怎麼租不起 would ask why B cannot afford it. B means "how could I ever afford it?": 怎麼租得起？
A is talking about the monthly rent: 租.
租得到 is managing to find a place. B is talking about the price: 租得起.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 得, then 起: 怎麼租得起？

result.traditional: 這麼貴，我怎麼租得起？
result.simplified: 这么贵，我怎么租得起？
result.pinyin: Zhème guì, wǒ zěnme zūdeqǐ?
result.english: It's so expensive. How could I afford to rent it?

summary: V得起 and V不起 say whether you can afford something.
It is used with only a few verbs, such as 吃, 喝, 買, 住 and 租.
You can't say V起了 or 沒V起. Say 買不起, not 沒買起.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: It’s Fun to Go to the Night Market
grammarPages.titleEnglish: V飽: full after eating or sleeping
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say whether you got enough to eat or enough sleep.
grammarPages.explanation: The resultative complement “飽” implies that the subject feels fully satisfied or has enough. Thus, “飽” often comes after “吃 (eat)” and “睡 (sleep)”. The “V得飽/V不飽” pattern indicates whether something is potentially enough to satisfy the subject, while the “V飽了” and “沒V飽” patterns indicates whether the subject feels fully satisfied at last or not.
grammarPages.pattern: Verb + 飽 (result) / Verb + 得 / 不 + 飽 (potential)

text.traditional: 你只吃了半碗飯，怎麼吃得飽呢？
text.simplified: 你只吃了半碗饭，怎么吃得饱呢？
text.pinyin: Nǐ zhǐ chī le bàn wǎn fàn, zěnme chī de bǎo ne?
text.english: You only ate half a bowl of rice—how can you be full?

text.traditional: 我昨天只睡了三個鐘頭的覺，當然沒睡飽！
text.simplified: 我昨天只睡了三个钟头的觉，当然没睡饱！
text.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān zhǐ shuì le sān ge zhōngtóu de jiào, dāngrán méi shuì bǎo!
text.english: I only slept three hours yesterday, so of course I didn't get enough sleep!

text.traditional: 今天的舞會我們準備了很多好吃的食物，大家一定吃得飽。
text.simplified: 今天的舞会我们准备了很多好吃的食物，大家一定吃得饱。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān de wǔhuì wǒmen zhǔnbèi le hěn duō hǎochī de shíwù, dàjiā yídìng chī de bǎo.
text.english: We prepared a lot of delicious food for today's dance party; everyone will surely eat their fill.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The resultative complement “飽” implies that the subject feels fully satisfied or has enough. Thus, “飽” often comes after “吃 (eat)” and “睡 (sleep)”. The “V得飽/V不飽” pattern indicates whether something is potentially enough to satisfy the subject, while the “V飽了” and “沒V飽” patterns indicates whether the subject feels fully satisfied at last or not.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The resultative complement “飽” implies that the subject feels fully satisfied or has enough. Thus, “飽” often comes after “吃 (eat)” and “睡 (sleep)”. The “V得飽/V不飽” pattern indicates whether something is potentially enough to satisfy the subject, while the “V飽了” and “沒V飽” patterns indicates whether the subject feels fully satisfied at last or not.

repairs.note: There is too little food, so he will not get full: 吃不飽.
吃不起 is not being able to afford it. Too little food means not getting full: 吃不飽.
吃不完 is having too much to finish. Here there is too little: 吃不飽.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 不, then 飽: 吃不飽.

result.traditional: 這些菜太少了，哥哥吃不飽。
result.simplified: 这些菜太少了，哥哥吃不饱。
result.pinyin: Zhèxiē cài tài shǎo le, gēge chībùbǎo.
result.english: There is too little food; my older brother won't get full.

segments.traditional: 你晚餐只吃了一點兒水果，
segments.simplified: 你晚餐只吃了一点儿水果，

repairs.note: The sentence is about dinner, so the verb is 吃.
V起 is about being able to afford something. Being full is V飽.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 飽, then 了, and 嗎 at the very end: 吃飽了嗎？

result.traditional: 你晚餐只吃了一點兒水果，吃飽了嗎？
result.simplified: 你晚餐只吃了一点儿水果，吃饱了吗？
result.pinyin: Nǐ wǎncān zhǐ chī le yìdiǎnr shuǐguǒ, chībǎo le ma?
result.english: You only had a little fruit for dinner. Are you full?

segments.traditional: 他昨晚睡了十個鐘頭，當然
segments.simplified: 他昨晚睡了十个钟头，当然

repairs.note: The sentence is about sleeping ten hours: 睡.
Ten hours is plenty, so he did get enough sleep: 睡飽了.
Ten hours is plenty, so he did get enough sleep: 睡飽了.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 飽, then 了: 睡飽了.

result.traditional: 他昨晚睡了十個鐘頭，當然睡飽了。
result.simplified: 他昨晚睡了十个钟头，当然睡饱了。
result.pinyin: Tā zuówǎn shuì le shí ge zhōngtóu, dāngrán shuìbǎo le.
result.english: He slept ten hours last night; of course he got enough sleep.

summary: 飽 after a verb means you have had enough, as in 睡飽 and 吃得飽.
V飽了 and 沒V飽 say whether you got enough in the end.
V得飽 and V不飽 say whether you are able to get enough.
Put 飽 right after the verb: 睡飽了, not 睡了飽.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: It’s Fun to Go to the Night Market
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 對……有（沒）興趣: to be interested in
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what someone is or is not interested in.
grammarPages.explanation: “興趣” is used when the subject is passionate about doing something or does something very often.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 對 + Noun / Verb Phrase + 有 / 沒（有）興趣

text.traditional: 台灣人不都對吃臭豆腐有興趣。
text.simplified: 台湾人不都对吃臭豆腐有兴趣。
text.pinyin: Táiwān rén bù dōu duì chī chòu dòufǔ yǒu xìngqù.
text.english: Not all Taiwanese people are interested in eating stinky tofu.

text.traditional: 弟弟只對數學有興趣，其他的都沒興趣。
text.simplified: 弟弟只对数学有兴趣，其他的都没兴趣。
text.pinyin: Dìdi zhǐ duì shùxué yǒu xìngqù, qítā de dōu méi xìngqù.
text.english: My younger brother is only interested in math; he's not interested in anything else.

text.traditional: 陳小姐對逛百貨公司很有興趣，每個週末都去。
text.simplified: 陈小姐对逛百货公司很有兴趣，每个周末都去。
text.pinyin: Chén xiǎojiě duì guàng bǎihuò gōngsī hěn yǒu xìngqù, měi ge zhōumò dōu qù.
text.english: Miss Chen is very interested in shopping at department stores and goes every weekend.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “興趣” is used when the subject is passionate about doing something or does something very often.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “興趣” is used when the subject is passionate about doing something or does something very often.

practice.title: Make sentences with 對……有／沒（有）興趣 and the given patterns.

repairs.note: 跟 means "with". What someone is interested in comes after 對.
興趣 is a thing you have, so it cannot follow 很 directly. It is 有…興趣.

items.fallbackRepair: The person first, then 對 + the activity, then 有一點兒, then 興趣.

result.traditional: 陳先生對做家事有一點兒興趣。
result.simplified: 陈先生对做家事有一点儿兴趣。
result.pinyin: Chén xiānshēng duì zuò jiāshì yǒu yìdiǎnr xìngqù.
result.english: Mr. Chen has a little interest in doing housework.

repairs.note: 給 marks the one who receives something. What someone is interested in comes after 對.
興趣 is a thing you have. After 越來越 it needs 有: 越來越有興趣.
跟 means "with". What someone is interested in comes after 對.

items.fallbackRepair: The person first, then 對 before the activity; after it 越來越, then 有興趣.

result.traditional: 山本良介對學中文越來越有興趣。
result.simplified: 山本良介对学中文越来越有兴趣。
result.pinyin: Shānběn Liángjiè duì xué Zhōngwén yuèláiyuè yǒu xìngqù.
result.english: Yamamoto Ryosuke is more and more interested in learning Chinese.

repairs.note: "Any night market at all" is a question word + 都: 哪個夜市都….
跟 means "with". What someone is interested in comes after 對.

items.fallbackRepair: 對 before the activity, the question word before 夜市, then 都, then 有興趣.

result.traditional: 白小姐對逛哪個夜市都有興趣。
result.simplified: 白小姐对逛哪个夜市都有兴趣。
