Qíshí, yě yǒu rén shēngqì huòshì shāngxīn de shíhòu, huì zìjǐ yígerén qù KTV, yìbiān chàng, yìbiān kū, děng chàng wán yǐhòu, xīnqíng jiù hǎo duō le.
text.english: Taiwanese KTV bars have another special feature—that is, a wide range of food and beverages. As long as you pay a little more, you can eat as much as you want. You do not have to worry that you'll get hungry while singing. Some KTV bars also have funny musical instruments, so that the guests can enjoy their singing more. Actually, there are also some people who go alone to a KTV bar when they are angry or sad. They cry while singing. When they finish singing, their moods become much better.

text.traditional: 要是你想慶祝生日，去KTV跟大家合唱，一定會很開心的；如果心情不好，去KTV自己一個人唱歌，也能把不愉快的事情忘了，所以去KTV真是一個不錯的選擇。
text.simplified: 要是你想庆祝生日，去KTV跟大家合唱，一定会很开心的；如果心情不好，去KTV自己一个人唱歌，也能把不愉快的事情忘了，所以去KTV真是一个不错的选择。
text.pinyin: Yàoshì nǐ xiǎng qìngzhù shēngrì, qù KTV gēn dàjiā héchàng, yídìng huì hěn kāixīn de; rúguǒ xīnqíng bùhǎo, qù KTV zìjǐ yígerén chànggē, yě néng bǎ bù yúkuài de shìqíng wàngle, suǒyǐ qù KTV zhēnshì yíge búcuò de xuǎnzé.
text.english: If you want to celebrate your birthday, go to KTV bars to sing with people, you must be very happy; if you are in a bad mood, go to KTV bars to sing on your own, you can also forget the unpleasant things. So going to KTV bars is really a good choice.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Let’s Go to KTV to Sing!
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Stress that a number is smaller than expected.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern indicates the number is fewer than the speaker's expectation, different from the usage of 「才」 in Lesson Two. Both 「才」 and 「只」 imply a small number. However, 「才」 emphasizes the small number is the speaker's subjective opinion. Also, 「才」 can be followed directly with number words; 「只」 is placed before the verb and cannot be followed with number words, e.g., 「＊這件衣服只一百塊錢。」
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 才 + Number (+ Measure word) + …

text.traditional: 今天咖啡館裡才三個人，客人真少。
text.simplified: 今天咖啡馆里才三个人，客人真少。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān kāfēiguǎn lǐ cái sān ge rén, kèrén zhēn shǎo.
text.english: There are only three people in the café today; there are really few customers.

text.traditional: 我今天中午才吃了一個麵包，現在好餓。
text.simplified: 我今天中午才吃了一个面包，现在好饿。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān zhōngwǔ cái chī le yíge miànbāo, xiànzài hǎo è.
text.english: I only ate one piece of bread at noon today; I'm so hungry now.

text.traditional: A：那個孩子籃球打得很好，他學了很久吧？B：老師說他很聰明，才教了半個月就教會（他）了。
text.simplified: A：那个孩子篮球打得很好，他学了很久吧？B：老师说他很聪明，才教了半个月就教会（他）了。
text.pinyin: A: Nàge háizi lánqiú dǎ de hěn hǎo, tā xué le hěn jiǔ ba? B: Lǎoshī shuō tā hěn cōngmíng, cái jiāo le bàn ge yuè jiù jiāo huì (tā) le.
text.english: A: That child plays basketball very well. He must have been learning for a long time, right? B: The teacher said he is very smart; after only half a month of teaching, he had already learned it.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern indicates the number is fewer than the speaker's expectation, different from the usage of 「才」 in Lesson Two. Both 「才」 and 「只」 imply a small number. However, 「才」 emphasizes the small number is the speaker's subjective opinion. Also, 「才」 can be followed directly with number words; 「只」 is placed before the verb and cannot be followed with number words, e.g., 「＊這件衣服只一百塊錢。」
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern indicates the number is fewer than the speaker's expectation, different from the usage of 「才」 in Lesson Two. Both 「才」 and 「只」 imply a small number. However, 「才」 emphasizes the small number is the speaker's subjective opinion. Also, 「才」 can be followed directly with number words; 「只」 is placed before the verb and cannot be followed with number words, e.g., 「＊這件衣服只一百塊錢。」

repairs.note: 才 says the number is small. 很多次 is not a small number.
都 before a number means "already that many" and makes it sound large. A small number, fewer than expected, takes 才.

items.fallbackRepair: 才 before the verb, and the number of times last: 才去過一次.

result.traditional: 我才去過一次。
result.simplified: 我才去过一次。
result.pinyin: Wǒ cái qùguo yí cì.
result.english: I've only been once.

segments.traditional: 你買的那瓶香水很有名，一定很貴吧？
segments.simplified: 你买的那瓶香水很有名，一定很贵吧？

repairs.note: 只 goes before a verb and cannot sit right before a number. 才 can: 才五百塊錢.
B says it is not expensive, so the price is the small one.
都 before a number means "already that many" and makes it sound large. A small number, fewer than expected, takes 才.

items.fallbackRepair: 才 right before the amount: 才五百塊錢.

result.traditional: 不貴啊！才五百塊錢。
result.simplified: 不贵啊！才五百块钱。
result.pinyin: Bú guì a! Cái wǔbǎi kuài qián.
result.english: It isn't expensive! Only five hundred dollars.

segments.traditional: 你的臉好紅喔！是不是喝了很多酒？
segments.simplified: 你的脸好红喔！是不是喝了很多酒？

repairs.note: He says 不多, so the number is the small one.
都 before a number means "already that many" and makes it sound large. A small number, fewer than expected, takes 才.

items.fallbackRepair: 才 before the verb, and the amount last: 才喝了一杯.

result.traditional: 不多，才喝了一杯。
result.pinyin: Bù duō, cái hē le yì bēi.
result.english: Not much. I only had one glass.

summary: 才 before a number says the amount is less than the speaker expected.
只 can also mean a small amount, but it goes before a verb, not directly before a number. 才 can.
才 shows it is the speaker's own opinion that the amount is small.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Let’s Go to KTV to Sing!
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that something makes someone feel a certain way.
grammarPages.explanation: In the pattern 「A 讓 B + Vs」, A is the cause that makes B have certain feelings.
grammarPages.pattern: A + 讓 + B + Feeling

text.traditional: 朋友送了我一個生日蛋糕，讓我很開心。
text.simplified: 朋友送了我一个生日蛋糕，让我很开心。
text.pinyin: Péngyǒu sòng le wǒ yíge shēngrì dàngāo, ràng wǒ hěn kāixīn.
text.english: A friend gave me a birthday cake, which made me very happy.

text.traditional: 爸爸開了八個小時的車，讓他累得不得了。
text.simplified: 爸爸开了八个小时的车，让他累得不得了。
text.pinyin: Bàba kāi le bā ge xiǎoshí de chē, ràng tā lèi de bùdéliǎo.
text.english: Dad drove for eight hours, which made him incredibly tired.

text.traditional: 昨天吃了不乾淨的東西，讓我的肚子不太舒服。
text.simplified: 昨天吃了不干净的东西，让我的肚子不太舒服。
text.pinyin: Zuótiān chī le bù gānjìng de dōngxi, ràng wǒ de dùzi bú tài shūfu.
text.english: Yesterday I ate something unclean, which made my stomach feel a bit uncomfortable.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In the pattern 「A 讓 B + Vs」, A is the cause that makes B have certain feelings.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In the pattern 「A 讓 B + Vs」, A is the cause that makes B have certain feelings.

segments.traditional: 我已經兩個星期沒倒垃圾了，所以媽媽很生氣。
segments.simplified: 我已经两个星期没倒垃圾了，所以妈妈很生气。

segments.traditional: 我已經兩個星期沒倒垃圾了，
segments.simplified: 我已经两个星期没倒垃圾了，

repairs.note: 被 is for something that is done to someone. Causing a feeling takes 讓.
把 is for doing something to a thing. Causing a feeling takes 讓.
The first sentence says who is angry: Mom.

items.fallbackRepair: 讓, then the person, then the feeling: 讓媽媽很生氣.

result.traditional: 我已經兩個星期沒倒垃圾了，讓媽媽很生氣。
result.simplified: 我已经两个星期没倒垃圾了，让妈妈很生气。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng liǎng ge xīngqí méi dào lèsè le, ràng māma hěn shēngqì.
result.english: I haven't taken out the trash for two weeks, which has made Mom very angry.

segments.traditional: 我一想到明天要去旅行，就很興奮，所以睡不著。
segments.simplified: 我一想到明天要去旅行，就很兴奋，所以睡不着。

repairs.note: 被 is for something that is done to someone. Causing a feeling takes 讓.
把 is for doing something to a thing. Causing a feeling takes 讓.
The first sentence says the speaker is excited: 興奮.

items.fallbackRepair: 讓, then the person, then the feeling: 讓我很興奮.

result.traditional: 想到明天要去旅行，讓我很興奮，所以睡不著。
result.simplified: 想到明天要去旅行，让我很兴奋，所以睡不着。
result.pinyin: Xiǎngdào míngtiān yào qù lǚxíng, ràng wǒ hěn xīngfèn, suǒyǐ shuìbùzháo.
result.english: Thinking about tomorrow's trip has me so excited that I can't sleep.

segments.traditional: 我不喜歡坐飛機，一聽到坐飛機就緊張得不得了。
segments.simplified: 我不喜欢坐飞机，一听到坐飞机就紧张得不得了。

segments.traditional: 我不喜歡坐飛機，坐飛機
segments.simplified: 我不喜欢坐飞机，坐飞机

repairs.note: 被 is for something that is done to someone. Causing a feeling takes 讓.
把 is for doing something to a thing. Causing a feeling takes 讓.
The speaker does not like flying, so the feeling is not a happy one.

items.fallbackRepair: 讓, then the person, then the feeling: 讓我緊張得不得了.

result.traditional: 我不喜歡坐飛機，坐飛機讓我緊張得不得了。
result.simplified: 我不喜欢坐飞机，坐飞机让我紧张得不得了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuān zuò fēijī, zuò fēijī ràng wǒ jǐnzhāng de bùdéliǎo.
result.english: I don't like flying; flying makes me terribly nervous.

summary: 讓 says A is the reason B feels or becomes a certain way.
Put the person who feels right after 讓, then the feeling: 讓我很開心. The cause comes first.

items.title: Grammar 1–6 · Traveling to Hualien by Train

dialogue.title: 坐火車到花蓮去旅行
grammarFocus: 一 + M（+N）+ 都／也 + Neg（+Vaux）+ V
一點兒 + 都／也 + Neg + Vs

text.traditional: （在教室）
text.simplified: （在教室）
text.pinyin: (Zài jiàoshì)
text.english: (In a classroom)

text.traditional: 還有一個星期就要放假了，我打算到花蓮去旅行，好好看看台灣東部的風景。
text.simplified: 还有一个星期就要放假了，我打算到花莲去旅行，好好看看台湾东部的风景。
text.pinyin: Háiyǒu yíge xīngqí jiùyào fàngjià le, wǒ dǎsuàn dào Huālián qù lǚxíng, hǎohǎo kànkan Táiwān dōngbù de fēngjǐng.
text.english: It's only one week until the holidays. I'm planning to go to Hualien and take a thorough look at the scenery of eastern Taiwan.

text.traditional: 前年我去花蓮玩，住在朋友的民宿，他不但請我吃飯，還送給我好幾包當地的名產跟風景明信片呢！
text.simplified: 前年我去花莲玩，住在朋友的民宿，他不但请我吃饭，还送给我好几包当地的名产跟风景明信片呢！
text.pinyin: Qiánnián wǒ qù Huālián wán, zhù zài péngyǒu de mínsù, tā búdàn qǐng wǒ chīfàn, hái sòng gěi wǒ hǎojǐ bāo dāngdì de míngchǎn gēn fēngjǐng míngxìnpiàn ne!
text.english: I went on a trip to Hualien two years ago and stayed at a friend's bed and breakfast. He not only treated me to a meal, but also gave me quite a few bags of local specialty and postcards with landscapes!

text.traditional: 真好！你可以幫我訂那家民宿嗎？
text.simplified: 真好！你可以帮我订那家民宿吗？
text.pinyin: Zhēn hǎo! Nǐ kěyǐ bāng wǒ dìng nà jiā mínsù ma?
text.english: That's really nice! Can you help me book that bed and breakfast?

text.traditional: 可以啊！他的民宿有游泳池，也有免費的無線網路，最棒的是，從房間往外看，還可以看到美麗的大海，你一定會喜歡的。
text.simplified: 可以啊！他的民宿有游泳池，也有免费的无线网路，最棒的是，从房间往外看，还可以看到美丽的大海，你一定会喜欢的。
text.pinyin: Kěyǐ a! Tā de mínsù yǒu yóuyǒngchí, yě yǒu miǎnfèi de wúxiàn wǎnglù, zuì bàng de shì, cóng fángjiān wǎng wài kàn, hái kěyǐ kàndào měilì de dàhǎi, nǐ yídìng huì xǐhuān de.
text.english: Yes, I can! His bed and breakfast has a swimming pool and free Wi-Fi. The best thing is that you can see the beautiful ocean when you look outside from your room, and you will definitely like it.

text.traditional: 住一個晚上要多少錢？要是太貴，我就住不起了。
text.simplified: 住一个晚上要多少钱？要是太贵，我就住不起了。
text.pinyin: Zhù yíge wǎnshàng yào duōshǎo qián? Yàoshì tài guì, wǒ jiù zhù bù qǐ le.
text.english: How much is it for a night? If it's too expensive, I may not afford it.

text.traditional: 別擔心，我會跟他說你是學生，請他算便宜一點兒。
text.simplified: 别担心，我会跟他说你是学生，请他算便宜一点儿。
text.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, wǒ huì gēn tā shuō nǐ shì xuéshēng, qǐng tā suàn piányí yìdiǎnr.
text.english: Don't worry! I'll tell him you are a student and ask him to make it a bit cheaper for you.

text.traditional: （良介拿出一塊錢來）
text.simplified: （良介拿出一块钱来）
text.pinyin: (Liángjiè ná chū yíkuài qián lái)
text.english: (Ryosuke takes out a dollar.)

text.traditional: （笑著說）你看！我只剩下一塊錢，沒錢吃飯了。
text.simplified: （笑着说）你看！我只剩下一块钱，没钱吃饭了。
text.pinyin: (Xiào zhe shuō) Nǐ kàn! Wǒ zhǐ shèngxià yíkuài qián, méi qián chīfàn le.
text.english: (laughing) Look! I only have a dollar left. I have no money for food.

text.traditional: 你比我好，我今天出門時忘了帶錢包，現在一毛錢都沒有，我們中午讓美心請客吧。
text.simplified: 你比我好，我今天出门时忘了带钱包，现在一毛钱都没有，我们中午让美心请客吧。
text.pinyin: Nǐ bǐ wǒ hǎo, wǒ jīntiān chūmén shí wàngle dài qiánbāo, xiànzài yì máo qián dōu méiyǒu, wǒmen zhōngwǔ ràng Měixīn qǐngkè ba.
text.english: You're better than me. I forgot my wallet when I went out today. Now I don't even have a single cent. We shall let Meixin buy us lunch.

text.traditional: （兩人哈哈大笑。這時候，美心剛好從外面走進來）
text.simplified: （两人哈哈大笑。这时候，美心刚好从外面走进来）
text.pinyin: (Liǎng rén hāhā dàxiào. Zhè shí hòu, Měixīn gānghǎo cóng wàimiàn zǒu jìn lái)
text.english: (Both of them are laughing out loud. At that very moment, Meixin walks in.)

text.traditional: 你們在聊什麼？聊得這麼開心？
text.simplified: 你们在聊什么？聊得这么开心？
text.pinyin: Nǐmen zài liáo shénme? Liáo de zhème kāixīn?
text.english: What are you chatting about? You are chatting so happily, aren't you?

text.traditional: 我們正在聊去花蓮旅行的事，可欣要幫我訂民宿。
text.simplified: 我们正在聊去花莲旅行的事，可欣要帮我订民宿。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen zhèngzài liáo qù Huālián lǚxíng de shì, Kěxīn yào bāng wǒ dìng mínsù.
text.english: We are talking about traveling to Hualien. Kexin is going to help me book a bed and breakfast.

text.traditional: 住民宿不錯，你要怎麼去呢？
text.simplified: 住民宿不错，你要怎么去呢？
text.pinyin: Zhù mínsù búcuò, nǐ yào zěnme qù ne?
text.english: Staying at a bed and breakfast is good. How are you planning to go?

text.traditional: 我還沒決定。聽說蘇花公路有一點兒危險，下大雨的時候，山上的大石頭可能會掉下來。
text.simplified: 我还没决定。听说苏花公路有一点儿危险，下大雨的时候，山上的大石头可能会掉下来。
text.pinyin: Wǒ háiméi juédìng. Tīngshuō Sūhuā Gōnglù yǒuyìdiǎnr wéixiǎn, xià dàyǔ de shíhòu, shān shàng de dà shítou kěnéng huì diàoxiàlái.
text.english: I haven't decided yet. I heard that Suhua Highway is a little bit dangerous. During heavy rains, the mountain rocks may fall down.

text.traditional: 蘇花公路是比較危險，搭火車去比較安全，可是假日的票很難買，一下子就賣光了，你最好趕快上網訂票。
text.simplified: 苏花公路是比较危险，搭火车去比较安全，可是假日的票很难买，一下子就卖光了，你最好赶快上网订票。
text.pinyin: Sūhuā Gōnglù shì bǐjiào wéixiǎn, dā huǒchē qù bǐjiào ānquán, kěshì jiàrì de piào hěn nán mǎi, yíxiàzi jiù mài guāng le, nǐ zuìhǎo gǎnkuài shàngwǎng dìngpiào.
text.english: Suhua Highway is indeed more dangerous. Taking the train is safer, but the tickets for holidays are difficult to buy. It only takes a short while until they are sold out. You'd better hurry up and book them online.

text.traditional: 我上過台灣鐵路局的網站，可是看不懂網頁，覺得訂票很難。
text.simplified: 我上过台湾铁路局的网站，可是看不懂网页，觉得订票很难。
text.pinyin: Wǒ shàng guò Táiwān Tiělùjú de wǎngzhàn, kěshì kàn bù dǒng wǎngyè, juéde dìngpiào hěn nán.
text.english: I visited the website of Taiwan Railways, but I didn't understand the web pages. I think booking tickets is very difficult.

text.traditional: 在台灣，上網訂票、訂位一點兒都不難，我現在就幫你訂。（用手機上台鐵的網站）你要訂什麼時候的？
text.simplified: 在台湾，上网订票、订位一点儿都不难，我现在就帮你订。（用手机上台铁的网站）你要订什么时候的？
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, shàngwǎng dìngpiào, dìngwèi yìdiǎnr dōu bù nán, wǒ xiànzài jiù bāng nǐ dìng. (Yòng shǒujī shàng Táitiě de wǎngzhàn) Nǐ yào dìng shénme shíhòu de?
text.english: In Taiwan, booking tickets or making a reservation online is not difficult at all. I can help you book them now. (She entered the website of Taiwan Railways on her cellphone.) For when do you want to book the tickets?

text.traditional: 大概六月底。火車票貴不貴？
text.simplified: 大概六月底。火车票贵不贵？
text.pinyin: Dàgài liù yuè dǐ. Huǒchē piào guì bú guì?
text.english: Approximately for the end of June. Are the train tickets expensive?

text.traditional: 太魯閣號比較貴，可是只停幾個站，兩個多鐘頭就到花蓮了。
text.simplified: 太鲁阁号比较贵，可是只停几个站，两个多钟头就到花莲了。
text.pinyin: Tàilǔgé Hào bǐjiào guì, kěshì zhǐ tíng jǐ ge zhàn, liǎng ge duō zhōngtóu jiù dào Huālián le.
text.english: The Taroko Express is more expensive, but stops only at a few stations. It only takes a bit over two hours to arrive in Hualien.

text.traditional: 貴一點兒沒關係，要是訂得到第一班太魯閣號，早上從台北出發，中午就可以去太魯閣國家公園爬山了。
text.simplified: 贵一点儿没关系，要是订得到第一班太鲁阁号，早上从台北出发，中午就可以去太鲁阁国家公园爬山了。
text.pinyin: Guì yìdiǎnr méiguānxi, yàoshì dìng de dào dìyī bān Tàilǔgé Hào, zǎoshàng cóng Táiběi chūfā, zhōngwǔ jiù kěyǐ qù Tàilǔgé guójiā gōngyuán páshān le.
text.english: It's alright if it's a bit expensive. If I can book the first Taroko Express trip and leave from Taipei in the morning, I will be able to go to Taroko National Park to climb the mountains at noon.

text.traditional: 我前年就是搭太魯閣號去的，真的又快又方便！
text.simplified: 我前年就是搭太鲁阁号去的，真的又快又方便！
text.pinyin: Wǒ qiánnián jiùshì dā Tàilǔgé Hào qù de, zhēnde yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn!
text.english: Two years ago I went by the Taroko Express, too. It is really fast and convenient!

text.traditional: 不好意思，我想坐在窗戶旁邊，可以自己選座位嗎？
text.simplified: 不好意思，我想坐在窗户旁边，可以自己选座位吗？
text.pinyin: Bùhǎoyìsi, wǒ xiǎng zuò zài chuānghù pángbiān, kěyǐ zìjǐ xuǎn zuòwèi ma?
text.english: Excuse me. I want to sit by the window. Can I choose the seat by myself?

text.traditional: 沒辦法，位子都是電腦選的。（看著網頁）訂好了！你把訂票號碼記下來，這個日期以前去便利商店付錢，就可以拿到票了。
text.simplified: 没办法，位子都是电脑选的。（看着网页）订好了！你把订票号码记下来，这个日期以前去便利商店付钱，就可以拿到票了。
text.pinyin: Méibànfǎ, wèizi dōu shì diànnǎo xuǎn de. (Kàn zhe wǎngyè) Dìng hǎo le! Nǐ bǎ dìngpiào hàomǎ jìxiàlái, zhège rìqí yǐqián qù biànlì shāngdiàn fù qián, jiù kěyǐ ná dào piào le.
text.english: There's no way. The seats are all chosen by the computer. (She looks at the website.) Already booked! Write the reservation number down, and go to a convenience store to pay before this date. After that, you can get your tickets.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Traveling to Hualien by Train
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 不但…，還…: not only… but also…
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Add a second, more important point with 不但…，還….
grammarPages.explanation: In addition to the situation after “不但”, the speaker lays more stress on the situation after “還”. In this pattern, the first subject should be consistent with the second one.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 不但 + Clause 1，還 + Clause 2

text.traditional: 我去夜市，不但要吃雞排，還要吃蚵仔煎。
text.simplified: 我去夜市，不但要吃鸡排，还要吃蚵仔煎。
text.pinyin: Wǒ qù yèshì, búdàn yào chī jīpái, háiyào chī ézǐjiān.
text.english: When I go to the night market, I want to eat not only chicken cutlet but also oyster omelet.

text.traditional: 那個印尼學生不但會說中文，還會寫很多中國字。
text.simplified: 那个印尼学生不但会说中文，还会写很多中国字。
text.pinyin: Nà ge Yìnní xuéshēng búdàn huì shuō Zhōngwén, hái huì xiě hěn duō Zhōngguó zì.
text.english: That Indonesian student can not only speak Chinese but also write many Chinese characters.

text.traditional: 這家民宿不但有免費的無線網路，還有游泳池呢！
text.simplified: 这家民宿不但有免费的无线网路，还有游泳池呢！
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā mínsù búdàn yǒu miǎnfèi de wúxiàn wǎnglù, háiyǒu yóuyǒngchí ne!
text.english: This B&B not only has free Wi-Fi but also a swimming pool!

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In addition to the situation after “不但”, the speaker lays more stress on the situation after “還”. In this pattern, the first subject should be consistent with the second one.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In addition to the situation after “不但”, the speaker lays more stress on the situation after “還”. In this pattern, the first subject should be consistent with the second one.

repairs.note: 不但…，還… adds a second point of the same kind. Fast and comfortable are both good points; expensive is not.
不但 is answered by 還, which adds one more point. 可是 would turn against the first half.

items.fallbackRepair: 不但 before the first good point, 還 before the second.

result.traditional: 搭太魯閣號去花蓮，不但很快，還很舒服。
result.simplified: 搭太鲁阁号去花莲，不但很快，还很舒服。
result.pinyin: Dā Tàilǔgé Hào qù Huālián, búdàn hěn kuài, hái hěn shūfu.
result.english: Taking the Taroko Express to Hualien is not only fast but also comfortable.

alternatives.traditional: 搭太魯閣號去花蓮，不但很舒服，還很快。
alternatives.simplified: 搭太鲁阁号去花莲，不但很舒服，还很快。
alternatives.pinyin: Dā Tàilǔgé Hào qù Huālián, búdàn hěn shūfu, hái hěn kuài.
alternatives.english: Taking the Taroko Express to Hualien is not only comfortable but also fast.

repairs.note: 還是 means "or" in a question, or "still". To add one more point after 不但, use 還.
和 joins things (書和筆), not two actions. After 不但, the second action starts with 還.

items.fallbackRepair: 不但 before the first thing you can do, 還 before the second.

result.traditional: 去國外念書，不但可以學英文，還可以認識新朋友。
result.simplified: 去国外念书，不但可以学英文，还可以认识新朋友。
result.pinyin: Qù guówài niànshū, búdàn kěyǐ xué Yīngwén, hái kěyǐ rènshì xīn péngyǒu.
result.english: Studying abroad, you can not only learn English but also make new friends.

alternatives.traditional: 去國外念書，不但可以認識新朋友，還可以學英文。
alternatives.simplified: 去国外念书，不但可以认识新朋友，还可以学英文。
alternatives.pinyin: Qù guówài niànshū, búdàn kěyǐ rènshì xīn péngyǒu, hái kěyǐ xué Yīngwén.
alternatives.english: Studying abroad, you can not only make new friends but also learn English.

repairs.note: 還有 adds one more thing to a list (還有一個問題). Before a verb, "also" is just 還.
可以 is followed by something you can do there: 吃飯.

items.fallbackRepair: 不但 opens the first half. In the second half 還 comes before 可以: 還可以吃飯.

result.traditional: 台灣的 KTV 不但可以唱歌，還可以吃飯呢！
result.simplified: 台湾的 KTV 不但可以唱歌，还可以吃饭呢！
result.pinyin: Táiwān de KTV búdàn kěyǐ chànggē, hái kěyǐ chīfàn ne!
result.english: At a KTV in Taiwan you can not only sing, you can even have a meal!

summary: 不但 gives one fact, and 還 adds another that is stronger.
Both parts have the same subject, and the second one can be left out.
Add the second fact with 還 or 也, not 但是.
If the subjects are different, leave out 不但 and use 也 in the second part.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Traveling to Hualien by Train
grammarPages.titleTraditional: 一 + M（+N）+ 都／也 + Neg（+Vaux）+ V
grammarPages.titleSimplified: 一 + M（+N）+ 都／也 + Neg（+Vaux）+ V
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 一 + Measure word + 都/也 + not: not even one
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Emphasize that there is not even one of something.
grammarPages.explanation: The pattern “一 M 都/也不（沒）” indicates “there is not any...” or “don't want any...”, and shows a strange and unexpected situation with a bit of exaggeration.
grammarPages.pattern: 一 + Measure word (+ Noun) + 都／也 + 不／沒 + Verb

text.traditional: 我等了一個小時，一班公車都沒來。
text.simplified: 我等了一个小时，一班公车都没来。
text.pinyin: Wǒ děng le yí ge xiǎoshí, yì bān gōngchē dōu méi lái.
text.english: I waited for an hour, but not a single bus came.

text.traditional: 我忘了帶錢包，現在一毛（錢）都沒有。
text.simplified: 我忘了带钱包，现在一毛（钱）都没有。
text.pinyin: Wǒ wàngle dài qiánbāo, xiànzài yì máo (qián) dōu méiyǒu.
text.english: I forgot my wallet. Now I don't have even a dime.

text.traditional: 這裡一家醫院也沒有，要是生病了就很麻煩。
text.simplified: 这里一家医院也没有，要是生病了就很麻烦。
text.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yì jiā yīyuàn yě méiyǒu, yàoshì shēngbìng le jiù hěn máfán.
text.english: There isn't even one hospital here. If you get sick, it will be a lot of trouble.

text.traditional: 那個學生不愛上課，一個字都不願意寫，所以老師很生氣。
text.simplified: 那个学生不爱上课，一个字都不愿意写，所以老师很生气。
text.pinyin: Nà ge xuéshēng bú ài shàngkè, yí ge zì dōu bú yuànyì xiě, suǒyǐ lǎoshī hěn shēngqì.
text.english: That student doesn't like going to class and isn't willing to write even one character, so the teacher is very angry.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The pattern “一 M 都/也不（沒）” indicates “there is not any...” or “don't want any...”, and shows a strange and unexpected situation with a bit of exaggeration.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The pattern “一 M 都/也不（沒）” indicates “there is not any...” or “don't want any...”, and shows a strange and unexpected situation with a bit of exaggeration.

repairs.note: "Not even one" always starts from 一: 一個位子也沒有.
杯 counts drinks by the cup (一杯茶). A seat takes 個.
件 counts clothes and matters (一件衣服). A seat takes 個.

items.fallbackRepair: 一, then the measure word, then the thing: 一個位子.

result.traditional: 那家餐廳客滿了，一個位子也沒有。
result.simplified: 那家餐厅客满了，一个位子也没有。
result.pinyin: Nà jiā cāntīng kèmǎn le, yí ge wèizi yě méiyǒu.
result.english: That restaurant is full; there isn't even one seat.

repairs.note: 位 counts people politely (一位老師). Shops and restaurants take 家.
張 counts flat things (一張紙, 一張桌子). Shops and restaurants take 家.
"Not even one" always starts from 一: 一家便利商店都沒有.

items.fallbackRepair: 一, then the measure word, then the thing: 一家便利商店.

result.traditional: 住在這裡真不方便，一家便利商店都沒有。
result.simplified: 住在这里真不方便，一家便利商店都没有。
result.pinyin: Zhù zài zhèlǐ zhēn bù fāngbiàn, yì jiā biànlì shāngdiàn dōu méiyǒu.
result.english: Living here is really inconvenient; there isn't even one convenience store.

segments.traditional: ，為什麼要跟我們來 KTV 呢？
segments.simplified: ，为什么要跟我们来 KTV 呢？

repairs.note: This pattern is a strong "not even one", so the verb must be negative: 不會.
Songs are counted with 首: 一首歌.

items.fallbackRepair: The one thing comes first (一首歌), then 都, then the negative: 一首歌都不會唱.

result.traditional: 你一首歌都不會唱，為什麼要跟我們來 KTV 呢？
result.simplified: 你一首歌都不会唱，为什么要跟我们来 KTV 呢？
result.pinyin: Nǐ yì shǒu gē dōu bú huì chàng, wèishénme yào gēn wǒmen lái KTV ne?
result.english: You can't sing even one song, so why do you want to come to KTV with us?

segments.traditional: 那棟公寓的房租很便宜，可是裡面沒有家具，
segments.simplified: 那栋公寓的房租很便宜，可是里面没有家具，

repairs.note: 本 counts books. The apartment has no furniture (家具): 一張桌子.
The sentence is about furniture (家具). A book is not furniture; a table is.

items.fallbackRepair: 一, then the measure word, then the thing: 一張桌子.

result.traditional: 那棟公寓的房租很便宜，可是裡面沒有家具，一張桌子也沒有。
result.simplified: 那栋公寓的房租很便宜，可是里面没有家具，一张桌子也没有。
result.pinyin: Nà dòng gōngyù de fángzū hěn piányí, kěshì lǐmiàn méiyǒu jiājù, yì zhāng zhuōzi yě méiyǒu.
result.english: The rent for that apartment is cheap, but there is no furniture inside, not even one table.

summary: 一 plus a measure word, then 都 or 也 plus 不 or 沒, means not even one or not at all.
It often sounds exaggerated or surprising.
Don't leave out the measure word after 一.
Use 不, not 沒, before 願意: 一個字都不願意寫.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Traveling to Hualien by Train
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 讓: to make, to let; to allow, to permit (politely)
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Politely say that someone lets or allows another person to do something.
grammarPages.explanation: （1）This “讓” functions as a verb. There are different usages of 讓, such as “to make” and “to let”, ie: “有的 KTV 還有好玩的樂器，讓客人唱得更開心。（to make）（L6）” and the dialogue in this lesson, “讓美心請客吧。”（to let）. The “讓 (to let)” is more polite than “叫” or “要”, ie: “老師叫你去辦公室找他” is an order while “老師讓你去辦公室找他” is a polite expression. （2）“讓” also indicates to permit and to allow somebody to do something, ie: “父母讓我一個人在學校附近租房子。” and “我不舒服，老闆讓我回家休息。”
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 讓 + Person + Verb (+ Object)

text.traditional: 他上班常遲到，工作也做不好，所以老闆讓/叫/要他明天別來上班了。
text.simplified: 他上班常迟到，工作也做不好，所以老板让/叫/要他明天别来上班了。
text.pinyin: Tā shàngbān cháng chídào, gōngzuò yě zuò bùhǎo, suǒyǐ lǎobǎn ràng/ jiào/ yào tā míngtiān bié lái shàngbān le.
text.english: He is often late for work and doesn't do his work well, so the boss told him not to come to work tomorrow.

text.traditional: 陳小姐讓/叫/要男朋友在樓下等一下，因為她還沒選好要穿哪件衣服。
text.simplified: 陈小姐让/叫/要男朋友在楼下等一下，因为她还没选好要穿哪件衣服。
text.pinyin: Chén xiǎojiě ràng/ jiào/ yào nánpéngyǒu zài lóuxià děng yíxià, yīnwèi tā háiméi xuǎn hǎo yào chuān nǎ jiàn yīfu.
text.english: Miss Chen asked her boyfriend to wait downstairs because she still hasn't chosen what to wear.

text.traditional: A：今天我忘了帶錢，讓你請吃午餐，可以嗎？B：沒問題，你想吃什麼？我讓餐廳老闆送過來。
text.simplified: A：今天我忘了带钱，让你请吃午餐，可以吗？B：没问题，你想吃什么？我让餐厅老板送过来。
text.pinyin: A: Jīntiān wǒ wàngle dài qián, ràng nǐ qǐng chī wǔcān, kěyǐ ma? B: Méi wèntí, nǐ xiǎng chī shénme? Wǒ ràng cāntīng lǎobǎn sòng guòlái.
text.english: A: I forgot to bring money today. Is it okay if I let you treat me to lunch? B: No problem. What do you want to eat? I'll have the restaurant owner deliver it.

text.traditional: 客人：這些菜吃不完，可不可以讓我帶回家？老闆：不可以喔！帶回去就不新鮮了。
text.simplified: 客人：这些菜吃不完，可不可以让我带回家？老板：不可以喔！带回去就不新鲜了。
text.pinyin: Kèrén: Zhèxiē cài chī bù wán, kě bù kěyǐ ràng wǒ dài huí jiā? Lǎobǎn: Bù kěyǐ o! Dài huí qù jiù bù xīnxiān le.
text.english: Guest: We can't finish these dishes. Can you let me take them home? Owner: No. They won't be fresh if you take them home.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: （1）This “讓” functions as a verb. There are different usages of 讓, such as “to make” and “to let”, ie: “有的 KTV 還有好玩的樂器，讓客人唱得更開心。（to make）（L6）” and the dialogue in this lesson, “讓美心請客吧。”（to let）. The “讓 (to let)” is more polite than “叫” or “要”, ie: “老師叫你去辦公室找他” is an order while “老師讓你去辦公室找他” is a polite expression. （2）“讓” also indicates to permit and to allow somebody to do something, ie: “父母讓我一個人在學校附近租房子。” and “我不舒服，老闆讓我回家休息。”
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: （1）This “讓” functions as a verb. There are different usages of 讓, such as “to make” and “to let”, ie: “有的 KTV 還有好玩的樂器，讓客人唱得更開心。（to make）（L6）” and the dialogue in this lesson, “讓美心請客吧。”（to let）. The “讓 (to let)” is more polite than “叫” or “要”, ie: “老師叫你去辦公室找他” is an order while “老師讓你去辦公室找他” is a polite expression. （2）“讓” also indicates to permit and to allow somebody to do something, ie: “父母讓我一個人在學校附近租房子。” and “我不舒服，老闆讓我回家休息。”

segments.traditional: 這個月我買了不少書，錢都用完了，可以讓我
segments.simplified: 这个月我买了不少书，钱都用完了，可以让我

repairs.note: The money is gone this month, so the student asks to pay later: 下個月再付.
The landlord is the one speaking, and he just said no. He tells the student to ask someone else: 父母.
The landlord is talking to the student: the parents would help you (幫你), not him.

items.fallbackRepair: After 讓 comes the person, then what that person does: 讓我下個月再付, 讓父母幫你.

result.traditional: 這個月我買了不少書，錢都用完了，可以讓我下個月再付嗎？沒辦法，你讓父母幫你，這樣就可以付了。
result.simplified: 这个月我买了不少书，钱都用完了，可以让我下个月再付吗？没办法，你让父母帮你，这样就可以付了。
result.pinyin: Zhège yuè wǒ mǎi le bùshǎo shū, qián dōu yòngwán le, kěyǐ ràng wǒ xià ge yuè zài fù ma? Méibànfǎ, nǐ ràng fùmǔ bāng nǐ, zhèyàng jiù kěyǐ fù le.
result.english: I bought quite a few books this month and my money is all gone. Could you let me pay next month? — No way. Have your parents help you; then you can pay.

segments.traditional: 這個週末我們一起去阿里山露營，好嗎？
segments.simplified: 这个周末我们一起去阿里山露营，好吗？

repairs.note: She is the one who needs time to think, so it is 讓我.
叫 tells someone to do something. Asking for time for yourself is 讓我….
請 asks someone else to do something. Asking to be given time is 讓我….

items.fallbackRepair: 讓, then the person, then the action: 讓我想一想.

result.traditional: 我們才認識三天，讓我想一想，再告訴你。
result.simplified: 我们才认识三天，让我想一想，再告诉你。
result.pinyin: Wǒmen cái rènshì sān tiān, ràng wǒ xiǎng yì xiǎng, zài gàosu nǐ.
result.english: We have only known each other for three days. Let me think about it, and then I'll tell you.

segments.traditional: 大學畢業以後，你最好出國留學。
segments.simplified: 大学毕业以后，你最好出国留学。

segments.traditional: 我已經二十歲了，要不要出國留學，
segments.simplified: 我已经二十岁了，要不要出国留学，

repairs.note: No one else is part of this talk. The son is twenty and means himself: 讓我自己決定.

items.fallbackRepair: 讓, then the person, then 自己, then the action: 讓我自己決定.

result.traditional: 我已經二十歲了，要不要出國留學，讓我自己決定。
result.simplified: 我已经二十岁了，要不要出国留学，让我自己决定。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng èrshí suì le, yào búyào chūguó liúxué, ràng wǒ zìjǐ juédìng.
result.english: I'm already twenty. Let me decide for myself whether to study abroad or not.

segments.traditional: 我的頭不疼了，為什麼不讓我回家呢？
segments.simplified: 我的头不疼了，为什么不让我回家呢？

repairs.note: The doctor is the one who allows it, and the patient is the one who goes home: 讓你.
Taking the medicine is what the doctor is waiting for. After that the patient may go: 就讓你回家.

items.fallbackRepair: 就 first, then 讓, then the person, then the action: 就讓你回家.

result.traditional: 等你把這個藥吃了，就讓你回家。
result.simplified: 等你把这个药吃了，就让你回家。
result.pinyin: Děng nǐ bǎ zhège yào chī le, jiù ràng nǐ huí jiā.
result.english: Once you have taken this medicine, I'll let you go home.

summary: 讓 plus a person plus a verb means let or allow someone to do something.
It is a polite way to ask someone to act. It sounds softer than 叫 or 要 and is not an order.
Put the person right after 讓. Put 了 at the end or after the verb, not after 讓.
This is 讓 for letting or asking, not 讓 for making someone feel something.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Traveling to Hualien by Train
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 是 + Adjective: indeed, it is true
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Emphasize that something really is a certain way.
grammarPages.explanation: In Chinese, intransitive state verbs, such as “美”, “漂亮”, “年輕”, etc., do not have to come after “是”. However, “是” can be added when the speaker wants to confirm or emphasize the degree of Vs.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 是 + (Adverb) + Adjective

text.traditional: A：我覺得王小姐比以前漂亮了。B：她是比以前漂亮多了。
text.simplified: A：我觉得王小姐比以前漂亮了。B：她是比以前漂亮多了。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ juéde Wáng xiǎojiě bǐ yǐqián piàoliàng le. B: Tā shì bǐ yǐqián piàoliàng duō le.
text.english: A: I think Miss Wang is prettier than before. B: She is indeed much prettier than before.

text.traditional: A：外國人都覺得中國字很難寫，你覺得呢？B：是有點兒難寫，可是多練習幾次就好了。
text.simplified: A：外国人都觉得中国字很难写，你觉得呢？B：是有点儿难写，可是多练习几次就好了。
text.pinyin: A: Wàiguórén dōu juéde Zhōngguó zì hěn nán xiě, nǐ juéde ne? B: Shì yǒudiǎnr nán xiě, kěshì duō liànxí jǐ cì jiù hǎo le.
text.english: A: Foreigners all think Chinese characters are hard to write. What do you think? B: They are indeed a little hard to write, but they'll be fine after a few more times of practice.

text.traditional: 良介：聽說蘇花公路的風景很美，是真的嗎？美心：是真的，可是下大雨的時候，那條路比較危險。
text.simplified: 良介：听说苏花公路的风景很美，是真的吗？美心：是真的，可是下大雨的时候，那条路比较危险。
text.pinyin: Liángjiè: Tīngshuō Sūhuā Gōnglù de fēngjǐng hěn měi, shì zhēnde ma? Měixīn: Shì zhēnde, kěshì xià dàyǔ de shíhòu, nà tiáo lù bǐjiào wéixiǎn.
text.english: Ryosuke: I heard the scenery on the Suhua Highway is beautiful. Is that true? Meixin: It is true, but that road is rather dangerous when it rains heavily.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In Chinese, intransitive state verbs, such as “美”, “漂亮”, “年輕”, etc., do not have to come after “是”. However, “是” can be added when the speaker wants to confirm or emphasize the degree of Vs.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In Chinese, intransitive state verbs, such as “美”, “漂亮”, “年輕”, etc., do not have to come after “是”. However, “是” can be added when the speaker wants to confirm or emphasize the degree of Vs.

repairs.note: Being busy is no reason to go home; being tired is. B confirms A's guess: 累.
B is going home, so B agrees: 是有點兒累.
Before a feeling, "a little" is 有點兒 (有點兒累). 一點兒 comes after, when comparing (便宜一點兒).

items.fallbackRepair: 是 first, then how much, then the feeling: 是有點兒累.

result.traditional: 我是有點兒累，所以現在要回家了。
result.simplified: 我是有点儿累，所以现在要回家了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ shì yǒudiǎnr lèi, suǒyǐ xiànzài yào huí jiā le.
result.english: I am a little tired, so I'm going home now.

segments.traditional: 中文很重要，把中文學好了，比較容易找工作。
segments.simplified: 中文很重要，把中文学好了，比较容易找工作。

segments.traditional: ，想到中國去工作的外國人一定得學。
segments.simplified: ，想到中国去工作的外国人一定得学。

repairs.note: 是 confirms what A just said. A said Chinese is important: 重要.
To agree that something really is so, put 是 before 很 + the quality, not 有.

items.fallbackRepair: 是 goes before 很 + the quality: 是很重要.

result.traditional: 中文是很重要，想到中國去工作的外國人一定得學。
result.simplified: 中文是很重要，想到中国去工作的外国人一定得学。
result.pinyin: Zhōngwén shì hěn zhòngyào, xiǎng dào Zhōngguó qù gōngzuò de wàiguórén yídìng děi xué.
result.english: Chinese is indeed important; foreigners who want to work in China definitely have to learn it.

segments.traditional: 這支新手機五萬塊，太貴了吧？
segments.simplified: 这支新手机五万块，太贵了吧？

segments.traditional: ，可是這個牌子很有名，我一定要買。
segments.simplified: ，可是这个牌子很有名，我一定要买。

repairs.note: B goes on with 可是, so B first agrees with A that it is expensive: 貴.
是 confirms what A just said. A said the phone is expensive: 貴.

items.fallbackRepair: 是 first, then 很, then the quality: 是很貴.

result.traditional: 是很貴，可是這個牌子很有名，我一定要買。
result.simplified: 是很贵，可是这个牌子很有名，我一定要买。
result.pinyin: Shì hěn guì, kěshì zhège páizi hěn yǒumíng, wǒ yídìng yào mǎi.
result.english: It is expensive, true, but this brand is famous; I must buy it.

summary: Add 是 before an adjective like 美 or 漂亮 to confirm it or stress how much.
A degree word can go between 是 and the adjective.
Put 是 after the subject. Don't add it every time: normally say 很漂亮.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Traveling to Hualien by Train
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that something has been completely used up or eaten.
grammarPages.explanation: The “光” here serves as a verb complement denoting “running out” or “nothing left”, and sometimes it suggests a sense of regret and disappointment. It often collocates with “把”, ie: “把錢用光了” and “弟弟把糖吃光了”; however, “我把功課寫光了” is unacceptable.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + (把 + Object) + Verb + 光 + 了

text.traditional: 弟弟把我的巧克力都吃光了，讓我很生氣。
text.simplified: 弟弟把我的巧克力都吃光了，让我很生气。
text.pinyin: Dìdi bǎ wǒ de qiǎokèlì dōu chī guāng le, ràng wǒ hěn shēngqì.
text.english: My younger brother ate all my chocolate, which made me very angry.

text.traditional: 時間很晚了，咖啡館的客人差不多都走光了。
text.simplified: 时间很晚了，咖啡馆的客人差不多都走光了。
text.pinyin: Shíjiān hěn wǎn le, kāfēiguǎn de kèrén chàbùduō dōu zǒu guāng le.
text.english: It was very late, and almost all the customers in the café had left.

text.traditional: 要是你一下子就把獎學金用光，下個月就沒錢付房租了。
text.simplified: 要是你一下子就把奖学金用光，下个月就没钱付房租了。
text.pinyin: Yàoshì nǐ yíxiàzi jiù bǎ jiǎngxuéjīn yòng guāng, xià ge yuè jiù méi qián fù fángzū le.
text.english: If you use up your scholarship all at once, you won't have money to pay rent next month.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The “光” here serves as a verb complement denoting “running out” or “nothing left”, and sometimes it suggests a sense of regret and disappointment. It often collocates with “把”, ie: “把錢用光了” and “弟弟把糖吃光了”; however, “我把功課寫光了” is unacceptable.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The “光” here serves as a verb complement denoting “running out” or “nothing left”, and sometimes it suggests a sense of regret and disappointment. It often collocates with “把”, ie: “把錢用光了” and “弟弟把糖吃光了”; however, “我把功課寫光了” is unacceptable.

segments.traditional: 這個捷運站有免費的地圖，可是已經被
segments.simplified: 这个捷运站有免费的地图，可是已经被

repairs.note: Maps are taken, not eaten: 拿.
V到 means managing to get something (拿到了). "None left" is V光.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb first, then 光, then 了: 拿光了.

result.traditional: 這個捷運站有免費的地圖，可是已經被拿光了。
result.simplified: 这个捷运站有免费的地图，可是已经被拿光了。
result.pinyin: Zhège jiéyùn zhàn yǒu miǎnfèi de dìtú, kěshì yǐjīng bèi náguāng le.
result.english: This MRT station has free maps, but they have already all been taken.

segments.traditional: 媽媽做的餃子太好吃了，我不到十分鐘就
segments.simplified: 妈妈做的饺子太好吃了，我不到十分钟就

repairs.note: Dumplings are eaten, not drunk: 吃.
Mom made the dumplings (做). What the speaker did was eat them all: 吃光了.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb first, then 光, then 了: 吃光了.

result.traditional: 媽媽做的餃子太好吃了，我不到十分鐘就吃光了。
result.simplified: 妈妈做的饺子太好吃了，我不到十分钟就吃光了。
result.pinyin: Māma zuò de jiǎozi tài hǎochī le, wǒ bú dào shí fēnzhōng jiù chīguāng le.
result.english: The dumplings Mom made were so delicious that I ate them all in less than ten minutes.

segments.traditional: 你最好別一個人把這瓶酒
segments.simplified: 你最好别一个人把这瓶酒

repairs.note: Wine is something you drink: 喝.
V到 means managing to get something (喝到了). Leaving nothing in the bottle is 喝光.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb first, then 光: 喝光.

result.traditional: 你最好別一個人把這瓶酒喝光，這樣對身體不好。
result.simplified: 你最好别一个人把这瓶酒喝光，这样对身体不好。
result.pinyin: Nǐ zuìhǎo bié yígerén bǎ zhè píng jiǔ hēguāng, zhèyàng duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
result.english: You had better not finish this bottle of wine by yourself; that is bad for your health.

segments.traditional: 今天的功課很多，我寫了三個小時才
segments.simplified: 今天的功课很多，我写了三个小时才

repairs.note: 光 is for things used up until none is left (吃光, 用光). Finishing a task is V完: 寫完.
V到 means managing to get or reach something. Finishing a task is V完: 寫完.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb first, then 完: 寫完.

result.traditional: 今天的功課很多，我寫了三個小時才寫完。
result.simplified: 今天的功课很多，我写了三个小时才写完。
result.pinyin: Jīntiān de gōngkè hěn duō, wǒ xiě le sān ge xiǎoshí cái xiěwán.
result.english: There was a lot of homework today; it took me three hours to finish it.

summary: 光 after a verb means something is used up or eaten up, with none left.
It often goes with 把 and 了, and can sound unhappy or regretful.
Put 光 after the verb: 吃光了, not 光吃了.
Don't use it for homework. Say 寫完, not 寫光.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Traveling to Hualien by Train
grammarPages.titleTraditional: 一點兒 + 都／也 + Neg + Vs
grammarPages.titleSimplified: 一点儿 + 都／也 + Neg + Vs
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 一點兒都/也不: not at all
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say strongly that something is not at all a certain way.
grammarPages.explanation: The expression “一點兒都/也不” shows strong negation, often followed by verbs or state verbs to emphasize the subject is not in a certain status at all.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 一點兒 + 都／也 + 不／沒 + Adjective／Verb

text.traditional: 這杯珍珠奶茶是無糖的，一點兒都不甜。
text.simplified: 这杯珍珠奶茶是无糖的，一点儿都不甜。
text.pinyin: Zhè bēi zhēnzhū nǎichá shì wú táng de, yìdiǎnr dōu bù tián.
text.english: This cup of bubble tea is sugar-free; it's not sweet at all.

text.traditional: 網路訂票一點兒也不難，你可以自己上網試試看。
text.simplified: 网路订票一点儿也不难，你可以自己上网试试看。
text.pinyin: Wǎnglù dìngpiào yìdiǎnr yě bù nán, nǐ kěyǐ zìjǐ shàngwǎng shìshi kàn.
text.english: Booking tickets online is not difficult at all. You can go online and try it yourself.

text.traditional: 我跟他一點兒都不熟，為什麼要一起去KTV唱歌呢？
text.simplified: 我跟他一点儿都不熟，为什么要一起去KTV唱歌呢？
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn tā yìdiǎnr dōu bù shóu, wèishénme yào yìqǐ qù KTV chànggē ne?
text.english: He and I are not close at all. Why would we go to KTV and sing together?

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The expression “一點兒都/也不” shows strong negation, often followed by verbs or state verbs to emphasize the subject is not in a certain status at all.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The expression “一點兒都/也不” shows strong negation, often followed by verbs or state verbs to emphasize the subject is not in a certain status at all.

segments.traditional: 你兒子在美國留學，你擔心嗎？
segments.simplified: 你儿子在美国留学，你担心吗？

segments.traditional: 擔心，他會自己做飯、打掃。
segments.simplified: 担心，他会自己做饭、打扫。

repairs.note: 有一點兒擔心 would mean she does worry a little. Her son can cook and clean, so she doesn't worry at all: 一點兒都不.
Her son can cook and clean by himself, so she is not worried. 一點兒都… is followed by 不: 一點兒都不擔心.

items.fallbackRepair: 一點兒 first, then 都, then 不: 一點兒都不擔心.

result.traditional: 我一點兒都不擔心，他會自己做飯、打掃。
result.simplified: 我一点儿都不担心，他会自己做饭、打扫。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yìdiǎnr dōu bù dānxīn, tā huì zìjǐ zuòfàn, dǎsǎo.
result.english: I'm not worried at all; he can cook and clean by himself.

segments.traditional: 日本菜辣嗎？我不喜歡吃辣的東西。
segments.simplified: 日本菜辣吗？我不喜欢吃辣的东西。

repairs.note: The question was whether Japanese food is spicy: 辣.
After 一點兒, the strong "not at all" takes 也 or 都, not 還.
一點兒也… is followed by a negative: 不辣.

items.fallbackRepair: 也 first, then 不, then the quality: 一點兒也不辣.

result.traditional: 日本菜一點兒也不辣，你吃吃看就知道了。
result.simplified: 日本菜一点儿也不辣，你吃吃看就知道了。
result.pinyin: Rìběn cài yìdiǎnr yě bú là, nǐ chī chī kàn jiù zhīdào le.
result.english: Japanese food is not spicy at all. Try it and you'll see.

segments.traditional: 你為什麼只吃菜，不喝湯？
segments.simplified: 你为什么只吃菜，不喝汤？

repairs.note: Soup is something you drink, so it is 好喝 or 不好喝.
一下 goes after an action (等一下). "Not at all" is 一點兒都不….

items.fallbackRepair: 一點兒 first, then 都, then 不, then the quality: 一點兒都不好喝.

result.traditional: 這碗湯一點兒都不好喝，我不要喝。
result.simplified: 这碗汤一点儿都不好喝，我不要喝。
result.pinyin: Zhè wǎn tāng yìdiǎnr dōu bù hǎohē, wǒ búyào hē.
result.english: This bowl of soup doesn't taste good at all; I don't want to drink it.

summary: 一點兒 plus 都 or 也 plus 不 or 沒 means not at all.
Put 一點兒 before 都, not after: 一點兒都不甜.
有一點兒 means a little. 一點兒都 with a no word means not at all.

items.title: Grammar 7–8 · Online Ticket Booking

text.traditional: 我跟室友計畫春假去阿里山森林遊樂區走走。那時候草綠了、花開了，天氣也暖和了。不必帶太多行李，也不需要穿大衣，只要穿一雙好走的鞋子，再帶一件外套、雨衣、幾雙襪子跟幾件內衣褲就夠了。
text.simplified: 我跟室友计划春假去阿里山森林游乐区走走。那时候草绿了、花开了，天气也暖和了。不必带太多行李，也不需要穿大衣，只要穿一双好走的鞋子，再带一件外套、雨衣、几双袜子跟几件内衣裤就够了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn shìyǒu jìhuà chūnjià qù Ālǐ Shān sēnlín yóulè qū zǒuzǒu. Nà shíhòu cǎo lǜ le, huā kāi le, tiānqì yě nuǎnhuo le. Búbì dài tài duō xínglǐ, yě bù xūyào chuān dàyī, zhǐyào chuān yì shuāng hǎo zǒu de xiézi, zài dài yí jiàn wàitào, yǔyī, jǐ shuāng wàzi gēn jǐ jiàn nèiyīkù jiù gòu le.
text.english: My roommate and I are planning to walk around Alishan Forest Recreation Area during the spring break. At that time the grass is green, the flowers are blooming, and the weather is already warm, too. We do not have to bring too much luggage or wear a coat. Just wear a pair of good walking shoes, and then bring a jacket, a raincoat, a few pairs of socks and some underwear is enough.

text.traditional: 本來我想參加阿里山的團體旅遊，這樣就不必自己上網訂票、訂旅館，可是室友覺得自己去比較自由，也不趕時間，所以我們決定第一天搭台鐵到嘉義，再從嘉義搭小火車上阿里山，當天晚上就可以在山上散步、看星星了。沒想到剛上台鐵的網站，就發現春假第一天的票都賣光了。原來除了去國外旅行，想留在國內玩的人也不少。
text.simplified: 本来我想参加阿里山的团体旅游，这样就不必自己上网订票、订旅馆，可是室友觉得自己去比较自由，也不赶时间，所以我们决定第一天搭台铁到嘉义，再从嘉义搭小火车上阿里山，当天晚上就可以在山上散步、看星星了。没想到刚上台铁的网站，就发现春假第一天的票都卖光了。原来除了去国外旅行，想留在国内玩的人也不少。
text.pinyin: Běnlái wǒ xiǎng cānjiā Ālǐ Shān de tuántǐ lǚyóu, zhèyàng jiù búbì zìjǐ shàngwǎng dìngpiào, dìng lǚguǎn, kěshì shìyǒu juéde zìjǐ qù bǐjiào zìyóu, yě bù gǎn shíjiān, suǒyǐ wǒmen juédìng dìyī tiān dā Táitiě dào Jiāyì, zài cóng Jiāyì dā xiǎo huǒchē shàng Ālǐ Shān, dāngtiān wǎnshàng jiù kěyǐ zài shān shàng sànbù, kàn xīngxīng le. Méixiǎngdào gāng shàng Táitiě de wǎngzhàn, jiù fāxiàn chūnjià dìyī tiān de piào dōu mài guāng le. Yuánlái chúle qù guówài lǚxíng, xiǎng liú zài guónèi wán de rén yě bùshǎo.
text.english: Originally, I wanted to participate in a group tour to Alishan so that I wouldn't have to book the tickets or a hotel by myself. However, my roommate thought that going on our own gives us more freedom and we do not have to hurry. So we decided to take the Taiwan Railways to Chiayi on the first day, then take the Alishan Forest Railway to go up to Alishan, and we can take a walk and see the stars on the mountain that evening. I didn't expect as soon as I went to the website of Taiwan Railways to book the tickets for the first day of spring break, only to find that they had been sold out. It turns out that in addition to traveling abroad, many people still want to stay in the country and have fun.

text.traditional: 後來我上高鐵的網站，很幸運訂到了兩張台北到嘉義的車票，馬上用信用卡付了錢，這樣就放心了。雖然高鐵票比較貴，可是又快又舒服，而且第一天晚上住在嘉義市也不錯，因為當地的雞肉飯很有名，剛好趁這個機會去吃吃看。我正在想像一邊吃雞肉飯，一邊喝啤酒的樣子，室友忽然大叫，「成功了！阿里山小火車的票訂到了！」
text.simplified: 后来我上高铁的网站，很幸运订到了两张台北到嘉义的车票，马上用信用卡付了钱，这样就放心了。虽然高铁票比较贵，可是又快又舒服，而且第一天晚上住在嘉义市也不错，因为当地的鸡肉饭很有名，刚好趁这个机会去吃吃看。我正在想像一边吃鸡肉饭，一边喝啤酒的样子，室友忽然大叫，「成功了！阿里山小火车的票订到了！」
text.pinyin: Hòulái wǒ shàng gāotiě de wǎngzhàn, hěn xìngyùn dìng dào le liǎng zhāng Táiběi dào Jiāyì de chēpiào, mǎshàng yòng xìnyòngkǎ fù le qián, zhèyàng jiù fàngxīn le. Suīrán gāotiě piào bǐjiào guì, kěshì yòu kuài yòu shūfu, érqiě dìyī tiān wǎnshàng zhù zài Jiāyì Shì yě búcuò, yīnwèi dāngdì de jīròu fàn hěn yǒumíng, gānghǎo chèn zhège jīhuì qù chīchi kàn. Wǒ zhèngzài xiǎngxiàng yìbiān chī jīròu fàn, yìbiān hē píjiǔ de yàngzi, shìyǒu hūrán dà jiào, “Chénggōng le! Ālǐ Shān xiǎo huǒchē de piào dìng dào le!”
text.english: Later, on the website of the High Speed Rail, I was lucky enough to book two tickets from Taipei to Chiayi. I immediately paid for them with a credit card, so I was relieved. Although the high-speed rail tickets are more expensive, the HSR is fast and comfortable. It is also good to stay in Chiayi City the first night because the local chicken rice is well-known and I can take this opportunity to try it. When I was imagining that we were drinking beer while eating chicken rice, my roommate suddenly shouted “I made it! I booked the Alishan Forest Railway tickets!”

text.traditional: 我們能利用網路做好多事情，除了訂車票、機票、餐廳，還能買到各式各樣、又便宜又流行的衣服。有網路真好！
text.simplified: 我们能利用网路做好多事情，除了订车票、机票、餐厅，还能买到各式各样、又便宜又流行的衣服。有网路真好！
text.pinyin: Wǒmen néng lìyòng wǎnglù zuò hǎo duō shìqíng, chúle dìng chēpiào, jīpiào, cāntīng, hái néng mǎi dào gèshìgèyàng, yòu piányí yòu liúxíng de yīfu. Yǒu wǎnglù zhēn hǎo!
text.english: We can use the Internet to do so many things. In addition to booking public transport tickets, air tickets, restaurants, we can also buy a variety of inexpensive fashion clothes. It's really great to have the Internet!

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Traveling to Hualien by Train
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one thing happened right after another.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern indicates when the situation after “剛” happens, another situation or action occurs right away. It emphasizes the close connection between two situations or actions. If the two clauses has different subjects, the subject of the latter clause should be placed before “就”.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 剛 + Verb₁，(+ Subject₂) + 就 + Verb₂

text.traditional: 那個蛋糕剛烤好就被孩子吃光了。
text.simplified: 那个蛋糕刚烤好就被孩子吃光了。
text.pinyin: Nà ge dàngāo gāng kǎo hǎo jiù bèi háizi chī guāng le.
text.english: That cake was eaten up by the children as soon as it was baked.

text.traditional: 他剛搬進宿舍，無線網路就壞了。
text.simplified: 他刚搬进宿舍，无线网路就坏了。
text.pinyin: Tā gāng bān jìn sùshè, wúxiàn wǎnglù jiù huài le.
text.english: The Wi-Fi broke right after he moved into the dorm.

text.traditional: 他剛畢業就找到了一份好工作，真是太幸運了！
text.simplified: 他刚毕业就找到了一份好工作，真是太幸运了！
text.pinyin: Tā gāng bìyè jiù zhǎodào le yí fèn hǎo gōngzuò, zhēnshì tài xìngyùn le!
text.english: He found a good job right after graduating. He is really so lucky!

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern indicates when the situation after “剛” happens, another situation or action occurs right away. It emphasizes the close connection between two situations or actions. If the two clauses has different subjects, the subject of the latter clause should be placed before “就”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern indicates when the situation after “剛” happens, another situation or action occurs right away. It emphasizes the close connection between two situations or actions. If the two clauses has different subjects, the subject of the latter clause should be placed before “就”.

practice.title: Complete the sentences with the given phrases.

repairs.note: Here 才 would say it happens later than expected. One thing right after another is 剛…就….
再 puts off the second action until later (吃飽了再洗澡). Right after is 剛…就….

items.fallbackRepair: 剛 before what happens first, 就 before what follows at once: 剛吃飽就洗澡.

result.traditional: 醫生說剛吃飽就洗澡，這樣對身體不好。
result.simplified: 医生说刚吃饱就洗澡，这样对身体不好。
result.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō gāng chībǎo jiù xǐzǎo, zhèyàng duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
result.english: The doctor says that taking a bath right after a full meal is bad for your health.

repairs.note: 也 adds something to what was said before. One action right after another is 剛…就….
Driving after a meal is not dangerous. The danger is driving right after drinking: 喝酒.

items.fallbackRepair: 剛 before the first action, then 就 before 開車: 剛喝酒就開車.

result.traditional: 陳先生剛喝酒就開車，這樣太危險了。
result.simplified: 陈先生刚喝酒就开车，这样太危险了。
result.pinyin: Chén xiānshēng gāng hē jiǔ jiù kāichē, zhèyàng tài wéixiǎn le.
result.english: Mr. Chen drives right after drinking; that is too dangerous.

repairs.note: Students go home when the exam is over, not when it starts: 結束.
Here 才 would say it happens later than expected, and it does not go with 了 here. Right after is 就.

items.fallbackRepair: The second clause has its own subject, and it comes before 就: 學生就回家了.

result.traditional: 考試剛結束，學生就回家了。
result.simplified: 考试刚结束，学生就回家了。
result.pinyin: Kǎoshì gāng jiéshù, xuéshēng jiù huí jiā le.
result.english: The exam had just ended, and the students went home right away.

summary: 剛 gives the first thing, and 就 gives the second thing that happens right after.
If the second part has a different subject, put it before 就.
Don't add 了 right after the first action. Go straight to 就.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Traveling to Hualien by Train
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that someone uses a good chance or time to do something.
grammarPages.explanation: The expression “趁著” means taking advantage of a certain chance or time to do something beneficial to oneself. “趁” can be followed by nouns, verb phrases, and intransitive state verbs, etc.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 趁（著）+ Chance／Time + Verb Phrase

text.traditional: 媽媽趁（著）好天氣，把髒衣服都洗了。
text.simplified: 妈妈趁（着）好天气，把脏衣服都洗了。
text.pinyin: Māma chèn (zhe) hǎo tiānqì, bǎ zāng yīfu dōu xǐ le.
text.english: Mom took advantage of the good weather and washed all the dirty clothes.

text.traditional: 張先生趁著到花蓮旅行時，買了一些當地的名產。
text.simplified: 张先生趁着到花莲旅行时，买了一些当地的名产。
text.pinyin: Zhāng xiānshēng chènzhe dào Huālián lǚxíng shí, mǎi le yìxiē dāngdì de míngchǎn.
text.english: Mr. Zhang took advantage of his trip to Hualien to buy some local specialties.

text.traditional: 他趁著去法國留學的時候，參觀了有名的博物館。
text.simplified: 他趁着去法国留学的时候，参观了有名的博物馆。
text.pinyin: Tā chènzhe qù Fǎguó liúxué de shíhòu, cānguān le yǒumíng de bówùguǎn.
text.english: He took advantage of his time studying in France to visit famous museums.

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The expression “趁著” means taking advantage of a certain chance or time to do something beneficial to oneself. “趁” can be followed by nouns, verb phrases, and intransitive state verbs, etc.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The expression “趁著” means taking advantage of a certain chance or time to do something beneficial to oneself. “趁” can be followed by nouns, verb phrases, and intransitive state verbs, etc.

repairs.note: Students play on their phones when no one is watching: 老師不在.
雖然 needs a turn with 可是 after it. Using a chance to do something is 趁著.

items.fallbackRepair: 趁著 first, then the chance they use: 趁著老師不在.

result.traditional: 有學生趁著老師不在，看手機、玩遊戲。
result.simplified: 有学生趁着老师不在，看手机、玩游戏。
result.pinyin: Yǒu xuéshēng chènzhe lǎoshī bú zài, kàn shǒujī, wán yóuxì.
result.english: Some students take advantage of the teacher being away to look at their phones and play games.

repairs.note: The child ate all the candy when no one was there to say no: 不在家.
剛…就… is one thing right after another. Using a chance to do something is 趁著.
一邊 comes in a pair, for two actions at the same time. Using a chance is 趁著.

items.fallbackRepair: 趁著 first, then the chance the child uses: 趁著父母不在家.

result.traditional: 孩子趁著父母不在家，把糖都吃光了。
result.simplified: 孩子趁着父母不在家，把糖都吃光了。
result.pinyin: Háizi chènzhe fùmǔ bú zài jiā, bǎ táng dōu chīguāng le.
result.english: While the parents were out, the child ate up all the candy.

repairs.note: While you are young you should do more of it, not less: 多去旅行.
在 marks a place or something going on right now. Using the time while you are young is 趁年輕.

items.fallbackRepair: 趁 before the chance (年輕), then 多 before what to do more of.

result.traditional: 你應該趁年輕，多去旅行。
result.simplified: 你应该趁年轻，多去旅行。
result.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi chèn niánqīng, duō qù lǚxíng.
result.english: You should travel more while you are young.

summary: 趁 means using a chance, a time, or good weather to do something that helps you.
After it you can use a noun, a verb phrase, or a state word. 著 is optional.
趁 uses a chance. 因為 gives a reason.
Don't say 趁了. Say 趁著 or 趁.

items.title: Grammar 1–5 · Give Me the Stickers, please. I Want to Exchange Them for Snoopy!

grammarPages.lessonTitle: 請給我貼紙，我要換史努比！
grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Give Me the Stickers, please. I Want to Exchange Them for Snoopy!
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Set a quantity threshold that unlocks an offer or condition.
grammarPages.explanation: “滿” is followed by a number. This pattern means reaching a certain amount or number.
grammarPages.pattern: 滿 + Number + Measure word (+ Noun)，+ Result

text.traditional: 在那家店訂飲料，滿十杯就可以替客人送過去。
text.english: At that shop, they can deliver an order to the customer once it reaches ten cups.
text.pinyin: Zài nà jiā diàn dìng yǐnliào, mǎn shí bēi jiù kěyǐ tì kèrén sòng guòqù.
text.simplified: 在那家店订饮料，满十杯就可以替客人送过去。

text.traditional: 在這家商店，買東西滿兩千塊（錢），就送一盒巧克力。
text.english: At this store, if you spend two thousand dollars, they will give you a box of chocolates.
text.pinyin: Zài zhè jiā shāngdiàn, mǎi dōngxi mǎn liǎngqiān kuài (qián), jiù sòng yì hé qiǎokèlì.
text.simplified: 在这家商店，买东西满两千块（钱），就送一盒巧克力。

text.traditional: 在台灣，便利商店不可以把酒賣給沒滿十八歲的人。
text.english: In Taiwan, convenience stores may not sell alcohol to anyone under eighteen.
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, biànlì shāngdiàn bù kěyǐ bǎ jiǔ mài gěi méi mǎn shíbā suì de rén.
text.simplified: 在台湾，便利商店不可以把酒卖给没满十八岁的人。

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “滿” is followed by a number. This pattern means reaching a certain amount or number.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “滿” is followed by a number. This pattern means reaching a certain amount or number.

segments.traditional: 在你的國家，幾歲可以開車？
segments.simplified: 在你的国家，几岁可以开车？

repairs.note: Age is counted in 歲: 十八歲.
Reaching an age is 滿 + the number + 歲. 多 cannot go before the number here.
第 makes an order (第十八, "the eighteenth"). Reaching an age is 滿 + the number + 歲.

items.fallbackRepair: 滿 comes first, then the number, then 歲: 滿十八歲.

result.traditional: 滿十八歲就可以開車。
result.simplified: 满十八岁就可以开车。
result.pinyin: Mǎn shíbā suì jiù kěyǐ kāichē.
result.english: Once you turn eighteen, you can drive.

segments.traditional: 老闆，這些名產我多買幾包，可以算便宜一點兒嗎？
segments.simplified: 老板，这些名产我多买几包，可以算便宜一点儿吗？

repairs.note: A is buying packs of local specialties (幾包), so the amount is counted in 包.
滿 is followed by a number: 滿十包.

items.fallbackRepair: The verb, then 滿, then the amount: 買滿十包.

result.traditional: 買滿十包，就算你便宜一點兒。
result.simplified: 买满十包，就算你便宜一点儿。
result.pinyin: Mǎi mǎn shí bāo, jiù suàn nǐ piányí yìdiǎnr.
result.english: Buy a full ten packs and I'll give you a better price.

repairs.note: 多久 asks how long. A length of time is counted in 年, not 歲.
The sentence ends in 了, so the twenty years are complete: 已經滿二十年了.

items.fallbackRepair: 已經 first, then 滿, then the length of time: 已經滿二十年了.

result.traditional: 他們結婚已經滿二十年了。
result.simplified: 他们结婚已经满二十年了。
result.pinyin: Tāmen jiéhūn yǐjīng mǎn èrshí nián le.
result.english: They have already been married a full twenty years.

summary: 滿 before a number and measure word means that amount is reached.
The next part says what applies once it is reached: 滿十杯就可以替客人送過去.
沒滿十八歲 means not yet eighteen.

grammarPages.lessonTitle: 請給我貼紙，我要換史努比！
grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Give Me the Stickers, please. I Want to Exchange Them for Snoopy!
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Emphasize an unexpected example with 連, including emphatic negative forms.
grammarPages.explanation: The pattern “連……都/也……” is used to emphasize a situation that is more special, abnormal, exaggerated, or with higher degree.
grammarPages.pattern: 連 + Focus + 都/也 + statement；連 + 一 + M (+ N) + 都/也 + Neg + V

text.traditional: 我最近很忙，連睡覺的時間都沒有。
text.english: I have been very busy lately; I do not even have time to sleep.
text.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn hěn máng, lián shuìjiào de shíjiān dōu méiyǒu.
text.simplified: 我最近很忙，连睡觉的时间都没有。

text.traditional: 他做的東西真不好吃，連他家的狗都不吃。
text.english: The food he makes is really bad; even his dog will not eat it.
text.pinyin: Tā zuò de dōngxi zhēn bù hǎochī, lián tā jiā de gǒu dōu bù chī.
text.simplified: 他做的东西真不好吃，连他家的狗都不吃。

text.traditional: 那家民宿很便宜，不但有免費的網路，連早餐、午餐也可以吃到飽。
text.english: That B&B is inexpensive. Not only does it have free internet; even breakfast and lunch are all-you-can-eat.
text.pinyin: Nà jiā mínsù hěn piányí, búdàn yǒu miǎnfèi de wǎnglù, lián zǎocān, wǔcān yě kěyǐ chīdàobǎo.
text.simplified: 那家民宿很便宜，不但有免费的网路，连早餐、午餐也可以吃到饱。

text.traditional: 這個孩子真討厭念書，連媽媽打他，他都不怕。
text.english: This child really hates studying; even when his mother hits him, he is not afraid.
text.pinyin: Zhè ge háizi zhēn tǎoyàn niànshū, lián māma dǎ tā, tā dōu bú pà.
text.simplified: 这个孩子真讨厌念书，连妈妈打他，他都不怕。

text.traditional: 他沒學過中文，連一句中文都不會說。
text.english: He has never studied Chinese; he cannot even say one sentence in Chinese.
text.pinyin: Tā méi xué guò Zhōngwén, lián yíjù Zhōngwén dōu bú huì shuō.
text.simplified: 他没学过中文，连一句中文都不会说。

text.traditional: 他的錢都花光了，連一顆糖也買不起。
text.english: He spent all his money and cannot even afford one piece of candy.
text.pinyin: Tā de qián dōu huāguāng le, lián yì kē táng yě mǎi bù qǐ.
text.simplified: 他的钱都花光了，连一颗糖也买不起。

text.traditional: 張先生剛來台灣的時候，連一個朋友都沒有。
text.english: When Mr. Zhang first came to Taiwan, he did not even have one friend.
text.pinyin: Zhāng xiānshēng gāng lái Táiwān de shíhòu, lián yíge péngyǒu dōu méiyǒu.
text.simplified: 张先生刚来台湾的时候，连一个朋友都没有。

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The pattern “連……都/也……” is used to emphasize a situation that is more special, abnormal, exaggerated, or with higher degree.

subsections.title: Even…
subsections.explanation: 「連」引出較特別、出乎意料或程度較高的例子；「都／也」放在該例子後，指出連這種情況也成立。

subsections.title: Not even one…
subsections.titleTraditional: 連 + 一 + M (+N) + 都／也 + Neg + V
subsections.explanation: 用「連＋一＋量詞（＋名詞）＋都／也＋不／沒＋動詞」強調連一個也不。
subsections.pattern: 連 + 一 + Measure word (+ Noun) + 都／也 + Negation + Verb

grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The pattern “連……都/也……” is used to emphasize a situation that is more special, abnormal, exaggerated, or with higher degree.

repairs.note: The character is very hard, so the surprise is that even the teacher cannot write it.
After 連 and the surprising one comes 都 (or 也), not 還.
After 連 and the surprising one comes 都 (or 也), not 就.

items.fallbackRepair: 連 before the surprising one, then 都, then what is true of them: 連老師都不會寫.

result.traditional: 這個字很難寫，連老師都不會寫。
result.simplified: 这个字很难写，连老师都不会写。
result.pinyin: Zhège zì hěn nán xiě, lián lǎoshī dōu bú huì xiě.
result.english: This character is very hard to write; even the teacher can't write it.

repairs.note: Here 才 would say it happens late. The surprise pattern is 連…都….
After 連 and the surprising thing comes 都 (or 也), not 就.

items.fallbackRepair: 連 before the surprising thing, then 都 before the verb: 連自己的名字都忘了.

result.traditional: 他喝了太多酒，連自己的名字都忘了。
result.simplified: 他喝了太多酒，连自己的名字都忘了。
result.pinyin: Tā hē le tài duō jiǔ, lián zìjǐ de míngzi dōu wàng le.
result.english: He drank too much; he even forgot his own name.

repairs.note: The sentence says soy milk in Taiwan is delicious, so even foreigners like it.
After 連 and the surprising one comes 都 (or 也), not 就.

items.fallbackRepair: 連 before the surprising one, then 都, then what is true of them: 連外國人都喜歡喝.

result.traditional: 台灣的豆漿很好喝，連外國人都喜歡喝。
result.simplified: 台湾的豆浆很好喝，连外国人都喜欢喝。
result.pinyin: Táiwān de dòujiāng hěn hǎohē, lián wàiguórén dōu xǐhuān hē.
result.english: Soy milk in Taiwan is delicious; even foreigners like to drink it.

repairs.note: He hates spending money, so the surprise is what he goes without: 不吃.
Here 才 would say it happens late. The surprise pattern is 連…都….

items.fallbackRepair: 連 before the surprising thing, then 都, then the verb: 連早餐都不吃.

result.traditional: 金先生不愛花錢，連早餐都不吃。
result.simplified: 金先生不爱花钱，连早餐都不吃。
result.pinyin: Jīn xiānshēng bú ài huā qián, lián zǎocān dōu bù chī.
result.english: Mr. Jin doesn't like spending money; he doesn't even eat breakfast.

repairs.note: 張 counts flat things (一張桌子). A seat takes 個.

items.fallbackRepair: 連 first, then 一 and the measure word, and 都 before 沒有: 連一個位子都沒有.

result.traditional: 那家餐廳已經客滿了，連一個位子都沒有。
result.simplified: 那家餐厅已经客满了，连一个位子都没有。
result.pinyin: Nà jiā cāntīng yǐjīng kèmǎn le, lián yí ge wèizi dōu méiyǒu.
result.english: That restaurant is already full; there isn't even one seat.

segments.traditional: 住在這個社區真不方便，附近
segments.simplified: 住在这个社区真不方便，附近

repairs.note: 位 counts people politely (一位老師). Shops take 家.
"Not even one" always starts from 一: 連一家商店也沒有.

items.fallbackRepair: 連 first, then 一 and the measure word, and 也 before 沒有: 連一家商店也沒有.

result.traditional: 住在這個社區真不方便，附近連一家商店也沒有。
result.simplified: 住在这个社区真不方便，附近连一家商店也没有。
result.pinyin: Zhù zài zhège shèqū zhēn bù fāngbiàn, fùjìn lián yì jiā shāngdiàn yě méiyǒu.
result.english: Living in this neighborhood is really inconvenient; there isn't even one shop nearby.

repairs.note: No one has to work on Sunday, and this pattern is a strong "not even one": 沒有.
No one has to work on Sunday. "Not even one" is 連一個人.

items.fallbackRepair: 連 first, then 一個人, then 都, then 沒有.

result.traditional: 星期天不用上班，公司連一個人都沒有。
result.simplified: 星期天不用上班，公司连一个人都没有。
result.pinyin: Xīngqítiān búyòng shàngbān, gōngsī lián yí ge rén dōu méiyǒu.
result.english: Nobody has to work on Sunday; there isn't even one person at the company.

summary: 連 brings up the most surprising or extreme example. 都 or 也 says it is true even for that.
Put 連 and the example before 都 or 也: 連睡覺的時間都沒有.
For not even one, put 一 and a measure word after 連, then 都 or 也 and 不 or 沒.
都 here doesn't mean all of them.

grammarPages.lessonTitle: 請給我貼紙，我要換史努比！
grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Give Me the Stickers, please. I Want to Exchange Them for Snoopy!
grammarPages.titleEnglish: A Noun Like This or That
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe a noun by giving an example with similar features.
grammarPages.explanation: The pattern “像……這樣/那樣……的+N” shows the features of the example coming after “像”.
grammarPages.pattern: 像 + Example + 這樣/那樣 + 的 + Noun

text.traditional: 我想住在像藍小姐家那樣安全的社區。
text.english: I want to live in a community as safe as Ms. Lan’s home.
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zhù zài xiàng Lán xiǎojiě jiā nàyàng ānquán de shèqū.
text.simplified: 我想住在像蓝小姐家那样安全的社区。

text.traditional: 很多外國遊客喜歡去像夜市那樣熱鬧的地方玩。
text.english: Many foreign tourists like going to lively places such as night markets.
text.pinyin: Hěn duō wàiguó yóukè xǐhuān qù xiàng yèshì nàyàng rènao de dìfāng wán.
text.simplified: 很多外国游客喜欢去像夜市那样热闹的地方玩。

text.traditional: 像洗碗筷這樣的家事，父母可以讓小孩自己做。
text.english: Parents can let children do household chores on their own, such as washing dishes and chopsticks.
text.pinyin: Xiàng xǐ wǎnkuài zhèyàng de jiāshì, fùmǔ kěyǐ ràng xiǎohái zìjǐ zuò.
text.simplified: 像洗碗筷这样的家事，父母可以让小孩自己做。

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: The pattern “像……這樣/那樣……的+N” shows the features of the example coming after “像”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: The pattern “像……這樣/那樣……的+N” shows the features of the example coming after “像”.

repairs.note: 這麼 goes before a quality (這麼好吃). After the example comes 這樣 or 那樣, then 的 and the noun.
The speaker likes to eat them (喜歡吃), so the noun is a kind of food: 小吃.

items.fallbackRepair: 像 + the example + 那樣 + 的 + the noun: 像雞排那樣的小吃.

result.traditional: 在夜市，像雞排那樣的小吃，我都喜歡吃。
result.simplified: 在夜市，像鸡排那样的小吃，我都喜欢吃。
result.pinyin: Zài yèshì, xiàng jīpái nàyàng de xiǎochī, wǒ dōu xǐhuān chī.
result.english: At the night market, I like to eat all the snacks like fried chicken cutlet.

segments.traditional: 你得滿十八歲，才可以做
segments.simplified: 你得满十八岁，才可以做

repairs.note: Anyone may drink water. Something you must be eighteen for is 喝酒.
這麼 goes before a quality (這麼貴). After the example comes 這樣, then 的 and the noun.
跟 means "with" or "and". Giving an example of a kind of thing starts with 像.

items.fallbackRepair: 像 + the example + 這樣 + 的 + the noun: 像喝酒這樣的事.

result.traditional: 你得滿十八歲，才可以做像喝酒這樣的事。
result.simplified: 你得满十八岁，才可以做像喝酒这样的事。
result.pinyin: Nǐ děi mǎn shíbā suì, cái kěyǐ zuò xiàng hē jiǔ zhèyàng de shì.
result.english: You have to be at least eighteen before you can do things like drinking alcohol.

segments.traditional: 週末的時候，莫以凡常去像
segments.simplified: 周末的时候，莫以凡常去像

repairs.note: He goes there to visit (去…參觀), so the noun is a place: 地方.
那麼 goes before a quality (那麼大). After the example comes 那樣, then 的 and the noun.

items.fallbackRepair: 像 + the example + 那樣 + 的 + the noun: 像博物館那樣的地方.

result.traditional: 週末的時候，莫以凡常去像博物館那樣的地方參觀。
result.simplified: 周末的时候，莫以凡常去像博物馆那样的地方参观。
result.pinyin: Zhōumò de shíhòu, Mò Yǐfán cháng qù xiàng bówùguǎn nàyàng de dìfāng cānguān.
result.english: On weekends, Mo Yifan often goes to visit places like museums.

summary: 像 brings up an example, and 這樣 or 那樣 points back to what the example is like.
Add 的 and a noun to name the kind of person, thing, or place that has those features.
Put the example before the kind: 像洗碗筷這樣的家事.

grammarPages.lessonTitle: 請給我貼紙，我要換史努比！
grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Give Me the Stickers, please. I Want to Exchange Them for Snoopy!
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Explain that an unwanted situation leaves only one practical choice.
grammarPages.explanation: “只好” is used in the situation where the subject has no alternative but to do something.
grammarPages.pattern: Reason / obstacle，Subject + 只好 + Remaining action

text.traditional: 因為訂不到去花蓮的火車票，我們只好坐飛機去。
text.english: Because we could not get a train ticket to Hualien, we had no choice but to fly there.
text.pinyin: Yīnwèi dìng bú dào qù Huālián de huǒchēpiào, wǒmen zhǐhǎo zuò fēijī qù.
text.simplified: 因为订不到去花莲的火车票，我们只好坐飞机去。

text.traditional: 妹妹想跟同學去看電影，可是明天有考試，只好在家看書。
text.english: My younger sister wants to go to a movie with her classmates, but she has an exam tomorrow, so she has no choice but to stay home and study.
text.pinyin: Mèimei xiǎng gēn tóngxué qù kàn diànyǐng, kěshì míngtiān yǒu kǎoshì, zhǐhǎo zài jiā kàn shū.
text.simplified: 妹妹想跟同学去看电影，可是明天有考试，只好在家看书。

text.traditional: 這個月我買了太多衣服，現在錢包裡只剩下三百塊錢，只好每天吃麵包了。
text.english: I bought too many clothes this month. I have only three hundred dollars left in my wallet, so I have no choice but to eat bread every day.
text.pinyin: Zhè ge yuè wǒ mǎi le tài duō yīfu, xiànzài qiánbāo lǐ zhǐ shèngxià sānbǎi kuài qián, zhǐhǎo měitiān chī miànbāo le.
text.simplified: 这个月我买了太多衣服，现在钱包里只剩下三百块钱，只好每天吃面包了。

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “只好” is used in the situation where the subject has no alternative but to do something.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “只好” is used in the situation where the subject has no alternative but to do something.

practice.title: What do you say if these things happen?

segments.traditional: 你本來要去公園野餐，可是出門的時候，開始下大雨了。
segments.simplified: 你本来要去公园野餐，可是出门的时候，开始下大雨了。

repairs.note: 只要 means "only want" or "as long as". Having no other choice is 只好.
It is raining hard, so the park is out. What is left is eating at home.
It is raining hard, so the picnic is off. What is left is eating at home.

items.fallbackRepair: 只好 first, then the only thing left to do: 只好在家吃飯.

result.traditional: 下雨了，我只好在家吃飯。
result.simplified: 下雨了，我只好在家吃饭。
result.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, wǒ zhǐhǎo zài jiā chīfàn.
result.english: It's raining, so I have no choice but to eat at home.

segments.traditional: 你們去餐廳吃飯，可是到的時候才發現已經沒有位子了。
segments.simplified: 你们去餐厅吃饭，可是到的时候才发现已经没有位子了。

segments.traditional: 這家餐廳已經沒有位子了，我們
segments.simplified: 这家餐厅已经没有位子了，我们

repairs.note: 只是 means "only" or "just". Having no other choice is 只好.
There are no seats left here, so eating here is not possible.
There are no seats left, so there is nowhere to sit down.

items.fallbackRepair: 只好 first, then the only thing left to do: 只好去別的餐廳.

result.traditional: 這家餐廳已經沒有位子了，我們只好去別的餐廳。
result.simplified: 这家餐厅已经没有位子了，我们只好去别的餐厅。
result.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng yǐjīng méiyǒu wèizi le, wǒmen zhǐhǎo qù biéde cāntīng.
result.english: This restaurant has no seats left, so we have no choice but to go to another restaurant.

segments.traditional: 你要出門的時候，發現腳踏車壞了。
segments.simplified: 你要出门的时候，发现脚踏车坏了。

segments.traditional: 我發現腳踏車不能騎了，
segments.simplified: 我发现脚踏车不能骑了，

repairs.note: 只要 means "only want" or "as long as". Having no other choice is 只好.
The bicycle cannot be ridden, so what is left is walking.
The bicycle cannot be ridden at all, so what is left is walking.

items.fallbackRepair: 只好 first, then the only thing left to do: 只好走路去.

result.traditional: 我發現腳踏車不能騎了，只好走路去。
result.simplified: 我发现脚踏车不能骑了，只好走路去。
result.pinyin: Wǒ fāxiàn jiǎotàchē bù néng qí le, zhǐhǎo zǒulù qù.
result.english: I found that my bicycle can't be ridden, so I have no choice but to walk.

summary: 只好 says you have no other choice, so you do the only thing left.
Say the reason or problem first. Put the action after 只好.
只好 shows a choice forced by limits. 可以 only shows ability or permission.

grammarPages.lessonTitle: 請給我貼紙，我要換史努比！
grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Give Me the Stickers, please. I Want to Exchange Them for Snoopy!
grammarPages.learnerPromise: State the purpose that motivates an action.
grammarPages.explanation: “為了” is followed by the purpose of an action or a behavior.
grammarPages.pattern: 為了 + Purpose，+ Action

text.traditional: 為了明天的約會，李小姐今天晚上要好好地保養。
text.english: To get ready for her date tomorrow, Ms. Li is going to take good care of her skin tonight.
text.pinyin: Wèile míngtiān de yuēhuì, Lǐ xiǎojiě jīntiān wǎnshàng yào hǎohǎo de bǎoyǎng.
text.simplified: 为了明天的约会，李小姐今天晚上要好好地保养。

text.traditional: 為了把英文學好，我決定下個學期去英國留學。
text.english: In order to learn English well, I decided to study in the United Kingdom next semester.
text.pinyin: Wèile bǎ Yīngwén xuéhǎo, wǒ juédìng xià ge xuéqí qù Yīngguó liúxué.
text.simplified: 为了把英文学好，我决定下个学期去英国留学。

text.traditional: 為了租到比較便宜的公寓，阮先生已經找了好幾個地方了。
text.english: To rent a less expensive apartment, Mr. Ruan has already looked at several places.
text.pinyin: Wèile zū dào bǐjiào piányí de gōngyù, Ruǎn xiānshēng yǐjīng zhǎo le hǎojǐ ge dìfāng le.
text.simplified: 为了租到比较便宜的公寓，阮先生已经找了好几个地方了。

grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “為了” is followed by the purpose of an action or a behavior.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “為了” is followed by the purpose of an action or a behavior.

segments.traditional: 卡拉 OK 比賽，我要好好地練習。
segments.simplified: 卡拉 OK 比赛，我要好好地练习。

repairs.note: 為什麼 asks "why". The goal of an action starts with 為了.
所以 starts the result, in the second half. The goal comes first, after 為了.
You practice hard to take part in a contest, not to watch one: 參加.

items.fallbackRepair: 為了 first, then the goal: 為了參加卡拉 OK 比賽.

result.traditional: 為了參加卡拉 OK 比賽，我要好好地練習。
result.simplified: 为了参加卡拉 OK 比赛，我要好好地练习。
result.pinyin: Wèile cānjiā kǎlā OK bǐsài, wǒ yào hǎohǎo de liànxí.
result.english: In order to take part in the karaoke contest, I am going to practice hard.

segments.traditional: 火車票，我要早一點兒上網訂票。
segments.simplified: 火车票，我要早一点儿上网订票。

repairs.note: You ride a train, not a ticket. The goal is getting the tickets: 訂到.
雖然 needs a turn with 可是 after it. The goal of an action starts with 為了.
所以 starts the result, in the second half. The goal comes first, after 為了.

items.fallbackRepair: 為了 first, then the goal: 為了訂到火車票.

result.traditional: 為了訂到火車票，我要早一點兒上網訂票。
result.simplified: 为了订到火车票，我要早一点儿上网订票。
result.pinyin: Wèile dìngdào huǒchēpiào, wǒ yào zǎo yìdiǎnr shàngwǎng dìngpiào.
result.english: In order to get train tickets, I am going to book online a little earlier.

repairs.note: Roses are a gift to please someone. The goal is to make her happy: 高興.
請 asks someone to do something for you. Making someone feel a certain way is 讓.
給 hands something to someone. Making someone feel a certain way is 讓.

items.fallbackRepair: 為了 first, then 讓 + the person + the feeling: 為了讓女朋友高興.

result.traditional: 為了讓女朋友高興，弟弟買了一束玫瑰花。
result.simplified: 为了让女朋友高兴，弟弟买了一束玫瑰花。
result.pinyin: Wèile ràng nǚpéngyǒu gāoxìng, dìdi mǎi le yí shù méiguīhuā.
result.english: To make his girlfriend happy, my younger brother bought a bunch of roses.

summary: 為了 says the purpose of an action.
After it, use a noun phrase or an action. The main action comes after the purpose.
For a cause, use 因為. 為了 gives the goal, not the reason.

dialogue.title: 請給我貼紙，我要換史努比！
dialogue.setting: 在教室裡 · In the classroom

text.traditional: （美心跟以凡在教室裡）
text.simplified: （美心跟以凡在教室里）
text.pinyin: (Měixīn gēn Yǐfán zài jiàoshì lǐ)
text.english: (Meixin and Yifan are in the classroom.)

text.traditional: 以凡，你貼在豆漿盒子上的那張貼紙，可以給我嗎？
text.simplified: 以凡，你贴在豆浆盒子上的那张贴纸，可以给我吗？
text.pinyin: Yǐfán, nǐ tiē zài dòujiāng hézi shàng de nà zhāng tiēzhǐ, kěyǐ gěi wǒ ma?
text.english: Yifan, can you give me the sticker that you pasted on the soy milk carton?

text.traditional: 妳說的貼紙是便利商店店員給我的這張嗎？
text.simplified: 你说的贴纸是便利商店店员给我的这张吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de tiēzhǐ shì biànlì shāngdiàn diànyuán gěi wǒ de zhè zhāng ma?
text.english: Are you talking about the one that the clerk of the convenience store gave me?

text.traditional: 是啊！我只差一張，就能換一個史努比（Snoopy）娃娃了！
text.simplified: 是啊！我只差一张，就能换一个史努比（Snoopy）娃娃了！
text.pinyin: Shì a! Wǒ zhǐ chà yì zhāng, jiù néng huàn yíge Shǐnǔbǐ (Snoopy) wáwa le!
text.english: Yes! I only need one more to be able to exchange for a Snoopy doll.

text.traditional: 給妳吧！我覺得它很可愛，才把它貼在盒子上，其實我不知道店員為什麼給我貼紙。
text.simplified: 给你吧！我觉得它很可爱，才把它贴在盒子上，其实我不知道店员为什么给我贴纸。
text.pinyin: Gěi nǐ ba! Wǒ juéde tā hěn kě'ài, cái bǎ tā tiē zài hézi shàng, qíshí wǒ bù zhīdào diànyuán wèishénme gěi wǒ tiēzhǐ.
text.english: Here you are! I put it on the soy milk carton only because I think it's cute. Actually, I don't know why the clerk gave me this sticker.

text.traditional: 這是便利商店的活動，買東西只要滿八十元，就會有一張貼紙，四十張貼紙就可以換一個娃娃，而且不用錢。
text.simplified: 这是便利商店的活动，买东西只要满八十元，就会有一张贴纸，四十张贴纸就可以换一个娃娃，而且不用钱。
text.pinyin: Zhè shì biànlì shāngdiàn de huódòng, mǎi dōngxi zhǐyào mǎn bāshí yuán, jiù huì yǒu yì zhāng tiēzhǐ, sìshí zhāng tiēzhǐ jiù kěyǐ huàn yíge wáwa, érqiě búyòng qián.
text.english: It's a sales promotion of convenience stores. As long as the price of the products you buy exceeds $80, you can get one sticker, 40 stickers can be exchanged for a doll for free.

text.traditional: 免費？真的連一塊錢都不用付，就可以得到像史努比那樣的娃娃嗎？
text.simplified: 免费？真的连一块钱都不用付，就可以得到像史努比那样的娃娃吗？
text.pinyin: Miǎnfèi? Zhēnde lián yíkuài qián dōu búyòng fù, jiù kěyǐ dédào xiàng Shǐnǔbǐ nàyàng de wáwa ma?
text.english: For free? You really don't have to pay even one dollar to get a doll like Snoopy?

text.traditional: 當然是真的。下次你去便利商店，看看門口貼的海報就知道了。這次送的娃娃非常可愛，我擔心很快就換完了！
text.simplified: 当然是真的。下次你去便利商店，看看门口贴的海报就知道了。这次送的娃娃非常可爱，我担心很快就换完了！
text.pinyin: Dāngrán shì zhēnde. Xià cì nǐ qù biànlì shāngdiàn, kànkan ménkǒu tiē de hǎibào jiù zhīdào le. Zhè cì sòng de wáwa fēicháng kě'ài, wǒ dānxīn hěn kuài jiù huàn wán le!
text.english: Of course it's true! Next time when you go to a convenience store, just take a look at the poster on the door and you'll know. This time the dolls given are very cute. I am afraid their stocks will run out soon!

text.traditional: 這次？妳的意思是像這樣的活動不只一次嗎？為什麼便利商店要辦這樣的活動呢？
text.simplified: 这次？你的意思是像这样的活动不只一次吗？为什么便利商店要办这样的活动呢？
text.pinyin: Zhè cì? Nǐ de yìsi shì xiàng zhèyàng de huódòng bù zhǐ yí cì ma? Wèishénme biànlì shāngdiàn yào bàn zhèyàng de huódòng ne?
text.english: This time? You mean this kind of sales promotion event can take place more than once? Why do convenience stores organize such sales promotion event?

text.traditional: 因為很多人容易被可愛的小東西吸引，所以商人就利用這種心理，做了像尺、牙刷、杯子、盤子這樣的小禮物，上面都有可愛的卡通人物，讓大家常常想去買東西。
text.simplified: 因为很多人容易被可爱的小东西吸引，所以商人就利用这种心理，做了像尺、牙刷、杯子、盘子这样的小礼物，上面都有可爱的卡通人物，让大家常常想去买东西。
text.pinyin: Yīnwèi hěn duō rén róngyì bèi kě'ài de xiǎo dōngxi xīyǐn, suǒyǐ shāngrén jiù lìyòng zhè zhǒng xīnlǐ, zuò le xiàng chǐ, yáshuā, bēizi, pánzi zhèyàng de xiǎo lǐwù, shàngmiàn dōu yǒu kě'ài de kǎtōng rénwù, ràng dàjiā chángcháng xiǎng qù mǎi dōngxi.
text.english: Many people are easily attracted by little, cute things, so businessmen take advantage of this psychological fact. They make small gifts such as rulers, toothbrushes, mugs, plates, and so on. They are all printed with cute cartoon characters, making everyone want to buy things more often.

text.traditional: 那麼，有些人想要快點兒得到喜愛的小禮物，只好多花錢買一些不需要的東西吧？
text.simplified: 那么，有些人想要快点儿得到喜爱的小礼物，只好多花钱买一些不需要的东西吧？
text.pinyin: Nàme, yǒuxiē rén xiǎngyào kuài diǎnr dédào xǐ'ài de xiǎo lǐwù, zhǐhǎo duō huāqián mǎi yìxiē bù xūyào de dōngxi ba?
text.english: In that case, some people want to get the gifts they love faster, so they spend more money on unnecessary things, right?

text.traditional: 你說對了！一開始是商人為了吸引顧客，才想出這個辦法的。沒想到小禮物太有吸引力了，後來就變成台灣便利商店的文化了。
text.simplified: 你说对了！一开始是商人为了吸引顾客，才想出这个办法的。没想到小礼物太有吸引力了，后来就变成台湾便利商店的文化了。
text.pinyin: Nǐ shuō duìle! Yìkāishǐ shì shāngrén wèile xīyǐn gùkè, cái xiǎng chū zhège bànfǎ de. Méixiǎngdào xiǎo lǐwù tài yǒu xīyǐnlì le, hòulái jiù biànchéng Táiwān biànlì shāngdiàn de wénhuà le.
text.english: You are right! At first, the businessmen came up with this idea in order to attract customers. They didn't expect those little gifts to be that attractive. Later, they have become a part of the culture of Taiwanese convenience stores.

text.traditional: 台灣所有便利商店都有這樣的活動嗎？
text.simplified: 台湾所有便利商店都有这样的活动吗？
text.pinyin: Táiwān suǒyǒu biànlì shāngdiàn dōu yǒu zhèyàng de huódòng ma?
text.english: Do all convenience stores in Taiwan have this kind of sales promotion event?

text.traditional: 差不多都有。這類活動對生意的影響很大，只要有「拿貼紙、送禮物」的活動，就會增加不少顧客。
text.simplified: 差不多都有。这类活动对生意的影响很大，只要有「拿贴纸、送礼物」的活动，就会增加不少顾客。
text.pinyin: Chàbùduō dōu yǒu. Zhè lèi huódòng duì shēngyì de yǐngxiǎng hěn dà, zhǐyào yǒu “ná tiēzhǐ, sòng lǐwù” de huódòng, jiù huì zēngjiā bùshǎo gùkè.
